body.text: Ruyyaka [Rājānaka]: Vyaktivivekavyākhyā, 2nd vimarśa
body.translated_text: <s>Ruyyaka</s> [<s>Rājānaka</s>]: <s>Vyaktivivekavyākhyā</s>, 2nd <s>vimarśa</s> (investigation)

children.text: [Page 15]
children.translated_text: [Page 15]

children.text: atha dvitīyo vimarśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the second <s>vimarśa</s> (investigation).

body.text: evaṃ tāvat prathame vimarśe dhvanilakṣaṇaṃ dūṣayitvā dhvaniśāstragataṃ granthāntaraṃ dūṣayituṃ sāmānyena tāvat kāvyagatam anaucityollāsarūpaṃ dūṣaṇaprapañcam upapādayitum āha -

children.text: iha khalv ityādinā / uktam iti sahṛdayaiḥ / antaraṅgam iti sākṣād rasaviṣayatvāt / ādyair iti dhvanikāraprabhṛtibhiḥ / tad uktam -
children.translated_text: By the words 'iha khalu' etc. / 'It is said' — by connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). / 'Internal' (<s>antaraṅga</s>) — because it directly pertains to <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). / 'By the earlier ones' — by the <s>Dhvanikāra</s> (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>) and others. / It is said —

body.translated_text: Having thus refuted the definition of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) in the first <s>vimarśa</s>, in order to refute another section of the <s>dhvani</s> treatise, he begins by establishing in a general manner the elaboration of defects (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) in the form of the display of impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>) found in poetry — he says:

children.text: anaucityād ṛte nānyad rasabhaṅgasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: There is no other cause of the destruction of <s>rasa</s> than impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>).

children.text: prasiddhaucityabandhas tu rasasyopaniṣat parā //
children.translated_text: The bond of well-known propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) is the supreme <s>upaniṣad</s> (secret essence) of <s>rasa</s>.

body.text: ityādinā / bahiraṅgam iti vācyamukhena rase paryavasānād vidheyaḥ prādhānyena pratipipādayiṣito yo 'rthas tasya avimarśo 'nanusaṃdhānam upasarjanīkaraṇāt / prakramaḥ kasya cid vastuno nirvāhāyārambhas tasya bhedo madhye 'nyathīkaraṇam anyathānirvāhaś ca / kramasya paripāṭyā bheda ullaṅghanaṃ vyutkrama iti yāvat / paunaruktyaṃ punaḥpratipādanam / vācyasya vaktavyasya avacanam anuktiḥ / etā avāntarabhedabhinnāḥ pañca dūṣanajātayaḥ /
body.translated_text: By the words 'etc.' / 'External' (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) — because it culminates in <s>rasa</s> through the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>); the 'non-consideration of the predicate' (<s>vidheyāvimarśa</s>) — the non-contemplation, the subordination, of the meaning that is principally intended to be conveyed. / '<s>Prakrama</s>' (sequence) — the commencement for the continuation of some subject; its 'break' (<s>bheda</s>) — making it otherwise in the middle, carrying it out differently. / 'Break in order' (<s>kramabheda</s>) — a transgression of the sequence, that is, an inversion (<s>vyutkrama</s>). / 'Repetition' (<s>paunaruktya</s>) — restating [the same thing]. / 'Non-statement' (<s>avacana</s>) — of what should be said (<s>vācya</s>), its non-utterance. / These, subdivided into various kinds, are the five classes of defects (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: yad etad ihagranthakṛtā vicārasaraṇim āśritya vidheyāvimarśādidoṣapañcakam udbhāvitaṃ, na tatrādyatanapuruṣamātrabuddhipraṇayanāsūyayānādaraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / pūrvair evaṃvidhadoṣodbhāvanarūpasya vicārasya praṇītatvāt / tathā hi / "dāsyāḥ putra" ityādāv ākrośe ṣaṣṭhyā alukaṃ pratipādayatā sūtrakṛtā (PS_6,3.21) vidheyāvimarśaḥ sūcita eva / tathā "svāmīśvarādhipatidāyādety" (PS_2,3.39) atra sūtre na hi bhavati "gavāṃ svāmī aśveṣu ca" iti vadatā bhāṣyakṛtā spaṣṭam eva prakramabhedaḥ pratipāditaḥ / tathā "kṛñcānuprayujyate liṭi" (PS_3,1.40) iy atrānuprayogasyānuśabdaparyālocanayā vyavahitapūrvaprayogaṃ "taṃ pātayāṃ prathamam āsa" ityādau niṣedhatā cādīnāṃ ca na hi bhavati "ca vṛkṣaḥ" ityādinā prayoganiyamakhyāpanena dyotakatvaṃ kathayatā asthānaprayogalakṣaṇaḥ kramabhedaḥ kaṭākṣita eva / tathā "karmadhārayamatvarthīyābhyāṃ bahuvrīhir laghutvāt syād" iti vṛttilāghavaṃ cintayatā kātyāyanena paunaruktyam api prakāśitam eva / tathā "īṣad asamāptau" (PS_5,3.67) ity atra pratijñānasamadhigamyaṃ sūtrakāroktaṃ rūpakalakṣaṇam arthaṃ dūṣayatā "prakṛtyarthasadṛśe kalpavādividhānam" iti pratijñānasamadhigamyārthabhūtām upamāṃ vyavasthāpayatopamāśrayeṇa

children.text: [Page 16]
children.translated_text: [Page 16]

children.text: vācyāvacanam api dyotitam eva / etena rūpakāśrayeṇāvācyavacanam api dyotitam eva / tad evaṃ mahāviduṣāṃ mārgam anusṛtya sahṛdayaśikṣādarāya vicāraya(ndaraṃ?)to 'sya mahāmater na kaś cit paryanuyogaleśasyāpy avasara ity alam atiprasaṅgena /
children.translated_text: the non-statement of what should be said (<s>vācyāvacana</s>) has also been indicated. By this, through the use of metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>), the non-statement of what should be said has also been indicated. Thus, following the path of the great scholars, as this great intellect [the author] examines [the matter] out of eagerness for the training of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), there is not even a trace of occasion for objection. Enough of digression.

body.translated_text: That this five-fold set of defects — non-consideration of the predicate (<s>vidheyāvimarśa</s>) etc. — has been identified by the author of this work following the path of critical analysis, one should not dismiss with contempt out of jealousy that it was produced merely by the intelligence of a contemporary. For such critical analysis in the form of identifying defects was composed by earlier [authorities] too. Thus: In [the rule about] the abusive [use, as in] '<s>dāsyāḥ putra</s>' ('son of a slave-woman'), by establishing the non-elision of the sixth case-ending (<s>ṣaṣṭhī aluk</s>), the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (<s>Pāṇini</s>) (PS 6.3.21) has indicated [the defect of] non-consideration of the predicate. Likewise in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>svāmīśvarādhipatidāyādety</s>...' (PS 2.3.39), by saying 'one cannot say <s>gavāṃ svāmī aśveṣu ca</s> (lord of cows and also among horses),' the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Patañjali</s>) has clearly demonstrated a break in sequence (<s>prakramabheda</s>). Likewise in '<s>kṛñ cānuprayujyate liṭi</s>' (PS 3.1.40), by prohibiting the secondary use in the periphrastic perfect with intervening prior use as in '<s>taṃ pātayāṃ prathamam āsa</s>,' and by stating the convention of usage for <s>ca</s> and the like with '<s>na hi bhavati ca vṛkṣaḥ</s>' etc., thereby declaring their indicatory function (<s>dyotakatva</s>), he has obliquely referred to the defect of misplacement (<s>asthānaprayoga</s>), which is a form of order-breaking. Likewise <s>Kātyāyana</s>, by considering conciseness of expression (<s>vṛttilāghava</s>) in '<s>karmadhārayam atvarthīyābhyāṃ bahuvrīhir laghutvāt syāt</s>,' has made manifest repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>) as well. Likewise in '<s>īṣad asamāptau</s>' (PS 5.3.67), by criticizing the meaning having the characteristic of metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) stated by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s>, which is to be understood only from the proposition, and by establishing the simile (<s>upamā</s>) which is the meaning to be understood from the proposition, through the use of simile —

body.text: etasya ceti sāmānyenānaucityasya / doṣā iti kāvyasya vikṛtatvāpādanād dūṣaṇād doṣā iti / mugdha iti pṛṣṭasyāprativikṛtatve trīṇi kāraṇāni / prativacanāpratibhānalakṣaṇaṃ maugdhyaṃ pratibhāne 'py aprauḍharūpatvam asahyatvam / prauḍhatve 'pi guṇāsahiṣṇutvalakṣaṇaṃ mātsaryam / tāny atra saṃdihyamānatayā krameṇoktāni / yaḥ kilety atraiva cchedaḥ / chātrābhyarthanayeti praṣṭṛtvasyāṅgīkṛtam iti prativaktṛtvasya ca nirdeśaḥ / paurobhāgyaṃ doṣaikagrāhitvam / nanu yadi parakīye kāvye parihārāya doṣāṇāṃ vicāraḥ kriyate, tat kiṃ nijakāvye na teṣāṃ parihāraḥ / tathā ca "bhajate mātsaryamaunaṃ nu kim" ity ato 'nantaram "iti pṛṣṭa" ity evaṃ krameṇetiśabdo nirdeśyaḥ kramāntareṇa nirdeśāt kramabhedo na yujyate / evam anyat (śokāpadānādau?) jñeyam / tadartham āha - svakṛtiṣv iti kṛtiḥ kāvyam /
body.translated_text: 'Of this' — of impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>) in general. / 'Defects' (<s>doṣa</s>) — defects because they make the poem defective (<s>vikṛta</s>) by being faults. / 'Naive' (<s>mugdha</s>) — there are three reasons for the non-reciprocal refutation of the respondent: foolishness characterized by inability to conceive a response; even when conceiving, lack of mature form, that is, incompetence; even when mature, jealousy (<s>mātsarya</s>) characterized by intolerance of [the other's] merits. These are stated in sequence here as matters of doubt. / 'Yaḥ kila' — the break is right here. / 'By the request of students' — thus the role of questioner is accepted, and the role of respondent is indicated. / '<s>Paurobhāgya</s>' — the tendency to grasp only defects. / Now, if the examination of defects is made to remedy faults in others' poetry, why is there no remedy for them in one's own poetry? Thus, after 'does it adopt the silence of jealousy?' the word 'iti' should be indicated with 'iti pṛṣṭaḥ' in this sequence; since it is indicated in a different sequence, a break in order is not appropriate. The same should be understood in other [cases]. For this purpose he says: '<s>svakṛtiṣu</s>' — '<s>kṛti</s>' means poetry.

body.text: saṃrambha iti kutsitāḥ kariṇaḥ karikīṭāḥ "kutsitāni kutsanaiḥ" (PS_2,1.53) iti samāsaḥ / karikīṭānām āśādviradaiḥ pratinirdeśaḥ / meghaśakalānāṃ tu kalpāntatoyadaiḥ ya ity atraiva cchedaḥ / ayaṃ śloko vakroktijīvite vitatya vyākhyāta iti tata evāvadhāryaḥ /

children.text:
tāvacchabdo vidheyāvimarśatrayasyaitacchlokagatasyopakramadyotakaḥ / saṃbandhopapatter iti / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - "samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ" (PS_2,1.1) iti vacanāt samāsaḥ sāmarthyanimittakaḥ / sāmarthyaṃ ca saṅgatārthatvaṃ, saṅgatatvaṃ ca saṃbandhaḥ / sa cātra viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ / paryudāsasyaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ nañā abrāhmaṇa iti yathā / na cātra vakṣyamāṇanyāyena paryudāso ghaṭata iti / nanv abrāhmaṇa ityādau nañ kathaṃ viśeṣaṇam / viśeṣaṇaṃ hi viśeṣyasyoparañjakaṃ bhavati / na ca nañśabdo viruddhatvād vidhim uparañjayati / tat katham asya viśeṣaṇatvam / naitat / abrāhmaṇa ityādau brāhmaṇaśabdo brāhmaṇasadṛśe kṣatriyādau vartate / sā cākṣatriyādau brāhmaṇaśabdasya vṛttir nañā dyotyate / tad uktam - "nañ ivayuktam anyasadṛśādhikaraṇe tatha hy artha" iti / tatra ca śabdaśaktisvābhāvyaṃ kāraṇam / yathā caitat tathā nañsūtrabhāṣyād avaseyam /
pradhānatvam iti / yatra vidheḥ prādhānyaṃ pratiṣedhasyāprādhānyaṃ naña uttarapadena saṃbandhaḥ samarthasamāsa ekavākyatvaṃ ca tatra paryudāsaḥ "kiṃ cid varjayitvā kasya cid upadeśo nirāsa" iti nigamanāt / tatra kārikāyāṃ trayaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ dvayaṃ cākṣipyate / jugopeti / atra nañarthaviśiṣṭasyottarapadārthasya vidhir na trastatvādiniṣedhaḥ / tatrāpy atrastatvādeḥ siddhatvāt tadanuvādena gopanādi vidhīyata iti paryudāsatvam / aprādhānyam iti / yatra pratiṣedhasya prādhānyaṃ vidher aprādhānyyaṃ nañaḥ kriyāpadena saṃbandho 'samarthasamāsaḥ vākyabhedaś ca, tatra prasajya prāpayya pratiṣedha iti prasajyapratiṣedhaḥ / atra kārikāyāṃ traye nirdiṣṭe 'nyad dvayam ākṣiptam / na veti / atra dṛptaniśācaraṃ prati niṣedhaḥ pratīyate, na tv adṛptaniśācaravidhir iti prasajyapratiṣedhatā / saṃrambhavatpratiṣedho hy atreti / saṃrabdhavān yaḥ puruṣas tadgatā yeyaṃ saṃrabdhatā saṃrambhaṇakriyā tasyā vakṣyamāṇanyāyena pratiṣedha ity arthaḥ / asaṃradhavadvidhir iti saṃrabdhavatsadṛśasya saṃrambhasadṛśakriyākarttur udāsīnaprāyasya vidhir ity arthaḥ / yad uktaṃ "nañ iva yuktam" ityādi / tatreti saṃrabdahavatpratiṣedhe / na cāsāv iti prati
children.translated_text:
The word '<s>tāvat</s>' indicates the commencement of the three-fold non-consideration of the predicate (<s>vidheyāvimarśa</s>) contained in this verse. / 'Establishment of relation' (<s>saṃbandhopapatti</s>) — The meaning is this: From the statement '<s>samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ</s>' (PS 2.1.1), compound-formation is caused by semantic fitness (<s>sāmarthya</s>). Semantic fitness is coherence of meaning, and coherence is relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>). And here that [relation] is the qualifier-qualified relationship (<s>viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣyabhāva</s>). The negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) in exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) acts as a qualifier, as in '<s>abrāhmaṇa</s>' (non-Brahman). And here, by the principle to be stated, exclusion does not apply. / Now, in '<s>abrāhmaṇa</s>' etc., how is the negative particle a qualifier? A qualifier embellishes the qualified. But the negative particle, being contradictory, does not embellish an injunction. So how can it be a qualifier? / This is not so. In '<s>abrāhmaṇa</s>' etc., the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' applies to what is similar to a Brahman — a <s>Kṣatriya</s> etc. That usage of the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> etc. is indicated by the negative particle. As it is said: '<s>nañ</s>, like <s>iva</s>, is used in what is similar to and co-referential with another,' etc. And the reason for this is the natural power (<s>svābhāvya</s>) of the word. How this is so should be ascertained from the <s>bhāṣya</s> on the <s>nañ-sūtra</s>.
'Predominance' (<s>prādhānya</s>) — Where the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) has predominance and the negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) is non-predominant, [where] there is a relation of the negative particle with the latter member [of the compound], a meaningful compound (<s>samarthasamāsa</s>), and a single-sentence reading (<s>ekavākyatva</s>) — there is <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion by implication): 'excluding something, the teaching of something [else] is a rejection.' In the <s>kārikā</s>, three things are stated and two are implied. / '<s>Jugopa</s>' (he protected) — Here there is an injunction of the latter member's meaning qualified by the negative meaning, not a negation of being frightened etc. And since the non-frightened state etc. is already established, through its restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), protection etc. is enjoined — hence it is <s>paryudāsa</s>. / 'Non-predominance' — Where the negation has predominance and the injunction is non-predominant, [where] the negative particle relates to the verb, [where there is] a non-meaningful compound and sentence-splitting — there is <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (categorical/absolute negation): 'having extended (<s>prasajya</s>), having applied, there is a negation.' In the <s>kārikā</s>, three things are stated and another pair is implied. / '<s>Na va</s>' (or not) — Here a negation is understood with respect to the proud night-ranger (demon), not an injunction of a non-proud night-ranger — hence it is <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>. / 'The negation of one who possesses fury' — The meaning is: the fury-possession (<s>saṃrambhaṇakriyā</s>) belonging to a person who is furious — of that, a negation by the principle to be stated. / 'The injunction of one similar to the non-furious' — The meaning is: an injunction of one similar to the furious, an agent of action similar to fury, one who is mostly indifferent. As said: '<s>nañ</s>, like <s>iva</s>, is used,' etc. / 'There' — in the negation of one who possesses fury. / 'And that one' —

children.text: [Page 17]
children.translated_text: [Page 17]

children.text: ṣedhati / tatsiddhipakṣa iti vivakṣito yaḥ pradhānabhūtaniṣedhalakṣaṇo 'rthasya siddhipakṣa ity arthaḥ / asya vidhyanuvādabhāvasyeti / nañarthasya vidhir uttarapadārthasyānuvāda ity asya / samāse hi nañarthopasarjana uttarapadārthaḥ prādhānyena pratīyate / kāvyārtheti / atra vyavacchedyaṃ prasajyapratiṣedhaṃ pradarśya paricchedyaṃ paryudāsam udāharati /
children.translated_text: he negates. / '<s>Tatsiddhipakṣa</s>' (the side of its establishment) — the intended meaning is: 'the side of establishing the meaning whose predominant characteristic is negation.' / 'Of this state of injunction-and-restatement' (<s>vidhyanuvādabhāva</s>) — 'of this': the injunction of the negative meaning, the restatement of the latter member's meaning. / For in a compound, the latter member's meaning, with the negative meaning subordinate, is predominantly understood. / 'Poetic meaning' (<s>kāvyārtha</s>) — Here, having demonstrated the object of exclusion (<s>vyavacchedya</s>) as categorical negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), he illustrates the object of delimitation (<s>paricchedya</s>) as <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion by implication).

body.translated_text: 'Fury' (<s>saṃrambha</s>) — '<s>karikīṭa</s>' means contemptible elephants (<s>kutsitāḥ kariṇaḥ</s>), the compound being by the rule '<s>kutsitāni kutsanaiḥ</s>' (PS 2.1.53). / The reference to '<s>karikīṭas</s>' is by means of '<s>virada</s>' (elephants). / But for '<s>meghaśakala</s>' (cloud-fragments), [the reference is] by means of '<s>kalpāntatoyada</s>' (end-of-the-world rain-clouds). / The break is at '<s>ya</s>' here. / This verse has been explained at length in the <s>Vakroktijīvita</s>, and should be understood from there.

body.text: nanu prasajyapratiṣedhe nañaḥ kriyānvaye 'saṃrabdahavān ity atra saṃrambhakriyāniṣedho bhaviṣyati / tat ko 'tra doṣa ity āha: kriyākartraṃśabhāg iti / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ: asaṃrabdhavān ity atra dvāv aṃśau kriyāṃśaḥ kārakāṃśaś ca / tatrobhayāṃśabhāgarthaniṣedhe śabdaśaktisvābhāvyād vākye kriyāṃśaniṣedhas tasya prādhānyena vivakṣitasyāparāmarśo (...m anuktād?)vidheyāvimarśaḥ / yathā ca prasajyapratiṣedhe samāso neṣṭas tathoktanayena paryudāse 'py asamāso neṣyata ity āha

children.translated_text: [Section 39]

children.text: - nanu sādhv iti atra "na kurvate"ti karaṇakriyākartṛsadṛśena kriyāṃ praty udāsīnaprāyeṇety arthaḥ / akurvateti vācye na kurvateti kriyāṃśaniṣedhaḥ pratīter vaiparītyakārī / evaṃ nocitam apīty ucitatvamātraniṣedhaḥ pratīter vaiparītyakṛd eva / tacchravaṇaṃ kriyāśravaṇam / tayor iti siddhārthā vṛttiḥ / sādhyārthaṃ vākyam / asūryaṃpaśyādiṣv iti / atrāpi nañaḥ sūryeṇottarapadāthana
children.translated_text: Now, regarding '<s>sādhu</s>' (well) here — in 'na kurvate' (they do not do), the meaning resembles an agent indifferent to action, like an instrument-action-agent. The negation of the action-component in saying 'na kurvate' instead of 'akurvate' causes a reversal in cognition. Similarly, 'na ucitam api' (not proper either) — the mere negation of propriety causes a reversal in cognition. The hearing of 'that' is the hearing of action. 'Of those two' — the <s>vṛtti</s> (gloss) has an established meaning; the sentence has a meaning to be accomplished. 'In <s>asūryaṃpaśyā</s> etc.' — here also the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) has no connection with the meaning of the latter member '<s>sūrya</s>' (sun),

children.text: ⟨corr. into °padārthena⟩
children.translated_text: [Corrected to: 'with the meaning of the latter member']

children.text: nābhisaṃbandhaḥ, api tu taddraṣṭrarthenaiva / tatrāpi kartraṃśaḥ pradhānaṃ na kriyāṃśaḥ karttari khaśo vidhānād iti pūrvavad avaseyam / bhuṅkta iti atra hi vākyasya kriyāprādhānyaṃ pratīyamānabhavatyādikriyāpekṣe nañaḥ samanvaye śrāddhabhojī na bhavatīti vākyārthaḥ / aśrāddhabhojīty atra tu nañā bhoktus samanvaye śrāddhabhoktṛvyatirikto 'pi vighasāśyā+i++ pratīyate / yataś cātrāśrāddhabhojītyādau samāse pratiṣedho neṣṭaḥ, tata eva samarthasamāsas tadviparyayeṇāsamarthasamāsaś ca kārikādvayenoktaḥ / vākyabhedābhedayos tu sāmarthyāt pratītir ity avacanam /
children.translated_text: but only with the meaning 'one who sees that.' There too, the agent-component is primary, not the action-component, because the <s>khaś</s> suffix is prescribed for the agent — this should be understood as before. In '<s>bhuṅkte</s>' (he eats) here, the primacy of action in the sentence — when the negative particle is construed with the perceived action 'being' etc., the sentence-meaning is 'he is not a <s>śrāddha</s>-feeder.' But in '<s>aśrāddhabhojī</s>' (non-<s>śrāddha</s>-feeder), when the negative is construed with the eater, even one different from a <s>śrāddha</s>-feeder, such as a leftovers-eater, is cognized. And because in '<s>aśrāddhabhojī</s>' etc. negation as a compound is not desired, for that very reason the meaningful compound (<s>samarthasamāsa</s>) and, conversely, the non-meaningful compound (<s>asamarthasamāsa</s>) are stated in two verses. But for sentence-division and non-division, the cognition [arises] from capacity — hence [it is] unmentioned.

body.translated_text: Now, in a simple negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), since the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) is connected with the action, in '<s>asaṃrabdhavān</s>' (one who was not agitated), there will be a negation of the agitation-action. What fault is there? He says: 'the share of the action-and-agent component.' The meaning is this: in '<s>asaṃrabdhavān</s>' there are two components — the action-component and the agent-component (<s>kāraka</s>). When there is negation of the meaning shared by both components, by the natural power of words, the negation of the action-component in the sentence [entails] non-consideration of what is principally intended — [that is,] non-examination of the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>). And just as a compound is not desired in simple negation, so also in exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) a non-compound is not desired, according to the stated method — he says:

body.text: evakemaṃ

children.text: ⟨sic⟩
children.translated_text: [sic]

children.text: vidheyāvimarśaṃ vicārya dvitīyam udāharati - yo 'sāv ity atreti tacchabdaṃ praty ākāṅkṣāyāḥ kenāpy anivarttanāt /
children.translated_text: Having examined the non-examination of the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>), he gives the second example — 'yo 'sāv ity atra' (regarding 'he who is that one here') — because the expectation toward the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) is not removed by anything.
[Section 40]

children.text: ekatareti kvacid yacchabdenopakrame tacchabdenopasaṃhāraḥ / kva cit tacchabdenopakrame yacchabdenopasaṃhāraḥ prasajyate / etac ca dvayaṃ śābdopakramopasaṃhārakrameṇodāhariṣyati / tayor apīti / apiśabdo nañarthaṃ samuccinoti / prasajyapratiṣedhe hi nañartho vidheyo niṣedhyo 'rtho 'nuvādyaḥ / paryudāse tu viparyaya ity uktaṃ prāg / anuvādyavidheyeti / yattador nityābhisaṃbandhe 'pi śabdaśaktisvābhāvyād yado 'nuvādyaviṣayatvaṃ tado vidheyaviṣayatvam / nityatvād iti / apekṣāprāṇatayāvasthānāt / śābda iti śabdenobhayoḥ saṃsparśād / ubhayoḥ saṃsparśābhāva ārthatvam / tatra dvayī gatiḥ - anyatarānupādānaṃ dvayor anupādānaṃ vā / anyatarānupādanam api yattadāśrayabhāvena dvidhā / krameṇa caitad udāhariṣyati / upakalpito nityasāpekṣatvād upasthāpitaḥ / atra ca prasiddhādiviṣayatvaṃ yadā nirdiṣṭam / sā kalā yā prasiddheti sphuṭatvena pratīteḥ / kva cit tado 'pi vyapadiśyate, tasya yacchabdenaikaviṣayatvāt / te iti ye mayaivānubhūte ity arthaḥ / anviyeṣa sa iti / atra sa iti yaḥ prakrānta ity arthaḥ / upāttavastv iti vakṣyamāṇaśloke ko 'pīti yad upāttaṃ vastu tadviṣayatvenety arthaḥ / asya upakramopasaṃhārasya prakrāntavastuviṣayasya /
children.translated_text: 'One of the two' — sometimes the word '<s>yat</s>' (which) introduces and the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) concludes; sometimes the word '<s>tat</s>' introduces and the word '<s>yat</s>' concludes. These two [arrangements] he will illustrate in the order of verbal introduction and conclusion. 'Of those two also' — the word '<s>api</s>' conjoins the meaning of the negative. For in simple negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), the meaning of the negative is the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>) and the negated meaning is the subject (<s>anuvādya</s>). But in exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>), it is the reverse — as stated before. 'Subject and predicate' — even though the connection of '<s>yat</s>' and '<s>tat</s>' is constant, by the natural power of words, '<s>yat</s>' pertains to the subject and '<s>tat</s>' pertains to the predicate. 'Being constant' — because [their connection] persists as having expectation (<s>apekṣā</s>) as its life-breath. 'Verbal' — because the word touches both. When neither is touched by a word, it is semantic (<s>ārtha</s>). There, there are two possibilities — non-adoption of one, or non-adoption of both. Non-adoption of one is also twofold, based on being the locus of '<s>yat</s>' or '<s>tat</s>.' And this he will illustrate in order. 'Arranged' — presented, because of constant co-expectation. And here, when the domain of a well-known [referent] is stated by '<s>yat</s>.' 'That art which is well-known' — because it is clearly cognized. Sometimes even '<s>tat</s>' is used to designate, because it shares the same referential domain as the '<s>yat</s>'-word. 'Those' means 'those experienced by me.' 'He searched' — here '<s>sa</s>' (he) means 'the one who was under discussion.' 'The adopted thing' — in the verse to be stated, the meaning of '<s>ko'pi</s>' is 'with reference to whatever thing was adopted.' Of this introduction-and-conclusion structure, which pertains to the thing under discussion.

body.translated_text: [Textual fragment: <s>evakemaṃ</s>]

body.text: tacchabdāt prayogātiprasaṅganiyamaṃ prakāśayan parihāryaṃ viṣayaṃ pradarśayati / -

children.translated_text: [Section 41]

children.text: yas tv ekavākya iti
children.translated_text: '<s>yas tv ekavākya</s>' (but he who [is in] a single sentence) — that is,

children.text: ⟨var. fn. - yaś caikavākya iti mūlakośayoḥ pāṭhaḥ⟩
children.translated_text: [Variant reading note: '<s>yaś caikavākya</s>' is the reading in the root-text and the lexicon]

children.text: / ekavākyagrahaṇena parāmamṛśyasya pratyakṣāyamāṇatoktā / tataś ca vākyabhede na doṣaḥ / kartṛtveneti prādhānyaṃ sūcayati aprādhānyasya parāmarśo na duṣyatīti khyāpanārtham / sa ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: By the inclusion of '<s>ekavākya</s>' (single sentence), it is stated that the [referent] being considered is directly perceivable. And therefore in sentence-division there is no fault. 'As agent' (<s>kartṛtvena</s>) indicates primacy — for the purpose of making known that non-primary reference is not faulty. '<s>Sa</s>' means:

children.text: [Page 18]
children.translated_text: [Page 18]

children.text: parāmṛṣṭaḥ / tebhya iti kartṛtvavācakād idamādibhyaś ca / asau tacchabdaḥ / asamanvayād iti tacchabdasya parokṣārthapratipādakatve saṃbandhavirodhād ity arthaḥ / tādātmyāyeti / śaśikalāmaulisvarūpatvāyety arthaḥ / ārtha iti upakramopasaṃhārakramā nirdiṣṭaḥ / kalpitatatkramādīti / kalpitaṃ tad yac chabdanirdiṣṭaṃ karmādi viṣayo 'syeti yacchabdārthaḥ karmakaraṇāditayā viṣayatvenāsya kalpita ity arthaḥ / saṃbandhadvaividhyeti śābdārthabhedena dvaividhyam / yattad iti / yacchabdasamīpe samānādhikaraṇas tacchabda upādīyamānaḥ śabdaśaktisvābhāvyāt prasiddhavastuviṣayaṃ yacchabam ākāṅkṣati / vaiyadhikaraṇyena vyavadhānena ca nirdeśe tu nirdiṣṭenaiva yadā samanvayaṃ bhajate / "na kevalaṃ yo mahato 'pabhāṣate, śṛṇoti tasmād api yaḥ sa pāpabhāg" ity atra yady api yaḥ sa iti yattador nairantaryeṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyena ca nirdeśaḥ, tathāpi na "yat tad ūrjitam" iti nyāyena (yadi tacchabdānantaraṃ praty apekṣāyām?)
children.translated_text: 'referred to.' 'From those' — from the agent-denoting words '<s>idam</s>' etc. '<s>Asau</s>' is that '<s>tat</s>'-word. 'Because of non-construal' (<s>asamanvayāt</s>) — the meaning is: because of contradiction in the relationship, since the '<s>tat</s>'-word has the function of conveying a meaning not directly present (<s>parokṣa</s>). 'For identity' (<s>tādātmyāya</s>) — the meaning is: for being identical with the nature of the one whose crown is the crescent moon. 'Semantic' (<s>ārtha</s>) — the introduction-conclusion order is stated. 'Constructed referent etc.' (<s>kalpitatatkramādi</s>) — 'that which is constructed' means what is denoted by a word; action etc. as object — the meaning of '<s>yat</s>' is that it has as its domain [the referent] constructed in the capacity of action, instrument, etc. 'Duality of relationship' — duality based on the distinction between verbal and semantic. '<s>Yat-tat</s>' — when the '<s>tat</s>'-word is employed in close proximity to the '<s>yat</s>'-word, in the same case (<s>samānādhikaraṇa</s>), by the natural power of words, it expects a '<s>yat</s>'-word having a well-known referent. But when there is indication with a different case or with intervention, it shares the construal with what is already indicated.

children.text: ⟨conj. fn. - tacchabdo yacchabdāntaraṃ praty apekṣāyām⟩
children.translated_text: [Conjectural reading note: the '<s>tat</s>'-word expects another '<s>yat</s>'-word]

children.text: iha yadi tacchabdo nirantaropāttayacchabdāpekṣayaiva prayujyate, tadā syād eṣa doṣaḥ, yāvatā "na kevalaṃ ya" ity atra yacchabdāpekṣayā vyavadhānena prādhānyāt prayuktas tacchabdāntarānākāṅkṣaḥ prasaṅgena nirantaranirdiṣṭayacchabdānvayaṃ bhajamānaḥ pūrvasaṃskāreṇa na tacchabdāntaram ākāṅkṣatīty anavadyam etat / tad itthaṃ yattador upakramopasaṃhārakramo dvividhaḥ parighaṭitaḥ / sa cātra śloke na yujyata ity āha - evaṃ ceti / tadupādāna iti / (yacchabdo nātra tad eti prakrāntas tacchabdaḥ parāmṛśyate tatsaṃbandhapratītāv ity arthaḥ?).
children.translated_text: Here, if the '<s>tat</s>'-word is used only in expectation of the closely-placed '<s>yat</s>'-word, then this fault would arise. However, since in 'na kevalaṃ ya' (not only he who) the '<s>tat</s>'-word, employed with intervention [and] because of primacy, in expectation of the '<s>yat</s>'-word, does not expect another '<s>tat</s>'-word — [and] incidentally sharing construal with the closely-stated '<s>yat</s>'-word, by prior impression it does not expect another '<s>tat</s>'-word — this is faultless. Thus the introduction-conclusion order of '<s>yat</s>' and '<s>tat</s>' is twofold, as established. And that it does not apply to this verse, he says — 'evaṃ ca' (and thus). 'Its adoption' — [means] the '<s>yat</s>'-word does not refer here to 'tat'; the '<s>tat</s>'-word under discussion is being considered — when there is cognition of that relationship, such is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Revealing the rule against over-extension from the use of the '<s>tat</s>'-word, he shows the domain to be excluded —

body.text: nanu prayogadarśanam evātra samarthakaṃ bhaviṣyatīty āśaṅkya prayogasya prāmādikapāṭhaviparyāsahetukatvam āha - mīlitam iti / tadabhinnārthaḥ tacchabdābhinnārthaḥ / tasya adaśśabdasya / tacchabdābhinnārthatve 'daśśabdasya dūṣaṇadvayam uktam / kevalādaśśabdapryoge "asau marud" ityādau yacchabdākāṅkṣā syād ity ekaṃ yacchabdasahāyasyādaśśabdasya prayoge "yo 'sau jagattraye"tyādau prayuktatacchabdākāṅkṣā na syād iti dvitīyam / atra yasya prakopetyadaśśabdarahitayacchabdaprayogo dṛṣṭāntatvenokto yathāsya kevalasya tacchabdākāṅkṣā tathādaśśabdayuktasyā(pī)ty arthaḥ / (parikalpyata iti?)

children.translated_text: [Section 42]

children.text: tasya yathoktavastv iti yathā avigānena śiṣṭaprasiddhipāraṃparyeṇoktaṃ vastu tacchabdārthavivikto viṣayas tasya tanmate asaṃbhavaḥ / tvayā hy adaśśabdasya tacchabdārthatvam ucyate tatra yacchabdaparāmarśāpekṣāprasaṅgaḥ ity arthaḥ / parikalpyata iti prayogapravāhaprāmāṇyānyathānupapattyā(vā?)yātayārthāpattyety arthaḥ / tam antareṇeti / tacchabdena prayogapravāhaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ / tadatadarthatvaniścayo vivakṣitāvivakṣitārthatvaniścayaḥ / yadi tu tām iti tadabhinnārthatānupapattiḥ parāmṛṣṭā / gate 'nugataṃ yasya sa gatānugatikaḥ / matvarthīyo 'tra ṭhanpratyayaḥ / yenaiva pathā eko gacchati tenaivāvicāritenaiva yo gacchati sa ity arthaḥ / tato bhāvapratyayaḥ / avikalpam ity akārapraśleṣaḥ / niśśaṅkam ity arthaḥ / yad vā na vikalpamātreṇa, api tu sākṣād ity arthaḥ / smṛtibhūḥ kāmaḥ / dvitīyaḥ smṛtibhūśabdaḥ smaraṇaviṣaye prayuktaḥ / dagdhatvāt smṛtimātraśeṣa ity arthaḥ / kṣatāt vadhāt / vyavahitānām eveti yathā "yo 'vikalpam" ityādau / avyavahitatve veti / yathā "smṛtibhūr" ityādau / etadartham evodāharaṇadvayam uktam /
children.translated_text: Regarding "the subject as stated" (<s>yathoktavastu</s>) — the subject spoken of through the tradition of learned convention without alteration, the domain distinguished from the meaning of the <s>tat</s>-word (that-pronoun), its impossibility in that view. For you assert that the <s>adat</s>-word (this-pronoun) has the meaning of the <s>tat</s>-word; in that case, the need arises for dependence on the reference of the <s>yat</s>-word (which-pronoun) — this is the meaning. "Is assumed" (<s>parikalpyate</s>) means: through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) arrived at by the impossibility of explaining otherwise the authority of the flow of usage — this is the meaning. "Without that" (<s>tam antareṇa</s>) — by the <s>tat</s>-word, the flow of usage is referred to. "The determination of its being that-meaning or not-that-meaning" means the determination of intended and non-intended meaning. But if "that" (<s>tām</s>) refers to the impossibility of identity of meaning. "One whose going follows another's going" is a <s>gatānugatika</s> (blind follower); here the <s>ṭhan</s>-suffix has the sense of possession. It means: one who follows the very path another has taken, without examining it. From that, the abstract suffix (<s>bhāvapratyaya</s>). "Without deliberation" (<s>avikalpam</s>) — the <s>a</s>-prefix is elided by coalescence; the meaning is "without hesitation." Or alternatively, not by mere deliberation, but directly — this is the meaning. <s>Smṛtibhū</s> means desire (<s>kāma</s>). The second word <s>smṛtibhū</s> is used in the sense of the object of remembrance. The meaning is: because it is burnt, only memory remains. "From being wounded" (<s>kṣatāt</s>) means from being slain. "Of those that are separated" — as in "<s>yo 'vikalpam</s>" etc. "When not separated" — as in "<s>smṛtibhūḥ</s>" etc. For this very purpose, two examples have been stated.

body.translated_text: Now, anticipating the objection that the observation of usage itself will suffice as authority here, he states that usage can be caused by scribal error or textual corruption — 'mīlitam' (concealed). 'Of identical meaning with that' means of identical meaning with the '<s>tat</s>'-word. Of that '<s>adas</s>'-word (that one). When the '<s>adas</s>'-word has the same meaning as the '<s>tat</s>'-word, two faults are stated. First, in the use of the '<s>adas</s>'-word alone, as in '<s>asau marut</s>' (that wind-god), there would be an expectation for the '<s>yat</s>'-word. Second, in the use of the '<s>adas</s>'-word accompanied by the '<s>yat</s>'-word, as in '<s>yo 'sau jagattraye</s>' (he who in the three worlds), there would be no expectation for the already-used '<s>tat</s>'-word. Here, the use of the '<s>yat</s>'-word without the '<s>adas</s>'-word in '<s>yasya prakope</s>' (whose anger) is cited as an illustration — just as this [word] alone expects the '<s>tat</s>'-word, so too even when accompanied by the '<s>adas</s>'-word — such is the meaning.

children.text: [Page 19]
children.translated_text: [Page 19]

children.text: tatra hīti idamādisahitaprayoge / tayor iti yattadoḥ / taditareti yadṛcchayaikataraprayoge anyatarāpekṣety arthaḥ / sutarām iti idamādisāhityena prayukto yacchabdaḥ svabhāvato vikāsitāsya eva tacchabdaṃ pratīkṣate, evaṃ tacchabdo 'pi yacchabdam iti jñeyam / etac ca krameṇodāhṛtaṃ yad etad iti, so 'yam iti ca / (tad anyena granthena pradarśaka upayujyate?) tadvad asya yacchabdasya na prakrāntaparāmarśe saṃbandho, nāpi prakraṃsyamānavastusamanvayamārgopadeśe tacchabdādhyāhāraḥ śaraṇam / sa ca satkāvyakalaṅkāyamāno heya eva
children.translated_text: Regarding "here" (<s>tatra hi</s>) — in usage accompanied by <s>idam</s>-pronouns (this-pronouns) and the like. "Of those two" (<s>tayoḥ</s>) refers to the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns. "One of the other pair" (<s>taditara</s>) means: when one or the other is employed by chance, it depends on the other — this is the meaning. "All the more" (<s>sutarām</s>) means: the <s>yat</s>-word employed together with <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc. by its very nature, with its scope expanded, awaits the <s>tat</s>-word; similarly the <s>tat</s>-word also awaits the <s>yat</s>-word — this should be understood. And this has been illustrated in order: "<s>yad etad</s>" (which this), "<s>so 'yam</s>" (that very this), etc. (Is that shown by another text as an illustration?) Similarly, this <s>yat</s>-word has no connection with the reference to something already introduced, nor is the recourse to supplying the <s>tat</s>-word a refuge for indicating the path of construing with a subject yet to be introduced. And that, being a blemish on good poetry, is to be avoided.

children.text: anuktvaiveti yattador madhye parāmṛśyam anuktvā yatra nirantaraḥ prayogaḥ yathā "yat tad ūrjitam" ityādau tatra tayor yattador yathāyogaṃ punaḥ prayogo na duṣyati yatha "nūnaṃ tad api hāritam" ityādau / tathā tayor yattadoḥ / nirantaranirdiṣṭeṣv idamādiṣu satsu tayor yattadoḥ teṣām idamādīnāṃ ca saṅghaṭitatvena sthitānāṃ yathāyogaṃ yattadoḥ pratyavekṣā na nivarttate yathā aprayukteṣv idamādiṣu kevalayoḥ pṛthagavasthitayor apekṣā na nivarttate tadvat prayukteṣv apīty arthaḥ yathā "yad etac candrāntar" iti, "so 'yaṃ paṭa" iti ca / evaṃ prakṛte 'pi "yo 'sāv" iti / tatsāṅkaryeti / yacchabdasya pṛthag idamādisāhitye tacchabdasya ca pṛthag idamādisāhitye yattadoḥ parasparasāhitye ca bahavo bhedāḥ, teṣām udāharaṇeṣu diṅmātraṃ darśitam /
children.translated_text: "Without having stated" (<s>anuktvā</s>) — without stating the referent between the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns, where the usage is uninterrupted, as in "<s>yat tad ūrjitam</s>" (which that mighty one) etc., there the re-employment of the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns as appropriate is not faulty, as in "<s>nūnaṃ tad api hāritam</s>" (surely that too was taken away) etc. Likewise of those <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns: when <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc. are stated in immediate succession, the mutual expectation of the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns standing in conjunction with those <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc. does not cease — just as when <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc. are not employed, the expectation of the two standing separately does not cease, so too when they are employed — this is the meaning. As in "<s>yad etac candrāntar</s>" (which this within the moon), "<s>so 'yaṃ paṭa</s>" (that very this cloth), etc. Similarly in the present case too: "<s>yo 'sāv</s>" (who that one). Regarding "the confusion of these" (<s>tatsāṅkarya</s>) — the separate combination of the <s>yat</s>-word with <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc., and of the <s>tat</s>-word separately with <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc., and the mutual combination of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> — these produce many varieties, of which only an indication has been shown in the examples.

body.text: saṃprati prāyeṇa vākyārthasamanvayavyāpinor yattador yo 'yaṃ nityābhisaṃbandhatvenopakramopasaṃhārakramaḥ, sa prasaṅgād vicāryate / sa ca puṣṭāpuṣṭaduṣṭabhedena trividhaḥ / puṣṭo 'pi prathamaṃ śābdatvārthatvabhedena dvividhaḥ / śābdo 'pi yacchabdopakramas tacchabdopakramaś ceti dvividhaḥ / ārtho 'pi yacchabdamātrānupādāne tacchabdasyopāttasya prasiddhānubhūtaprakrāntaviṣayeṇa yadābhisaṃbandhāt trividhaḥ / yacchabdasya ca tacchabdānupādāne kevalam upāttasya prakrāntaviṣayeṇa kalpitatatkarmādiviṣayeṇa ca tadābhisaṃbandhād dvividhaḥ / ubhayānupādāne tu dvayor upāttavastuviṣayatākalpana eka eva bhedaḥ / evaṃ śābdo dvividha ārthaḥ ṣaḍbheda ity aṣṭavidho yattador upakramopasaṃhārakramaḥ puṣṭaḥ / tac caitac ceha granthakṛtodāhṛtam / "yat tadūrjitam" ityādau tu śābdasyārthasya copasaṃhārakramasya saṅkīrṇatvam iti nāsya pṛthagbhāvaḥ / apuṣṭasya duṣṭamadhye prasaṅgena varṇayiṣyamāṇatvād idānīṃ duṣṭo vyākriyate / tatra yattadoḥ sthāne tacchabdayacchabdanairantaryeṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyena cedamādīnaṃ duṣṭataiva teṣām atadarthatvāt tannikaṭe ca prayujyamānānāṃ prasiddhimātraparāmarśakatvād, yathā "yo 'sau kutra camatkṛter" iti / evaṃ tacchabdasācivyenedamādīnām udāharaṇam ūhyam / viprakṛṣṭatvena sannikṛṣṭatve 'pi vaiyadhikaraṇyena vā teṣām prayoge na duṣṭaṃ nāduṣṭam ity apuṣṭatvam eva yathā "yo 'vikalpam" iti "smṛtibhūḥ smṛtibhūr" iti ca / evaṃ tacchabdopakrama udāharttvayam / tathā tacchabdasya parokṣāyamāṇārthapratyavamarśitvād ekavākyasthapratyakṣāyamāṇapradhānabhūtārthapratyavamarśe duṣṭatvaṃ, yathā "sa vaḥ śaśikalāmaulir" ityādau / pradhānagrahaṇena na kartṛmātraṃ nirdiṣṭam, api tu kārakāntaram api prādhānyena vivakṣitatvāt pratyakṣāyamāṇam / tena
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns which generally pervade the construal of sentence-meaning, the order of introduction and conclusion (<s>upakramopasaṃhāra</s>) which constitutes their permanent mutual connection — this is examined incidentally. And it is threefold, by the distinction of well-formed (<s>puṣṭa</s>), not-well-formed (<s>apuṣṭa</s>), and faulty (<s>duṣṭa</s>). The well-formed too is first twofold, by the distinction of verbal (<s>śābda</s>) and semantic (<s>ārtha</s>). The verbal too is twofold: initiated by the <s>yat</s>-word and initiated by the <s>tat</s>-word. The semantic too is threefold: when only the <s>yat</s>-word is not employed, the <s>tat</s>-word that has been employed connects with the <s>yat</s>-meaning through the domain of something well-known, experienced, or already introduced. And of the <s>yat</s>-word, when the <s>tat</s>-word is not employed, it alone being employed connects with the <s>tat</s>-meaning through the domain of something already introduced, or through the domain of an imagined object-of-action etc. — thus twofold. When neither is employed, the ascription of referential scope to both through supplied subject-matter is a single variety. Thus the verbal is twofold, the semantic sixfold — hence the eightfold order of introduction and conclusion of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> is well-formed. And this and that have been illustrated here by the author. In "<s>yat tad ūrjitam</s>" etc., however, there is a mixture of verbal and semantic orders of conclusion, hence it is not treated separately. Since the not-well-formed will be described incidentally within the faulty, the faulty is now analyzed. There, in the place of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s>, the use of <s>idam</s>-pronouns etc. in immediate succession and co-reference with the <s>tat</s>-word and <s>yat</s>-word is indeed faulty, because those are not-of-that-meaning and, being used near them, refer only to what is well-known — as in "<s>yo 'sau kutra camatkṛteḥ</s>" (who that one, where is the wonder). Similarly, an example of <s>idam</s>-pronouns accompanied by the <s>tat</s>-word should be inferred. When they are employed with remoteness, even in proximity, or with different grammatical reference (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>), it is neither faulty nor not-faulty — this is the not-well-formed — as in "<s>yo 'vikalpam</s>" and "<s>smṛtibhūḥ smṛtibhūḥ</s>." Similarly, examples initiated by the <s>tat</s>-word should be supplied. Likewise, since the <s>tat</s>-word refers back to a meaning that is receding from view, its use for referring to a meaning that is directly present and principal within the same sentence is faulty — as in "<s>sa vaḥ śaśikalāmauliḥ</s>" (that crescent-moon-crowned one to you) etc. By the word "principal" is indicated not merely the agent, but also other <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) that are intended as principal, being directly present. Therefore —

children.text: "sa medinīṃ vinirjitya caturjaladhimekhalām /
children.translated_text: "Having conquered the earth girdled by four oceans,

children.text: sacivārpitatadbhāras tasyām āsta yathāsukham" //
children.translated_text: having entrusted its burdens to his ministers, he dwelt there at ease."

body.text: iti medinyās tacchabdaparāmarśo na sundara ity āhuḥ / yathā yattadoḥ padārthavākyārthagatatvena dvividhāvasthāne yad ekasya padārthaniṣṭhatvād anyasya vākyārthaviṣayatvaṃ tad bhinnaviṣayatvena nityābhisaṃbandhaparipanthi duṣṭam eva / yathā
body.translated_text: Here, the reference to the earth by the <s>tat</s>-word (<s>tasyām</s>, "on that") is not elegant — so they say. Just as the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> pronouns have a twofold status in terms of word-meaning and sentence-meaning, when one is at the word-meaning level while the other is at the sentence-meaning level, that, being of different domains, obstructs the permanent connection and is indeed faulty. As in —

children.text: [Page 20]
children.translated_text: [Page 20]

children.text: "hemrāṃ bhāraśatāni vā madamucāṃ bṛndāni vā dantināṃ
children.translated_text: "Hundreds of loads of gold, or herds of rutting elephants,

children.text: śrīharṣeṇa yad arpitāni guṇine bāṇāya kutrādya tat /
children.translated_text: which (<s>yad</s>) were bestowed by <s>Śrīharṣa</s> upon the meritorious <s>Bāṇa</s> — where is that (<s>tat</s>) now?

children.text: yā bāṇena tu tasya sūktivisarair uṭṭaṅkitāḥ kīrttayas
children.translated_text: But the fame-proclamations that (<s>yāḥ</s>) were engraved by <s>Bāṇa</s> with his volleys of fine speech —

children.text: tat kalpapralaye 'pi yānti na manāṅ manye parimlānatām //"
children.translated_text: that (<s>tat</s>), even at the dissolution of the world-age, does not undergo the slightest fading, I think."

body.text: iti / yā iti padārthaviṣayatvam anipātasya tacchabdasya / tad iti tu vākyārthaviṣayas tacchabdaḥ / padārthaviṣaye tā iti syāt / atraiva "yad bāṇena tu tasye"ti "tāḥ kalpapralaye 'pi" iti ca pāṭhe yado vākyārthaviṣayatve tadaḥ padārthaniṣṭhatva udāharaṇaṃ deyam / tasmād yā bāṇena tv iti tāḥ kalpapralaye 'pīti ca paṭhanīyam / iha tu
body.translated_text: Here, <s>yā</s> (which, feminine) has word-meaning scope as a non-indeclinable; the <s>tat</s>-word (<s>tat</s>) has sentence-meaning scope. At the word-meaning level, it should be <s>tāḥ</s> (those, feminine plural). In this very [verse], with the reading "<s>yad bāṇena tu tasya</s>" and "<s>tāḥ kalpapralaye 'pi</s>," when the <s>yad</s> has sentence-meaning scope, an example should be given where <s>tad</s> has word-meaning scope. Therefore, the correct readings should be "<s>yā bāṇena tu</s>" and "<s>tāḥ kalpapralaye 'pi</s>." But here —

children.text: "indīvaraṃ yadatasīkusumasya vṛttyā yat ketakaṃ jaraḍhabhūrjadalānuvṛttyā /
children.translated_text: "The blue lotus, which (<s>yad</s>) by the manner of the <s>atasī</s>-flower; which (<s>yat</s>) the <s>ketaka</s>, by the manner of old birch-bark leaves;

children.text: yan manyase ca vakulaṃ karavīravṛttyā sā sāmprataṃ madhupa hanta tavaiva hāniḥ //"
children.translated_text: and which (<s>yat</s>) you consider the <s>vakula</s> to be, by the manner of the <s>karavīra</s>-flower — that (<s>sā</s>), O bee, alas, is indeed your own loss."

body.text: iti na kevalaṃ yacchabdo vākyārthaviṣaye, yāvat tacchabdo 'pi / yadi paraṃ sa vākyārtho hānipadena piṇḍīkṛtya prakāśitas tacchabdena parāmṛṣṭaḥ / ata evātra tacchabdasya vidheyapadārthābhiprāyeṇa strīliṅgatvam / anuvādyābhiprāyeṇa tu tat sāmpratam iti / ubhayathāpi liṅgaparigrahaḥ śiṣṭapravāhe sthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, not only does the <s>yat</s>-word have sentence-meaning scope, but so does the <s>tat</s>-word. However, that sentence-meaning, having been consolidated by the word <s>hāni</s> (loss), is expressed and referred to by the <s>tat</s>-word. For this very reason, the <s>tat</s>-word here takes feminine gender with the intention of the predicate-meaning (<s>vidheya</s>); but with the intention of the subject (<s>anuvādya</s>), [it would be] "<s>tat sāmpratam</s>" (that now, neuter). Both genders are established in learned usage.

body.text: kiṃ ca yattador nityābhisaṃbandhād guṇapradhānayoś ca saṃbandhārhatvāt parāmṛśya ekatra yacchabdavākye tacchabdavākye vā nirdiṣṭa itaravākye tadā yadā vā pratyavamṛśyate / yacchabdavākye tu nirdiṣṭena yacchabdāntareṇa guṇānāṃ pradhānānāṃ ca parasparam abhisaṃbandhāt / evaṃ ca tathā parāmarśe dvau duṣṭābhedau / yathā:
body.translated_text: Moreover, because of the permanent connection of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s>, and because of the fitness of the relation between qualifier (<s>guṇa</s>) and principal (<s>pradhāna</s>), when having been referred to, what is stated in one — the <s>yat</s>-clause or the <s>tat</s>-clause — is reflected upon in the other clause, or when and where it is recalled. But when what is stated in the <s>yat</s>-clause is connected by another <s>yat</s>-word with the qualifiers and principals of each other — thus in such cross-reference, there are two faulty varieties. As in —

body.text:
"yeṣāṃ tās tridaśebhadānasaritaḥ pītāḥ pratāpoṣmabhir
  līlāpānabhuvaś ca nandanatarucchāyāsu yaiḥ kalpitāḥ /
  yeṣāṃ huṅkṛtayaḥ kṛtāmarapurakṣobhāḥ

children.text: ⟨°pura° Ed: °pati° var (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: variant reading: <s>°pura°</s> (city) for <s>°pati°</s> (lord) [editorial note]

children.text:
kṣapācāriṇāṃ
  kiṃ tais tvatparitoṣakāri vihitaṃ kiṃ cit pravādocitam //"
children.translated_text: of those night-wanderers (demons) — was anything done by them that was pleasing to you, anything worthy of being spoken of?"

body.translated_text: "Those whose rivers of celestial elephant-liquor were drunk by the heat of their valor, and by whom pleasure-drinking grounds were established in the shade of the <s>Nandana</s>-trees of paradise; whose war-cries caused the trembling of the city of the gods,

body.text: iti / kṣapācāriṇām iti ṣaṣṭhyantaṃ yacchabdena saṃbaddhaṃ yacchadbāntareṇa partyavamṛṣṭam / kṣapācāribhir iti pāṭho nyāyyaḥ / evaṃ tacchabdavākye nirdiṣṭaṃ yacchabdaiḥ parāmṛśyamānaṃ na duṣyati, yathā ca:
body.translated_text: Thus. The genitive-ending form '<s>kṣapācāriṇām</s>' (of the night-wanderers) is connected by the <s>yat</s>-pronoun and is referred back to by another <s>yat</s>-pronoun. The reading '<s>kṣapācāribhiḥ</s>' (by the night-wanderers, instrumental) is proper. Thus, what is specified in the <s>tat</s>-pronoun clause, when referred to by <s>yat</s>-pronouns, is not faulty. For example:

children.text: "puṇḍrekṣoḥ paripākapāṇḍunibiḍe yo madhyame parvaṇi
children.translated_text: "In the middle joint of the sugarcane, dense and pale with ripeness,

children.text: khyātaḥ kiṃ ca rasaḥ kaṣāyamadhuro yo rājajambūphale /
children.translated_text: what is that well-known flavor, astringent-sweet, which is in the royal <s>jambū</s>-fruit?

children.text: tasyāsvādadaśāviluṇṭanapaṭur yeṣāṃ vacovibhramaḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose verbal charm is skilled at looting the pleasure of tasting that —

children.text: sarvatraiva jayanti citramatayas te bharttṛmeṇḍādayaḥ //"
children.translated_text: everywhere victorious are those of wonderful thought, <s>Bhartṛmeṇḍa</s> and the rest."

body.text: iti / atra dvitīye yacchabdavākye rasaḥ parāmṛśyo nirdiṣṭas tacchabdena parāmṛśyate / prathame yacchabdavākye tu yacchadaparāmarśo na yujyate dvayor asaṃbandhād, yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus. Here in the second <s>yat</s>-clause, 'flavor' (<s>rasa</s>), which is to be referred to, is specified and is referred back to by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun. But in the first <s>yat</s>-clause, a reference by the <s>yat</s>-pronoun is not appropriate, since the two [clauses] are unconnected. For example:

children.text: "namo 'stu tābhyo bhuvane jayanti tāḥ sudhāmucas tāś ca kavīndrasūktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Homage to them — they triumph in the world! Those nectar-shedding utterances of the king of poets,

children.text: bhavaikavicchedi kathāśarīratām upaiti yāsāṃ caritaṃ pinākinaḥ //"
children.translated_text: which take on the embodiment of a narrative that severs [the bonds of] existence — the deeds of the Trident-Bearer (<s>Pinākī</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>)."

body.text: iti kavīndrasūktīnāṃ tacchabdavati vākye(na?) nirdiṣṭānāṃ tacchabdāntareṇa parāmarśo na yuktaḥ / kiṃ ca yattacchabdayoḥ svabhāvena vākyabhedotthāpakatve yad ekataravākye 'nyatarat padaṃ (prayujyānyatarat?) prayujyate tad api duṣṭam eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus, the reference by another <s>tat</s>-pronoun to the 'utterances of the king of poets,' which have been specified in the clause containing a <s>tat</s>-pronoun, is not appropriate. Moreover, when the <s>yat</s>- and <s>tat</s>-pronouns by their nature produce a division of clauses, and when in one clause one of the two words is used in place of the other, that too is indeed faulty. For example:

children.text: "aprākṛtasya caritātiśayaiś ca dṛṣṭair atyadbhutair apahṛtasya tathāpi nāsthā /
children.translated_text: "Of one whose extraordinary deeds have been witnessed, truly marvelous, and who is captivated by them — yet no attachment [arises];

children.text: ko 'py eṣa vīraśiśukākṛtir aprameyamāhātmyasārasam udāyamayaḥ padārthaḥ //"
children.translated_text: this is some ineffable entity, having the form of a child-hero, whose essence is of immeasurable greatness."

children.text: [Page 21]
children.translated_text: [Page 21]

children.text: ity atra yady apīty apekṣitam / na ca tadekavākyatāyāṃ saṃbandhuṃ yogyam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'although' (<s>yady api</s>) is expected. But it is not fit to be connected in a single-clause construction.

body.text: ekatrāpi vākye guṇakriyādigataṃ kalpitaṃ bhedam āśritya prakrāntavastuviṣayatacchabdaprayoge pradhānakriyāyāṃ parāmṛśyasya pradhānatvād eva svarūpeṇa nirdeśe guṇakriyādiviṣaye tu tacchabdena parāmarśe nyāyye yadviparyayakaraṇaṃ tad duṣṭam eva / yathā
body.translated_text: Even within a single clause, when a distinction is assumed based on a subordinate action or quality and the <s>tat</s>-pronoun is used for the main subject under discussion, since the referent is primary in the principal action, it should be specified in its own form; but in the domain of subordinate action and quality, reference by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun is proper — doing the reverse is indeed faulty. For example:

children.text: "prajānām eva bhūtyarthaṃ sa tābhyo balim agrahīt /
children.translated_text: "For the very prosperity of his subjects, he collected tribute from them;

children.text: sahasraguṇam utsraṣṭum ādatte hi rasaṃ raviḥ //"
children.translated_text: for the sun absorbs moisture only to release it a thousandfold."

body.text: iti / "baliṃ prajābhyo jagrāha sa tāsām eva bhūtaye" iti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ / tathaikaviṣayatve yattador ekasya dravyādiviṣayatve 'nyasya kālādigocaratve duṣṭam eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus. The reading '<s>baliṃ prajābhyo jagrāha sa tāsām eva bhūtaye</s>' (he collected tribute from the subjects for their very welfare) would be the correct reading. Likewise, when the <s>yat</s>- and <s>tat</s>-pronouns have the same referent, if one concerns a substance and the other concerns time and the like, it is indeed faulty. For example:

children.text: "tvam evaṃ saundaryā sa ca ruciratāyāḥ paricitaḥ
children.translated_text: "You in this way with beauty, and he, acquainted with loveliness —

children.text: kalānāṃ sīmānaṃ param iha yuvām eva bhajathaḥ /
children.translated_text: you two alone attain the ultimate boundary of the arts.

children.text: ayi! dvandvaṃ diṣṭyā tad iti subhage! saṃvadati vā-
children.translated_text: Ah! 'That pair — by good fortune!' says, O beautiful one,

children.text: mataḥ śeṣaṃ yat syāj jitam iha tadānīṃ guṇitayā //"
children.translated_text: the left [side]; whatever would remain — that then is conquered by the multiplied one."

body.text: atra "ataḥ śeṣaṃ cet syād" iti paṭhanīyaṃ cec chabdasya yadiśabdārthatvāt / tathā prakrāntaviṣayatve tacchabdasya vyavasthite tadviṣaye prakramyamāṇavastugocaratvaṃ doṣa eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: Here, one should read '<s>ataḥ śeṣaṃ cet syāt</s>' (if there were a remainder from this), since the word <s>cet</s> has the meaning of the word <s>yadi</s> (if). Likewise, when the <s>tat</s>-pronoun has been established for the subject under discussion, making the domain of the subject being introduced [the referent of] the <s>tat</s>-pronoun is a fault. For example:

children.text: "ye saṃtoṣasukhaprabuddhamanasas teṣāṃ na bhinno mado
children.translated_text: "Those whose minds are awakened by the happiness of contentment — for them there is no separate intoxication;

children.text: ye 'py ete dhanalobhasaṃkuladhiyas teṣāṃ tu dūre nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: and those whose minds are agitated by the greed for wealth — for them [happiness] is far from people.

children.text: itthaṃ kasya kṛte kṛtaḥ sa vidhinā tādṛk padaṃ saṃpadāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus for whose sake was that position of fortune created by Fate?

children.text: svātmany eva samāptahemamahimā merur na me rocate //"
children.translated_text: With the glory of gold completed in itself alone, [Mount] <s>Meru</s> does not please me."

body.text: atra meruḥ prakramyamāṇaḥ sa ity anena parāmṛṣṭaḥ / etad vākyabheda udāharaṇam / ekavākye tu:
body.translated_text: Here <s>Meru</s>, the subject being introduced, is referred to by '<s>sa</s>' (that). This is an illustration of clause-division. But in a single clause:

body.text: "tīrthe tadīye gajasetubandhāt pratīpagām uttarato 'sya gaṅgām /"
body.translated_text: "At the <s>tīrtha</s> of that [king], the <s>Gaṅgā</s> flowing northward from the elephant-bridge —"

body.text: iti deyam / tathā nirvīpsenaikenopakrame savīpsenānyena parāmarśo duṣṭa eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: this should be [the example]. Likewise, when something is introduced without repetition (<s>nirvīpsā</s>) and referred back to by another [pronoun] with repetition (<s>savīpsā</s>), it is indeed faulty. For example:

body.text: "yaḥ kalyāṇabahirbhūtaḥ sa sa durgatim aśnute /"
body.translated_text: "Whoever is excluded from virtue, he, he goes to a bad destination."

body.text: savīpsena tv ekena prakrame nirvīpsenānyenopasaṃhāraḥ savīpsasya pratyavamṛṣṭatvād duṣṭo 'nvayaḥ

children.text: ⟨na duṣṭānvayaḥ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: 'not a faulty construction' (conjectured by the editor)]

children.text: kin tv apuṣṭa eva / yathā:
children.translated_text: but rather merely unsupported. For example:

body.translated_text: However, when one [pronoun] with repetition introduces and another without repetition concludes, since the one with repetition has already been referred to, the construction is faulty —

children.text: "kalyāṇānāṃ tvam asi mahasāmīśiṣe tvaṃ vidhatse
children.translated_text: "You are [the lord] of auspicious things; you command greatness; you bestow

children.text: puṇyāṃ lakṣmīm iha mayi ciraṃ dhehi deva! prasīda /
children.translated_text: meritorious fortune; O god, place it in me for long! Be gracious!

children.text: yad yat pratijahi jagannātha! namrasya tan me
children.translated_text: Whatever you reject, O lord of the world, for me who bows — that,

children.text: bhadraṃ bhadraṃ vitara bhagavan! bhūyase maṅgalāya //"
children.translated_text: O blessed one, bestow it again and again as auspicious, for greater good fortune!"

body.text: iti / atra yad yad iti nirdiṣṭaṃ kevalena tacchabdena parāmṛṣṭam / etad yacchabdasya savīpsasyodāharaṇam / tacchabdasya tu savīpsasya nirvīpsena parāmarśa udāharaṇaṃ yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus. Here what is specified by '<s>yad yad</s>' (whatever, whatever) is referred to by the simple <s>tat</s>-pronoun alone. This is an illustration of the <s>yat</s>-pronoun with repetition. For the <s>tat</s>-pronoun with repetition, an illustration of reference without repetition is as follows:

body.text:
"kṣāntaṃ na kṣamayā gṛhocitasukhaṃ tyaktaṃ na santoṣataḥ
  soḍho dussahaśītavātatapanakleśo na taptaṃ tapaḥ /
  dhyātaṃ nityam ahar niśaṃ niyamitaprāṇair na śambhoḥ

children.text: ⟨var. śaureḥ⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: <s>Śauri</s> (i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>)]

children.text:
padaṃ
  tat tat karma kṛtaṃ yad eva munibhis tais taiḥ phalair vañcitāḥ //"
children.translated_text: all those, those very actions that the sages performed — by those, those very fruits they were cheated."

body.translated_text: "Endurance was practiced, but not through forbearance; household comforts were abandoned, but not from contentment; the unbearable hardship of cold, wind, and heat was borne, but no <s>tapas</s> (penance) was performed; meditation was constant day and night with controlled breath, but not on the abode of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —

children.text: [Page 22]
children.translated_text: [Page 22]

children.text: iti / yatra tu savīpsasya prakrame savīpsena pratyavamarśas tatra puṣṭatvam eva yathā
children.translated_text: Thus. But where the referent with repetition in the introduction is referred back to with repetition, there it is indeed well-supported. For example:

children.text: "yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibhartti svabhujagurum adaḥ pāṇḍavīnāṃ camūnāṃ
children.translated_text: "Whoever, whoever bears a weapon, heavy on his own arm — from those armies of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> women,

children.text: yo yaḥ pāñcālagotre śiśur adhikavayā garbhaśayyāṃ gato vā /
children.translated_text: whoever, whoever in the <s>Pāñcāla</s> clan, whether a child, one of greater age, or one gone to the bed of the womb,

children.text: yo yas tatkarmasākṣī carati mayi raṇe yaś ca yaś ca pradīptaḥ
children.translated_text: whoever, whoever walks as a witness of that deed in battle against me, and whoever, whoever blazes [with fury] —

children.text: krodhāndhas tasya tasya svayam api jagatām antakasyāntako 'ham //"
children.translated_text: blinded by wrath, of each and every one of them, I myself am the destroyer of the Destroyer of worlds (<s>Yama</s>)."

body.text: iti / yatra cānekasya savīpsasya cānekena pratyavamarśas, tatrāpi puṣṭatvam eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus. And where there is reference to multiple [entities] with repetition by multiple [pronouns], there too it is well-supported. For example:

children.text: "yo yo yaṃ yam avāpnuyād avayavoddeśaṃ spṛśan pāṇinā
children.translated_text: "Whatever, whatever portion of a limb one touches with the hand,

children.text: tat tanmātrakam eva yatra sa sa te rūpaṃ paraṃ manyate /
children.translated_text: only so much of that, that very thing, wherever it is — he considers it your supreme form.

children.text: tajjātyandhapuraṃ ha hā karipate! nīto 'si durvedhasā
children.translated_text: Alas, O lord of elephants, the city of the congenitally blind! You have been brought [there] by cruel fate!

children.text: ko nāmātra bhaved batākhilabhavan māhātmyavedī janaḥ //"
children.translated_text: Who indeed here could be a person who knows the full majesty of all existence?"

body.text: iti / yadi paraṃ yaṃ yam iti prakrame tat tanmātrakam eveti pratyavamarśe vidheyāvimarśaḥ savīpsasya tadarthasya samāse guṇībhāvāt / naitat / mātragrahaṇenāvadhāraṇam ucyate yathā - "prātipadikārthaliṅgaparimāṇavacanamātre" iti / taccāvadhāryamāṇaparatantram ity avadhāryamāṇasyaiva savīpsasya tadarthasyodrekāt prādhānyam akhaṇḍitam eva / pūrvapadārthaprādhānyena kva cit supsupeti samāso dṛśyate, yathā:
body.translated_text: Thus. If, however, in the introduction '<s>yaṃ yam</s>' (whichever) and in the reference '<s>tat tanmātrakam eva</s>' (only that much of that) — [one might object that] there is no reference to the predicate, since the meaning of the repeated pronoun becomes subordinate in the compound. This is not so. By the word <s>mātra</s> (only, mere), a restriction is expressed, as in '<s>prātipadikārthaliṅgaparimāṇavacanamātre</s>' (only in the meaning, gender, measure, and number of the nominal stem). And that [restriction] is dependent upon what is being restricted; therefore the predominance of the meaning of the very repeated pronoun being restricted is unimpaired. In some cases, a compound of the type <s>sup-sup</s> is seen with predominance of the prior member's meaning. For example:

children.text: "nirvāṇabhūyiṣṭham athāsya vīryaṃ sandhukṣayantīva vapur guṇena /
children.translated_text: "Her valor, mostly extinguished, as if being rekindled by her bodily grace —

children.text: anuprayātā vanadevatābhyām adṛśyata sthāvararājakanyā //"
children.translated_text: the princess of the trees, followed by the forest deities, was seen."

body.text: iti / atra hi bhūyiṣṭhaṃ nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇabhūyiṣṭham iti samāse nirvāṇārthasyaiva prādhānyaṃ tasya vīryaviśeṣaṇatvenāvasthitatvād / na tadvad iha tattanmātrakam iti tadarthasya prādhānyaṃ bhaviṣyati / kevalaṃ kṛte 'vadhāraṇārthe mātraśabde kimarthaḥ kapratyayaḥ / tasminn api vā kṛte evaśabdaḥ kimarthaḥ / evaśabda eva vā kiṃ na kriyate / naitat / kapratyayasya tāvad atra kutsāpratipādakatvāt / na paunaruktyaṃ tan tameveti kevalaivaśabdaprayoge vikṣipta iva tadarthaḥ pratīyate / mātragrahaṇe tu piṇḍitasyaiva tadarthasya pratītir ity asti viśeṣaḥ / yadi paraṃ dvayor upādānaṃ lokapratītyanusaraṇena dṛḍhīkṛtāvadhāraṇapratītyartham / dṛśyate hīdṛśeṣu dvayor avadhāraṇapratipādakayoḥ prayogaḥ / yathā - "bālā kevalam eva roditi galallolodakair aśrubhiḥ" / atraiva tad iti nirvīpsena tadā nirdiṣṭaṃ jātyandhapuraṃ nirvīpsenaiva yadā pratyavamṛśyate / tataś cātrānuguṇaparāmarśān na doṣaḥ kaś cit /
body.translated_text: Thus. Here indeed, in the compound '<s>nirvāṇabhūyiṣṭham</s>' (mostly extinguished), the meaning of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction) alone has predominance, because it is established as the qualifier of <s>vīrya</s> (valor). The case here with '<s>tattanmātrakam</s>' is not similar — the predominance of the <s>tat</s>-meaning will not [be lost]. [One might ask:] when the word <s>mātra</s> has already been used for the purpose of restriction, what is the purpose of the suffix <s>ka</s>? Or when that too has been used, what is the purpose of the word <s>eva</s>? Or why not simply use the word <s>eva</s> alone? This is not so. The suffix <s>ka</s> here has the function of expressing contempt. There is no redundancy. With the use of just the word <s>eva</s> alone in '<s>tan tam eva</s>' (that very one), the meaning would be perceived in a scattered manner. But with the word <s>mātra</s>, the perception of the very meaning of <s>tat</s> is consolidated — so there is a difference. However, the use of both is for the purpose of strengthening the restrictive perception in accordance with common usage. For indeed, in such cases the use of two words expressing restriction is observed. For example: '<s>bālā kevalam eva roditi</s>' (the girl merely only weeps with tears flowing down her cheeks). Here, the reference '<s>tat</s>' without repetition is used to refer back to '<s>jātyandhapuram</s>' (the city of the congenitally blind), which was specified without repetition. Therefore, since the reference is concordant, there is no fault whatsoever.

body.text: tathā (yatra) pūrvavākye yacchabdo nirdiṣṭa uttaravākye tu (na) tacchabdo nirdiṣṭaḥ, tatra sākāṅkṣatvād duṣṭaiva yathā -
body.translated_text: Likewise, where the <s>yat</s>-pronoun is specified in the first clause but the <s>tat</s>-pronoun is not specified in the second clause, there, because of expectancy [remaining unfulfilled], it is indeed faulty. For example:

body.text: "mīlitaṃ yad abhirāmatādhike sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtam /"
body.translated_text: "That closing of the eyes which was done so fittingly by the lotuses toward the moon, which excels in beauty —"

body.text: iti / uttaravākyagatatvena tu yacchabdaprayoge pūrvavākye tacchabdaprayoge na duṣṭatvam, api tu prākpratipāditaṃ puṣṭatvam eva sāmānyenopakramāt paścād viśeṣasyotthāpanāt / etadabhiprāyeṇa kalpitatatkarmādiviṣayatvam uktam / udāharaṇaṃ tu "sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtaṃ mīlitaṃ yadabhirāmatādhike" iti pūrvaślokārdhapāṭhaviparyaye yathā / yattacchabdayor aviśiṣṭe 'pi parāmarśakatve uttaravākye nirdiṣṭo yacchabdaḥ svabhāvata āvidūryeṇa pūrvavākyārthāśliṣṭatayā vastu parāmṛśati, tacchabdas tu parokṣāyamāṇārthaniṣṭhatvāt vaidūryeṇa / āvidūryaṃ ca prakṛtārthaṃ prakṛṣṭatāṃ nayad vākyārthaṃ śleṣayati / tataś ca tathābhūte viṣaye yacchabdasya prayogārhatve tacchabdasya prayogo 'puṣṭa eva.
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>yat</s>-word is employed in the latter clause, the use of the <s>tat</s>-word in the former clause is not a defect; rather, it is precisely the excellence previously discussed, since the general [topic] is introduced first and the particular [detail] is then brought forth. With this intention, it was said that the subject matter concerns constructed <s>tatkarma</s> and the like. The example, however, is: 'Well done [is what was] done to the moon with lotuses—the closing [of eyes] when loveliness is in excess'—when the first half-verse is read in reverse order. Although the <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> words have the same capacity for back-reference, the <s>yat</s>-word, being placed in the latter clause, by its nature refers to the actual object with proximity, being closely connected with the meaning of the former clause; while the <s>tat</s>-word [refers] with remoteness, because it pertains to a meaning that is becoming indirect. And proximity, leading the subject matter to eminence, binds together the sentence-meaning. Therefore, where the <s>yat</s>-word deserves to be used in such a context, the use of the <s>tat</s>-word is indeed unexcellent.

children.text: [Page 23]
children.translated_text: [Page 23]

children.text: "tasyāḥ śalākāñjananirmiteva kāntir bhruvor ānatarekhayor yā /
children.translated_text: "The beauty of her eyebrows with their curved lines, which appeared as if fashioned with a collyrium-stick—

children.text: tāṃ vīkṣya līlācaturām anaṅgaḥ svacāpasaundaryam adaṃ mumoca //"
children.translated_text: seeing her, playful and charming, <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love) abandoned his pride in the beauty of his own bow."

body.text: atra "sā yāṃ vīkṣye"ti yattadau viparyayeṇa paṭhanīyau / yathā ca:
body.translated_text: Here, '<s>sā yāṃ vīkṣya</s>' should be read with <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> reversed. And likewise:

children.text: "dṛṣṭir nāmṛtavarṣiṇī smitamadhuprasyandi vaktraṃ na kiṃ
children.translated_text: "Is the gaze not one that rains nectar? Does not the face overflow with the honey of smiles?

children.text: nārdrārdraṃ hṛdayaṃ na candanarasasparśāni vāṅgāni ca /
children.translated_text: Is not the heart most tender? Are not the limbs like the touch of sandalwood paste?

children.text: kasmin labdhapadena te kṛtam idaṃ krūreṇa dagdhāgninā
children.translated_text: In whom has this cruel fire, having found a foothold, done this [deed]?

children.text: nūnaṃ vajramayo 'nya eva dahanas tasyedam āceṣṭitam //"
children.translated_text: Surely the fire that burns must be another one, made of diamond—this is its doing."

body.text: atra yasyeti paṭhanīyam / yathā ca:
body.translated_text: Here '<s>yasya</s>' should be read [instead]. And likewise:

children.text: "ācāryo me sa khalu bhagavān asmadgrāhyanāmā
children.translated_text: "That blessed one is indeed my teacher, he whose name we must learn;

children.text: tasmād eṣā dhanur upaniṣat tatprasādāt kṣamo 'pi /
children.translated_text: therefore this <s>Upaniṣad</s> (secret teaching) of the bow [comes from him], and by his grace I too am able.

children.text: adhyāsīnaḥ katham aham aho vartma vaikhānasānāṃ
children.translated_text: Seated thus, how can I—alas—following the path of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> (forest hermits),

children.text: sītāpāṇigrahaṇapaṇitaṃ cāpam āropayāmi //"
children.translated_text: string the bow that was wagered for the hand of <s>Sītā</s>?"

body.text: atra ca "yasmād eṣā dhanur upaniṣad" iti paṭhanīyam / evaṃ ca prāg ukte "hemno bhārataśatānī"tyādau "tā bāṇena tu tasya sūktivisarair uṭṭaṅkitāḥ kīrtayo yāḥ kalpapralaye 'pi yānti na manāṅ manye parimlānatām" iti paṭhanīyam / api ca parāmṛśyam anuktvā yacchabdena ca vākyārthopakrame tacchabdavati parāmṛśyanirdeśe pūrvavākyārthe parāmṛśyam aspṛśantī upaplavamānā pratītir iti vākyārthapratipattiviprakarṣād apuṣṭatvam / yathā:
body.translated_text: And here '<s>yasmād eṣā dhanur upaniṣad</s>' should be read. Thus in the previously cited [verse] 'hundreds of <s>bhāras</s> of gold' and so on, it should be read as: 'those glories of his, engraved by the arrow-release of well-spoken words, which even at the dissolution of the <s>kalpa</s> do not in the slightest, I think, fade away.' Moreover, when the referent is not mentioned first and the sentence-meaning is introduced with the <s>yat</s>-word, while the reference to the referent appears with a <s>tat</s>-word—the cognition, not touching the referent in the meaning of the former clause, becomes disturbed; thus, due to the distance in apprehending the sentence-meaning, there is lack of excellence. As in:

children.text: "pādāhataṃ yad utthāya mūrdhānam adhirohati /
children.translated_text: "That which, when kicked by the foot, rises up and mounts the head—

children.text: svasthād evāvamānena dehinas tad varaṃ rajaḥ //"
children.translated_text: rather than [enduring] disrespect from one who is self-sufficient, that [role] of dust is preferable for an embodied being."

body.text: ata evātra ślokārdhayor viparyayapāṭhe puṣṭatvam eva / tathā pūrvavākyārthe nirdiṣṭasyārthasyottaravākyārthe sarvanāmamātreṇa parāmarśe nyāyye yaḥ svaśabdasahitasya sarvanāmno nirdeśaḥ sa duṣṭa eva / yathā:
body.translated_text: For this very reason, when the two half-verses are read in reversed order here, there is indeed excellence. Similarly, when a meaning stated in the former clause is to be referred back to in the latter clause by a mere pronoun, the indication of that pronoun accompanied by its own [substantive] word is indeed a defect. As in:

children.text: "udanvacchinnā bhūḥ sa ca nidhir apāṃ yojanaśataṃ
children.translated_text: "The earth is bounded by the ocean; and that reservoir of waters extends a hundred <s>yojanas</s>;

children.text: sadā pānthaḥ pūṣā gaganaparimāṇaṃ kalayati /
children.translated_text: the sun, an eternal traveler, measures the expanse of the sky.

children.text: iti prāyo bhāvaḥ sphuradavadhimudrāmukulitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, for the most part, [ordinary] cognition has its limits sealed by manifest boundaries;

children.text: satāṃ prajñonmeṣaḥ punar ayam asīmā vijayate //"
children.translated_text: but this dawning of the wisdom of the good is limitless—it triumphs!"

body.text: iti / atra "sa ca nidhir apām" iti sasvaśabdaḥ sarvanāmno nirdeśaḥ / evaṃ "rāmagiryāśrameṣv" iti prakṛte "tasminn adrau kati cid" ity atra jñeyam / atra tu ke cit samarthayante - "rāmagiryāśrameṣv" iti rāmagiriḥ samāsa upasarjanībhūto buddhāv udrekeṇānavabhāsāt kathaṃ sarvanāmnā parāmṛśyate "sarvanāmnānusandhir vṛtticchannasye"ti pradhānabhūtaparāmṛśyābhiprāyeṇa sthitaṃ yathā "samyagjñānapūrvikā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhir iti tad vyutpādyate" iti / atrādrāv iti nirdiśyamānam adrimātrapratīter na prakṛtam adriṃ gamayet / tasmād ubhayam atropādeyaṃ yathā "atha śabdnānuśāsanam / keṣāṃ śabdānām" iti / giriśabdena girau prakrānta adriśabdena paryāyāntareṇa tv āgatam āsamañjasyaṃ duṣpariharam eveti / udanvacchinnā bhūr ity atra tu udanvataḥ parāmṛśyasya naikaṭhyād yogyatvāc ca bhuvaḥ strītvena sa iti parāmarśānarhatvāc ca sarvanāmaparāmarśa eva yukto, na punaḥ svaśabdagocaratvam ity atra duṣṭataiva / kiṃ ca samudāyasya kasya cit kena cid vākyena nirdeśe vākyāntare tadavayavasya nirdhāreṇa karttavye tasya samudāyasaya nirdhāraṇaviṣayapratītaye

children.text: [Page 24]
children.translated_text: [Page 24]

children.text: yacchabdena nirdeśe karttavye nirdhāryamāṇasyāvayavasya nirdeśo duṣṭa eva / yathā:
children.translated_text: when the indication should be made with the <s>yat</s>-word for the purpose of cognizing the specification-object, the indication of the part being specified is indeed a defect. As in:

body.translated_text: Here, '<s>sa ca nidhir apām</s>' ('and that reservoir of waters') is an indication of a pronoun accompanied by its own substantive word. Similarly, in the context of '<s>Rāmagiryāśrameṣu</s>' ('in the hermitages of <s>Rāmagiri</s>'), the passage '<s>tasminn adrau katicit</s>' ('on that mountain, for some [days]') should be understood [in this light]. Here, however, some argue: since <s>Rāmagiri</s> is subordinated in the compound '<s>Rāmagiryāśrameṣu</s>' and does not prominently appear in the cognition due to its subordinate status, how can it be referred back to by a pronoun? [The answer is:] 'The connection by a pronoun is of what is concealed by a compound'—this is established with the intention that it refers to the principal referent, just as in '<s>samyagjñānapūrvikā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ</s>' ('the accomplishment of all human aims is preceded by right knowledge')—'that is to be explained.' Here, what is indicated as '<s>adrau</s>' ('on the mountain'), since it gives rise to only the concept of 'mountain' [in general], would not lead to the particular mountain under discussion. Therefore, both [devices] should be employed here, as in '<s>atha śabdānuśāsanam / keṣāṃ śabdānām</s>' ('Now, the teaching of words / of which words?'). By the word '<s>giri</s>' the mountain that has been introduced is [referenced], but by the word '<s>adri</s>' as a synonym, the resultant incongruity is indeed difficult to resolve. In '<s>udanvacchinnā bhūḥ</s>' however, since the ocean as the referent is nearby, since it is fitting, and since the earth, being feminine, is not suitable for back-reference with '<s>sa</s>' [masculine pronoun]—the pronoun-reference alone is appropriate, not the scope of the [substantive] word—so here there is indeed a defect. Furthermore, when some aggregate has been indicated by one sentence and in another sentence a part of that aggregate is to be specified, since the aggregate must be the object of specification,

children.text: "tasmād ajāyata manur navarājabījaṃ yasyānvaye sa sagaraḥ sa bhagīrathaś ca /
children.translated_text: "From him was born <s>Manu</s>, the seed of nine kings, in whose lineage were that <s>Sagara</s> and that <s>Bhagīratha</s>;

children.text: ekena yena jaladhiḥ parikhānito 'yam anyena siddhasaritā paripūritaś ca //"
children.translated_text: by one of whom this ocean was made into a moat, and by the other it was filled with the river achieved through <s>siddhi</s> (supernatural accomplishment)."

body.text: atra sa sagaraḥ sa bhagīrathaś ceti yan nirdiṣṭaṃ tasyaiketyādinā nirdhāraṇaṃ vihitam / nirdhāraṇaṃ ca jātiguṇakriyābhiḥ samudāyād ekadeśasya pṛthak karaṇam / na cātra samudāyaḥ kena cit padena nirdiṣṭaḥ / yaccaikeneti nirdiṣṭam, tan na samudāyaḥ, api tv ekadeśaḥ / tataś ca nirdeśyānirdeśād anirdeśyanirdeśyāc cātra duṣṭatvam / evaṃ ca samudāyasyaiva nirdhāraṇaviṣayasya yacchabdena nirdeśe karttavye "eko yayor jalanidhīn nicakhāna sapta gāṅgaiḥ payobhir abhivarṣitavān dvitīyaḥ" iti pāṭhaḥ śreyān /
body.translated_text: Here, what was indicated as 'that <s>Sagara</s>' and 'that <s>Bhagīratha</s>' has its specification made by '<s>ekena</s>' ('by one') and so on. Specification is the separating out of one part from an aggregate by means of genus, quality, or action. But here no aggregate has been indicated by any word. And what is indicated by '<s>ekena</s>' is not the aggregate but a part. Therefore, from the non-indication of what should be indicated and the indication of what should not be indicated, there is a defect here. And thus, when the aggregate that is the object of specification should have been indicated by the <s>yat</s>-word, the reading '<s>eko yayor jalanidhīn nicakhāna sapta gāṅgaiḥ payobhir abhivarṣitavān dvitīyaḥ</s>' ('one of the two of whom dug the seven seas, the second showered them with the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>') would be better.

body.text: kva cid yattacchabdāv agrahaṇena vidhyanuvādabhāvena vākyārthaprastāve yadantarānyathākaraṇaṃ tatra duṣṭatvaṃ yathā:
body.translated_text: Sometimes, when the <s>yat-tat</s> words are not employed, and the sentence-meaning is presented through the relation of injunction and restatement (<s>vidhi-anuvāda</s>), an alteration made within that [arrangement] constitutes a defect. As in:

body.text: "yat tvannetrasamānakānti salile magnaṃ tad indīvaram"
body.translated_text: "That blue lotus which, equal in beauty to your eye, had sunk into the water"—
