body.text: iti / atra prathamatṛtīyayoḥ pādayor yattacchabdaparigraheṇa vidhyanuvādabhāvenopanibandhaḥ / dvitīyapādagatatvena tadullaṅghanaṃ doṣaḥ / indīvarāṇāṃ rājahaṃsānāṃ ca bahutvāt sītāsaṃbandhivastūpamitayor indīvararājahaṃsayor vyāvṛttyarthaṃ vidhyanuvādabhāvaparigrahaḥ / candrasya tv ekatvāt tadakaraṇam iti ke cit / tad asat / candrasyāpi dvitīyācandrādibhedena bahutvasaṃbhavāt tatrāpi vidhyanuvādabhāvo yuktaḥ / indīvarāṇāṃ vyaktibhedena mukhyo bhedaḥ / candrasya punar ekavyaktirūpasya kālabhedād avasthābhedāc ca bhinnatvam amukhyam iti cen na / bhinnā eva candravyaktayaḥ / anyo hi dvitīyācandro 'nyaś ca pūrṇacandraḥ / ataś caiva dvitīyācandrādivyāvṛttyā pūrṇacandrapratītyarthaṃ mukhacchāyānukārīti viśeṣaṇaṃ dattam / na hi śaśiśabdaḥ pūrṇacandrābhidhāyī, tasya candramātravācakatvāt / saṅkhyāvyavahāreṣu candrasyaikatvapratītir iti cet / kva cij jātivyavahāreṣv apīndīvarādīnām ekatvaṃ siddham / tasmāt kavivyavahāre candragatatvenānekatvasya vyavahārāt tadāśrayeṇeha vidhyanuvādabhāvaḥ śreyān /
body.translated_text: here, the composition of the first and third <s>pādas</s> (verse-quarters) follows the injunction-restatement relation through the employment of the <s>yat-tat</s> words. The transgression of that [relation] in the second <s>pāda</s> is a defect. Since blue lotuses and royal swans are many, the injunction-restatement relation is adopted for the purpose of distinguishing the particular blue lotus and royal swan that are compared to things associated with <s>Sītā</s>. But since the moon is singular, it is not done [for the moon]—so say some. That is wrong. Since the moon too admits of multiplicity through the distinction of the second-day moon and so on, the injunction-restatement relation is appropriate there too. The differentiation of blue lotuses is primary, being through distinct individuals. But the multiplicity of the moon, which is a single individual, through distinctions of time and state is non-primary—if one objects thus, [we reply:] no, the moon-individuals are indeed distinct; for the second-day moon is different and the full moon is different. And for this very reason, the qualifier 'imitating the complexion of the face' was given for the purpose of cognizing the full moon by excluding the second-day moon and so on. For the word '<s>śaśin</s>' does not denote specifically the full moon, since it is a word for the moon in general. If [one says that] in numerical usage the singularity of the moon is understood—[we reply:] somewhere in generic usage the singularity of blue lotuses and the like is also established. Therefore, in poetic usage, since multiplicity is conventionally applied even to the moon, the injunction-restatement relation based on that [multiplicity] would be better here.

body.translated_text: Thus, in the [verse beginning] '<s>viracaya sicayāntam</s>,' the word '<s>tat</s>' (that), which should be placed in the sense of a causal marker at the beginning of the third quarter, is placed [elsewhere]. And there it has no purpose. Having been placed [elsewhere], it produces obtuseness of comprehension. / In some cases, when the principal action has been referred to by a '<s>tat</s>'-initial pronoun, employing it again with its own word for a subsidiary action is indeed faulty. As in the [verse] '<s>pratyāsanne nabhasi</s>' — here, by the pronoun '<s>tasmai</s>,' the previously introduced cloud (<s>megha</s>) is referred to, or else the '<s>jīmūta</s>' (thunder-cloud) in this verse [is referred to]. In the first case, the mention of '<s>jīmūta</s>' is purposeless, since the previously introduced cloud, already referred to in the principal action, is itself suitable for the [new] semantic relation. For it is not the case that for as many [things] as have a relation with something, each one is separately specified. Having been specified once, [the reference] is relied upon elsewhere through expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) etc. Therefore the mention of '<s>jīmūta</s>' should not be made; having been made, it rather produces dissonance (<s>vairasya</s>) by generating the cognition of another thing. If, however, the '<s>jīmūta</s>' in this verse is referred to by the word '<s>tat</s>,' that is wrong. For throughout this context, the reference to the previously introduced cloud (<s>megha</s>) is well-established — hence here too such reference is proper, and again the mention of '<s>jīmūta</s>' is

"saṅkhyāpūrvo dviguḥ" (PS_2,1.52) iti vacanāt / pratiṣedhasyeti "nañ" (PS_2,2.6) iti nañsūtrārambhāt / dvitīya iti vyadhikaraṇaḥ / kārakāṇām iti "kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam" (PS_2,1.32) ityādinā / saṃbandhasyeti "ṣaṣṭhī" (PS_2.3.50) ityādinā / tatrāpīti kārakasaṃbandhayoge adhistri upakumbham ityādau / svāśrayo viśeṣyam / vidheyadhurām iti śabdavṛtte yo vidheyaḥ tasya kakṣyāṃ vāstavīṃ vidheyatām ity arthaḥ / anūdyamānakalpatayeti / śābdaṃ prādhānyam anapekṣya vāstavena prādhānyenety arthaḥ / astam iyād iti ekārthībhāvād vibhaktatvenāpratīter ity arthaḥ / ekatreti vidheyānuvādyagarbhatve / anyatreti saṃbandhamātrapratipādane / vikalyeteti
children.translated_text: '—<s>vrīhiḥ samānādhikaraṇānām</s>' — from this statement, <s>bahuvrīhi</s> generally applies in the domain of co-referential [terms] only. But in cases like <s>susūkṣmajaṭakeśa</s> ('fine-matted-hair') etc., it is also desired for non-co-referential terms. In that very [domain of] co-referential word-meanings: / 'When of a number' — from the statement '<s>saṅkhyāpūrvo dviguḥ</s>' (A number-prefixed [compound] is a <s>dvigu</s>) (PS 2.1.52). / 'Of negation' — from the beginning of the <s>nañ-sūtra</s> '<s>nañ</s>' (PS 2.2.6). / 'The second' — [is] non-co-referential. / 'Of case-relations (<s>kāraka</s>)' — from [the rule] '<s>kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam</s>' (Agent and instrument frequently [form compounds] with <s>kṛt</s>-suffixed [words]) (PS 2.1.32) etc. / 'Of relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>)' — from '<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>' (the sixth case [genitive]) (PS 2.3.50) etc. / 'Even there' — in the <s>kāraka</s>-relation domain, as in '<s>adhistri</s>,' '<s>upakumbham</s>,' etc. / 'Its own substratum' — the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>). / 'The burden of the predicate' (<s>vidheyādhura</s>) — the real predicativity (<s>vidheyatā</s>) of what is the predicate in verbal expression — this is the meaning. / 'As having the status of what is being restated' — disregarding verbal predominance, [it is] with real predominance — this is the meaning. / 'Would go to ruin' (<s>astam iyāt</s>) — because, due to becoming a single meaning (<s>ekārthībhāva</s>), there is no cognition of [the members] as separate — this is the meaning. / 'In one [case]' — when [the compound] contains both predicate and restatement. / 'In the other' — in the mere expression of a relation. / '<s>Vikalyeta</s>' —

children.text: mahāvibhāṣayā vyavasthitavibhāṣātvād iti bhāvaḥ / ekasyaiveti / viśeṣaṇagatasya prādhānyasya anyasya tadgatasyaivāprādhānyasya / ekasya hīti, aparasya punar iti ca / atra phalabheda ity atra prakrāntaṃ phalaṃ saṃbandhanīyam / atra codayati virodhasyobhayavastuniṣṭhatvāsiddher atrābhāva uktaḥ / tad asat / (tarhi?) na hi sahānavasthānalakṣaṇo vastugata eka eva virodha(ḥ?) bhedo, yaḥ śītoṣṇādau labdhavṛttiḥ / kiṃ tarhi parasparaparihārasthitatālakṣaṇo vastvavastutvāśrayo dvitīyo 'py asti virodhaprakāraḥ / tadā hi yadi vastvāśrayo na saṃbhavati virodho vastvavastutvāśrayas tu kathaṃ na syād / ataś ca syāt pūrvapakṣavelāyāṃ "bhāvābhāvayor eve"ty uktam / naiṣa doṣaḥ / vastvavastvāśrayasya virodhasya tādātmyaniṣedhe vyāpārāt / yadi nāma prādhānyaṃ, tasyām eva kakṣyāyāṃ svayam aprādhānyaṃ na syād, aprādhānye vā prādhānyam / prādhānyavidheye punar apekṣāntareṇāprādhānyaṃ kathaṃ na syāt / na syād, yadi śītoṣṇavad dvayor vastutvaṃ syāt / na cātraitad asti vaivakṣikasyāvastutvāt / yathā rājapuruṣa ity atra rājño vaivakṣikam eva prādhānyaṃ vāstavaṃ punar aprādhānyam eva tadvad atrāpi draṣṭavyam / tad ayam atra piṇḍārthaḥ saṃsarganiṣedho 'tra kartavyaḥ / sa ca vastudvayaniṣṭha iti dvayor atrābhāvān naikenāparatra pratiṣedha iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because it is an option with fixed conditions (<s>vyavasthitavibhāṣā</s>) by the great option (<s>mahāvibhāṣā</s>). / 'Of one alone' — the predominance (<s>prādhānya</s>) that belongs to the qualifier, the non-predominance of another that also belongs to that [qualifier]. / 'Of one' and 'of the other' [are explained] thus. / 'Here, the difference in result (<s>phalabheda</s>)' — the result that is under discussion here should be connected. / Here he raises an objection: the absence [of contradiction] has been stated here because contradiction's residing in both entities is unestablished. / That is wrong. / For it is not the case that there is only one type of contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) — that residing in real things, characterized by impossibility of co-existence, which obtains in cases like hot and cold. Rather, there is also a second type of contradiction, characterized by standing through mutual exclusion, which resides in [the distinction between] reality and non-reality (<s>vastu-avastu</s>). For if contradiction cannot reside in real things, how can it not reside in the [distinction between] reality and non-reality? Hence it was said at the stage of the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>): 'only between existence and non-existence.' This is no defect. Because the contradiction residing in reality-and-non-reality has its operation in the negation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). Even if there is predominance, in that very capacity non-predominance of itself would not obtain, or given non-predominance, predominance [would not obtain]. But how can there not be non-predominance, by another consideration, in what has predominance as predicate? There would not be, if — like hot and cold — both were real things. But that is not the case here, since what depends on the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) is non-real (<s>avastu</s>). Just as in '<s>rājapuruṣa</s>' (king's man), the predominance of 'king' is merely speaker-intended, while in reality it is only non-predominant — so here too it should be understood. Thus, the summary meaning here is: a negation of combination must be made here. And that [negation] resides in two real things; since both are absent here, by one [thing] the negation cannot be applied elsewhere.

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the second [type of] non-consideration of the predicate (<s>vidheyāvimarśa</s>), he begins to elaborate the third [type] in this very verse —

children.text: anyeneti viśeṣyābhidhāyinety arthaḥ / anyonyam iti / parasparaviśeṣaṇānāṃ yady api "viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa" (PS_2,1.57) iti viśeṣaṇasya viśeṣyeṇaiva samāsa uktaḥ, tathāpi "kāṇakhañjādiṣu siddhaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayor yatheṣṭatvād" iti vacanenaikasya viśeṣyatvavivakṣām āśritya parasparaṃ viśeṣaṇānāṃ samāsaḥ samarthitaḥ / tadabhiprāyeṇānyonyam iti saṃbhāvanā / dārasukha iti dārāṇāṃ sukheti tatpuruṣaḥ kartavyaḥ / bahuvrīhau "rājāhassakhibhyaḥ" (PS_5,4.91) iti ṭac na syāt / he hasteti / "mṛtasya śiśor dvijasya" ity atra samāsaḥ śaṅkitaḥ / "rāmasya pāṇir asi" iti tu ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa udāharaṇam / atra kva cit kartṝṇām karmaṇāṃ ca prathamāntānāṃ kvāpi saṃbandhināṃ karmaṇāṃ ca ṣaṣṭhyantānāṃ kutrāpy āmantraṇānāṃ samāsaḥ śaṅkitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By another' — meaning: by what denotes the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>). / 'Mutually' — Although for mutually qualifying [terms], the compound is stated [by the rule] '<s>viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa</s>' (PS 2.1.57) — the qualifier compounds with the qualified only — nevertheless, by the statement 'in <s>kāṇakhañja</s> etc. it is established, because there is freedom regarding qualifier and qualified,' relying on the intention to treat one as qualified, the compound of mutually qualifying [terms] is justified. With that intention, the suggestion 'mutually' (<s>anyonyam</s>). / '<s>Dārasukha</s>' — '<s>dārāṇāṃ sukha</s>' (the happiness of wives) — a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> should be formed. In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the <s>ṭac</s>-suffix by '<s>rājāhassakhibhyaḥ</s>' (PS 5.4.91) would not apply. / '<s>He haste</s>' (O hand!) — In '<s>mṛtasya śiśor dvijasya</s>,' a compound is suspected. But '<s>rāmasya pāṇir asi</s>' is an example of a genitive (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) compound. Here, in some cases compounds of nominative agents and objects, in others of genitive related-terms and objects, in yet others of vocatives, are suspected.

children.text: vakṣyamāṇanayeneti / "vyāsaḥ pārāśaryaḥ" ityādivicāreṣu / cāpācārya iti / atra hi tripuravijayitvādyanuvādena cāpācāryatvādividhiḥ / anūdyamānaś cārtho vidheyasyotkarṣam āvahan pratīyate / na caivam iti upendravajrasthāne indravajraprayogāt / upagatam asmābhir iti / "duḥśravatvam api vṛttasya śabdānaucityam eva / tasyāpy anuprāsāder ive"tyādivadadbhiḥ
children.translated_text: 'By the principle to be stated' — in discussions such as '<s>Vyāsa</s> is <s>Pārāśarya</s>' etc. / '<s>Cāpācārya</s>' (Archery-teacher) — For here, by the restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of having conquered <s>Tripura</s> etc., the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) of being an archery-teacher etc. [is made]. And the restated meaning, bringing excellence to the predicate, is understood. / 'But not thus' — because an <s>Indravajrā</s> [meter] is used in place of an <s>Upendravajrā</s>. / 'We have accepted' — by those who say 'Even the cacophony of meter is merely verbal impropriety (<s>śabdānaucitya</s>); and that [impropriety] is like alliteration (<s>anuprāsa</s>) etc.'

children.text: pūrvaṃ paṭhitaḥ sāmañjasyaṃ bhajate, pratyudāharaṇaṃ ceti udāharaṇagranthaḥ samañjasa eva syāt / dṛśyate ca pustakeṣv evaṃ pāṭhaḥ / tasmād atra jāgaraṇīyam / kāraṇam atra parāśāro jamadagniś ca / tadabhāve hetur iti tacchabdena samāsaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ / tataś cātra pārāśaryādipadaṃ vyāsādāv utkarṣam arpayat punar uktam / takṣakasarpa iti takṣakaśabdenaivātra sarpaviśeṣatvāt sarpatve pratīte sarpapadam utkarṣasamarpaṇapravaṇam eveti tadarthasya vidheyatvam /
children.translated_text: if read before [this], it achieves consistency, and the counter-example — thus the passage of examples would be proper. And in manuscripts, this reading is indeed seen. Therefore one should be vigilant here. / The 'reason' (<s>kāraṇa</s>) here is <s>Parāśara</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>. / In their absence, the reason — by the word '<s>tat</s>' the compound is referred to. And thus the word '<s>pārāśarya</s>' etc., granting eminence to <s>Vyāsa</s> etc., is said again. / '<s>Takṣakasarpa</s>' (<s>Takṣaka</s>-serpent) — Since by the word '<s>takṣaka</s>' alone, its being a particular type of serpent is understood, the word '<s>sarpa</s>' (serpent), being inclined to grant eminence, has its meaning as the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>).

children.text: lohitas takṣaka iti yathā takṣakaśabdād eva sarpatvajātiḥ pratītā tadval lohitalakṣa(ṇo gu)ṇo 'pi tata evāvyabhicārāt pratītaḥ / tatas tau jātiguṇau vidheyatābhiprāyeṇoktau na samāsa nyagbhāvanīyau / uktanyāyād iti vidheyatvān na samāsaḥ pravartata ity arthaḥ / pakṣo na cāsty anyas tadatyaye iti / iha dvau pakṣāv ullikhitau takṣakasya svarūpamātrapratipādanaṃ vā lohitākhyaguṇavidhir vā / ubhayatrāpi kṛtā carcā / tadatyaye ca kathitapakṣadvayātikrame cānyas tṛtīyapakṣo nāstīty arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Lohitas takṣaka</s>' (The red <s>Takṣaka</s>) — Just as from the word '<s>takṣaka</s>' alone, the species-universal (<s>jāti</s>) of serpent-hood is understood, similarly the quality (<s>guṇa</s>) characterized by redness (<s>lohita</s>) is also understood from that very [word] alone, since there is no deviation. Therefore those two — the species-universal and the quality — are stated with the intention of predicativity, not to be subordinated by compounding. / 'By the stated principle' — meaning: because of predicativity, compound-formation does not proceed. / 'There is no other alternative at its passing' — Here two alternatives have been sketched: mere denotation of the essential nature of <s>Takṣaka</s>, or the injunction of the quality called redness. In both [cases], discussion has been made. And 'at its passing' — when both stated alternatives are transgressed — there is no third alternative, that is the meaning.

body.text: evam iyatā karmadhārayaṃ vicārya bahuvrīhinirūpaṇāyāha bahuvrīhau yatheti / tatas tad iti sthalīkaraṇādi yad viśeṣaṇatayopāttaṃ tat parāmṛśyate / tair vidhyādibhiḥ / tadapratītiḥ utkarṣāpakarāpratītiḥ / pratītibhedahetau samāsāsamāsayoge / pratītisāmarthye karmadhārayādiviṣaye / tadasaṃbhavaḥ pratītibhedāsaṃbhavaḥ / antyāvasthā prāptakāraṇeṣu yuktaiva kāryotpattir ity arthaḥ / etadabhyupagame dṛṣṭavirodham āha / evaṃ hīti / naiva veti nyāyāviśeṣāt / ardhajaratīyam iti ardhaṃ jaratyā iti "samāsāc ca tadviṣayā" (PS_5,3.106) iti cchapratyayaḥ / yathā jaratyā varāṅgaṃ kāmayate mukhaṃ na kāmayate tadvad evety arthaḥ /

children.translated_text: "That of him" (<s>tat tasya</s>) —

children.text: ⟨tatāsya var (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant reading: <s>tatāsya</s> (editorial variant)]

children.text: iti tad iti tasmāt / tau sūryacandramasau / tayor iti anuvādyayos sūryācandramasoḥ / pāramparyeṇeti vidheyatām āha pitāmahatvadvāreṇa / ata eva sūryācandramasāv iti dvandvanirdeśo dvayoḥ spardhitāṃ prakāśayati / urvaśyā ca bhuvā ceti samāsābhāvo varaṇasya mukhyāmukhyatvapradarśanārtham ekasya vāstavatvād aparasya kaviprauḍhoktiniṣpāditatvāt / iha ceti pratītivaicitryaṃ spaṣṭataram eva dhārayatu matimān iti pāścātya sanbandhanāyaṃ janaka iti / atra janakākhyarājarṣiprabhṛtayaḥ pitṛtvāder utkarṣam arpayanti /
children.translated_text: "that" (<s>tat</s>) means "from that" (<s>tasmāt</s>). "Those two" (<s>tau</s>) refers to the sun and moon. "Of those two" (<s>tayoḥ</s>) means of the sun and moon as subjects of predication. "Indirectly" (<s>pāramparyeṇa</s>) states the predicate: through the medium of grandfather-hood. For this very reason, the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) designation "sun and moon" reveals the rivalry of both. "Of <s>Urvaśī</s> and the earth" — the absence of compounding is for the purpose of showing the primary and secondary nature of the choosing, since one is real while the other is produced by the poet's bold expression. "And here" — let the wise person recognize that the variety of apprehension is quite clear; "the one named <s>Janaka</s>" is the connecting link to what follows. Here, the royal sage named <s>Janaka</s> and others confer superiority through fatherhood and the like.

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound) to this extent, he states the analysis of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound): "In the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, as follows." From that — what has been taken up as a qualifier, such as contextualization (<s>sthalīkaraṇa</s>) etc., is referred back to. "By those" means by injunction and the like. "Non-apprehension of that" means non-apprehension of superiority or inferiority. "Regarding the cause of the difference in apprehension, in the application of compound and non-compound" — "regarding the capacity of apprehension, in the domain of <s>karmadhāraya</s> etc." — "the impossibility of that" means the impossibility of a difference in apprehension. "The final stage" means: when the causes are present, the production of the effect is indeed appropriate — this is the meaning. He states the contradiction with observation upon accepting this: "For thus" etc. "Or not at all" — because there is no distinction in principle. "Half-old-woman" (<s>ardhajaratīya</s>) — "half of the old woman" — the <s>cha</s>-suffix follows from the rule "and in a compound relating to that" (PS 5.3.106). Just as one desires the beautiful limb of the old woman but does not desire her face — similarly, this is the meaning.

body.text: evaṃ bahuvrīhiṃ vicārya dviguṃ vyācaṣṭe dvigau yatheti / niravaśeṣa iti saptatvasaṅkhyāyāṃ vidheyatvena saṃrambhāspadatvaṃ samāse tu nyagbhāvāt / daśasv iti daśatvasaṅkhyāyā vidheyatvaṃ rāvaṇasya paribhavātiśayaṃ prakāśayati ekasminn api mūrdhani padanyāsaḥ paribhavāspadaṃ kiṃ punar daśāsv iti / pratyudāharaṇaṃ saptāṅgyām iha yasya sa itītyādipāṭhe / vaiśasaṃ bādhaḥ / evaṃ dviguṃ vyākhyāya nañsamāsaṃ vyācaṣṭe nañsamāseti / upadarśitam iti asaṃrabdhavān ity atra vidheyāvimarśavicāre anuktavān iti noktavān iti vācyam / tatpuruṣe kartrādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ kārakāṇāṃ saṃbandhasya ca krameṇodāharaṇāny āha deśetyādinā / so 'yam iti / atra sa evāyam iti vyākhyā / ahitasaṃbandhināṃ śastrāṇāṃ ghasmarāṇi grasanaśīlāni ata eva gurūṇi / karaṇaṃ pratīti kriyāṃ pratīty arthaḥ / tat tasyeti prakrāntatya

children.text: ⟨read prakrāntasya⟩
children.translated_text: [read: <s>prakrāntasya</s> (of the one introduced)]

children.text: viśeṣyasya karaṇasya / tasyeti rāmasya / śauryaṃ balam / nighnaḥ paravaśaḥ / tena tad iti rāmeṇeti viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: of the instrument as qualificand. "Of him" (<s>tasya</s>) means of <s>Rāma</s>. <s>Śaurya</s> means strength. <s>Nighna</s> means subjugated. "By him, that" means: "by <s>Rāma</s>" is the qualifier.

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, he expounds the <s>dvigu</s> (numeral compound): "In the <s>dvigu</s>, as follows." "Without remainder" (<s>niravaśeṣa</s>) means: in the number seven, the predicatedness becomes the locus of intensity, but in the compound this is diminished. "In the ten" — the predicatedness of the number ten reveals the extreme humiliation of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: placing a foot even on one head is a source of humiliation, how much more on ten — this is the meaning. The counter-example is in the reading "in the seven-limbed [army], here, he whose that." <s>Vaiśasa</s> means affliction. Having thus explained the <s>dvigu</s>, he expounds the <s>nañ-samāsa</s> (negative compound): "the <s>nañ-samāsa</s>." "Has been shown" means: in "one who is without agitation" (<s>asaṃrabdhavān</s>), in the examination of predicate-reflection, "has not spoken" — one should say "has not spoken" (<s>noktavān</s>). He gives examples in order of the six <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) — agent etc. — and the genitive relation in the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> (determinative compound), beginning with "place" etc. "This very one" (<s>so 'yam</s>) — here the explanation is "he indeed is this one." "Of weapons connected with the enemy" — <s>ghasmarāṇi</s> means voracious, hence heavy. "Regarding the instrument" (<s>karaṇam prati</s>) means: regarding the action — this is the meaning. "That of him" (<s>tat tasya</s>) means: of the qualifier that has been introduced,

children.text: anekeṣām iti / anekaśabdasya nañsamāse uttarapadārthaprādhānyād ekavacanaprasaṅgaḥ / satyam kiṃ tu nañprayogaviṣaye ekaśabdasyaikavyatiriktavastuviṣayatvaṃ yathā abrāhmaṇa ity atra brāhmaṇaśabdasya kṣatriyādigocaratvam / ekavyatiriktaṃ ca vastu kadā cid ekatvoparaktaṃ pratīyate, kadā cin nijenaiva svarūpeṇa / ādye pakṣe anekam iti bhavati dvitīye tv anekānīti / yathā ca (padamañjariḥ?) patañjaliḥ -
children.translated_text: Regarding "of many" (<s>anekeṣām</s>) — since in the <s>nañ-samāsa</s> (negative compound), the meaning of the latter member predominates, the singular number would apply to the word <s>aneka</s> (not-one). True; however, in the domain of the <s>nañ</s>-usage, the word <s>eka</s> (one) refers to things other than one — just as in <s>abrāhmaṇa</s> (non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>), the word <s>brāhmaṇa</s> refers to <s>kṣatriyas</s> etc. And the thing other than one is sometimes apprehended as tinged with oneness, and sometimes in its own intrinsic form. In the first case, it becomes <s>anekam</s> (singular); in the second, <s>anekāni</s> (plural). And as <s>Patañjali</s> [says] —

children.text: [Page 27]
children.translated_text: [Page 27]

children.text: pravṛttibhede prayojakaṃ cittam ekam anekeṣām (4pā. 5 sū.) iti / gurudattam iti guruṇā dattam iti vācyam / tat tasyā iti sītāyā viśeṣaṇabhūtāyāḥ sītākartṛtkāyā gamanakriyāyā ity arthaḥ / gurvartham iti gurave idaṃ gurvartham iti kriyāviśeṣaṇam etat / kriyāviśeṣaṇānāṃ karmatvaṃ napuṃsakaliṅgatvaṃ ca / īpsitatamatve tu ṣaṣṭhī syāt / arthanakriyāmukheneti arthayata iti nigamanāt / tat tasyeti tad gurvartham iti viśeṣaṇam / tasyārthinaḥ / avamatatām anabhipretatām / avamatatvaṃ garhitatvam / sutanirviśeṣam iti / kriyāviśeṣaṇam eva / pradakṣiṇakriyety atra pradakṣiṇakriyāyā atyayakriyākarmabhūtāyā antarāyahetukopanimittatvāt prādhānyam / evaṃ prathamaprabodhita iti prāthamyasya / tathā yathākāmatvayathākālatvayor jñeyam / yadavalokaneti rūpasampat parāmṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: "The mind is one, the motivator in the diversity of activities, of many" (Pā. 4, Sū. 5). Regarding "given by the teacher" (<s>gurudattam</s>) — one should say "given by the teacher" (<s>guruṇā dattam</s>). "That of her" (<s>tat tasyāḥ</s>) means: of <s>Sītā</s> who is the qualifier, meaning the action of going in which <s>Sītā</s> is the agent — this is the meaning. "For the teacher's purpose" (<s>gurvartham</s>) means: "this is for the teacher" — <s>gurvartham</s> is a qualifier of the action. Action-qualifiers take the accusative case and neuter gender. But if it is the most desired [goal], the genitive would apply. "Through the act of requesting" (<s>arthanakriyāmukhena</s>) — because the derivation is "one who requests" (<s>arthayate</s>). "That of him" (<s>tat tasya</s>) — "that" is the qualifier <s>gurvartham</s>; "of him" means of the supplicant. <s>Avamatatā</s> means undesiredness. <s>Avamatatva</s> means being despised. "Without distinction from a son" (<s>sutanirviśeṣam</s>) — this too is an action-qualifier. Regarding "the act of circumambulation" (<s>pradakṣiṇakriyā</s>) — here, since the act of circumambulation, being the object of the act of passing, is the incidental cause functioning as an intervening reason, it has predominance. Similarly, regarding "first awakened" (<s>prathamaprobodhita</s>), [the predominance] of firstness. Likewise for "at-will-ness" and "at-time-ness," this should be understood. "By the sight of which" (<s>yadavalokana</s>) — beauty of form is referred to.

children.text: svahasteneti karaṇapadam / svahastalikhitānīti svahastaśabdo 'trādarapratītihetukatvena lekhanaṃ praty utkarṣanimittam api samāse guṇīkṛtaḥ / pūrvavad iti kṛtasamāsavaiśasam / tac ca vipradattam iti pāṭhe / pitāmahapitāmatayeti pitāmaho brahmā pitāmahaḥ pūrvapuruṣo yasya / tayor janmanidhanayoḥ / tadvato janmanidhanavataḥ / tābhyāṃ janmanidhanābhyām / kṛtāntādhikam iti āsamudrāt
children.translated_text: "With one's own hand" (<s>svahastena</s>) is an instrumental word. "Written by one's own hand" (<s>svahastalikhitāni</s>) — here the word <s>svahasta</s> (own hand), being the cause of the apprehension of care, is the ground for superiority with respect to writing, yet in the compound it is subordinated. "As before" (<s>pūrvavat</s>) means: with the affliction of the compound as already described. "And that" is in the reading <s>vipradattam</s> (given by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>). "Grandfather-fatherhood" (<s>pitāmahapitāmata</s>) — <s>pitāmaha</s> means <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>pitāmaha</s> also means the ancestor of one. "Of those two" — of birth and death. "Of the one possessing that" — of the one possessing birth and death. "By those two" — by birth and death. "Beyond the god of death" (<s>kṛtāntādhikam</s>) — and one should say "up to the ocean,

children.text: ⟨kṭāntād adhikam āsamudrāt conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>kṛtāntād adhikam āsamudrāt</s> (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: kṣitīśānām iti ca vācyam / apādānasamānanyāyatvād avadhir api pañcamyanto 'tra gṛhyata iti pratyudāharaṇopapattiḥ / upāga(te?)meti upāgatā iti nirdiṣṭā upāgamakriyā /
children.translated_text: of the lords of the earth." Since the limit (<s>avadhi</s>) follows the same principle as the ablative, the word in the fifth case is also taken here — thus the counter-example is justified. "Has come" (<s>upāgama</s>) — the action of coming is specified as <s>upāgatā</s> (arrived).

children.text: raṇabhūṣita iti / atra raṇabhuvīti vācyam / śocanīyatāgatiḥ kriyā / tatra samāgamaprārthanā hetutvenopāttā / tasyāḥ saṃbandhidvāreṇa saṃbandhitvamukhena kapālina iti viśeṣaṇam / atra saṃbandhiśabdo bhāvavṛttiḥ saṃbandhitve varttate, yathā "dvyekayor dvivacanaikavacane" (PS_1.4.22) iti, sudhīram uvāceti / tat tasyā iti / tad viśeṣaṇam / tasyās samāgamaprārthanāyāḥ / tatra śocanīyatāgatau / sāmarthyam avyabhicāreṇa sampādakatvam / tasya sakaleti tacchabdaḥ kapālina ity asya parāmarśakaḥ / viśeṣyeṇa samāgamaprārthanayety anena / pratyavaraṃ guṇabhūtam / evaṃ tātasyeti, āryasyeti, skandasyeti, taveti cety eṣāṃ viśeṇaṇānām utkarṣasamarpakatvaṃ jñeyam / tasyaiveti
children.translated_text: Regarding "adorned by battle" (<s>raṇabhūṣita</s>) — here one should say "on the battlefield" (<s>raṇabhuvi</s>). "The state of being pitiable" (<s>śocanīyatāgatiḥ</s>) is the action. There, the entreaty for union is taken as the cause. Of that [entreaty], through the medium of its possessor, in the sense of being a possessor — "of <s>Kapālin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)" is the qualifier. Here the word <s>saṃbandhin</s> (possessor) functions in the abstract sense, denoting the state of being related — as in "the dual and singular for two and one" (PS 1.4.22), and in "he said to <s>Sudhīra</s>." "That of her" (<s>tat tasyāḥ</s>) — "that" is the qualifier; "of her" means of the entreaty for union. "There, regarding the state of pitiableness" — "capacity" (<s>sāmarthya</s>) means the ability to produce without deviation. "Its complete" (<s>tasya sakala</s>) — the <s>tat</s>-word refers back to "of <s>Kapālin</s>." "By the qualificand" — by the entreaty for union, this refers to what is subordinate. Thus, one should understand that the qualifiers "of the father" (<s>tātasya</s>), "of the noble one" (<s>āryasya</s>), "of <s>Skanda</s>" (<s>skandasya</s>), and "of you" (<s>tava</s>) confer superiority. "Of that very one" (<s>tasyaiva</s>) —

children.text: ⟨tasyeti var (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant reading: <s>tasya</s> (editorial variant)]

children.text: gauravadurāropatvanibandhanasya harasya / tacceti prādhānyam / tasyeti harasya / kalpitārthasyeti vistāritakṛtrimatvamātravācino 'dhijyatvamātralakṣaṇārthāropāt / aprayuktasyeti uktanayenāsminn arthe kavibhir aprayujyamānasya / guṇāntaralābha iti vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇasya vācyāvacanasya parihārāt / (atreti?)
children.translated_text: of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), on account of the difficulty of attributing gravity [to him]. "That" (<s>tat</s>) signifies predominance. "Of him" (<s>tasya</s>) means of <s>Hara</s>. "Of imagined meaning" (<s>kalpitārthasya</s>) means: of that which merely expresses extended artificiality, through the attribution of meaning characterized merely by having the bowstring drawn. "Of what is not used" (<s>aprayuktasya</s>) — of what is not employed by poets in this meaning, according to the principle stated. "Attainment of another quality" (<s>guṇāntaralābha</s>) — through the avoidance of the characteristic of expressibility and non-expressibility that will be described. "Here" (<s>atra</s>) —

children.text: ⟨mātreti conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>mātra</s> (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: evaṃ kṛtam ity atra karaṇam /
children.translated_text: "thus done" (<s>evaṃ kṛtam</s>) — here the instrument (<s>karaṇam</s>).

children.text: niṣka ābharaṇaviśeṣaḥ / vibhaktyanvayeti śrūyamāṇāyā vibhakter ity arthaḥ / tathā ca "ṣaṣṭhyā ākrośe" (PS_6.3.21) iti jñāpakam (rūpakam upadeśa iṣyata iti?) pramāṇāntareṇa "loko vedas tathādhyātmaṃ pramāṇaṃ trividham" ity uktarūpeṇa siddhau yau svasya viśeṣaṇasyotkarṣāpakarṣau tadādhāyinām arthād viśeṣyaṃ pratīty arthaḥ / ārthaṃ vāstavam / alukam āha "ṣaṣṭhyā ākrośe" (PS_6.3.21) ity anena / cintyam iti / etadavagamāya vicāryam ity arthaḥ / samāse ca vibhaktilopād iti / iha hi vibhaktiśravaṇāśravaṇe (vā?) anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ viśeṣaṇagatayor vāstavayoḥ prayojakatāṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Niṣka</s> is a particular ornament. "By the construal of the case-ending" (<s>vibhaktyanvaya</s>) means: of the case-ending that is heard — this is the meaning. And thus, the rule "the sixth case in abuse" (PS 6.3.21) is an indicator. (It is desired that the figurative usage be [regarded as] an instruction.) By another means of valid knowledge — in the form stated as "the world, the <s>Veda</s>, and the self-knowledge are the threefold means of valid knowledge" — when the superiority and inferiority of one's own qualifier are established, it necessarily conveys [meaning] toward the qualificand — this is the meaning. "Real" (<s>ārtha</s>) means actual. He states the non-elision (<s>aluk</s>) by the rule "the sixth case in abuse" (PS 6.3.21). "To be considered" (<s>cintya</s>) means: to be examined for the understanding of this — this is the meaning. "And because in the compound the case-ending is dropped" — for here, by the positive and negative concomitance of hearing and not hearing the case-ending, the actualities of the qualifier share

children.text: ⟨praśabdāt prāk "prādhānyaguṇabhāvayoḥ prayojakatāṃ" iti pūraṇam apekṣitaṃ bhāti⟩
children.translated_text: [The editor notes: before <s>pra</s>, the completion 'the causative capacity of predominance and subordination' seems required]

children.text: bhajete / te tu prāyeṇa vākyasamāsagatatvenopalabhyamāne samāsasya vibhaktyaśravaṇād vidheyāvimarśatām utpādayataḥ / ata eva samāse 'pi yadi vibhaktiḥ śrūyate, tadā na vidhe
children.translated_text: the causative capacity. But those, being mostly apprehended as belonging to the sentence and the compound domain, produce predicate-non-reflection due to the non-hearing of the case-ending in the compound. For this very reason, even in a compound, if the case-ending is heard, then there is no predicate-

children.text: [Page 28]
children.translated_text: [Page 28]

children.text: yāvimarśo yathā dāsyāḥ kāmuka ityādau / samāsas tu tatraikapadyādiprayojanatvena kṛtaḥ / tannibandhaneti utkarṣāpakarṣanibandhanā / evaṃ ca vibhaktyaśravaṇānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitvaṃ vidheyāvimarśasya vyāptyā pradarśitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: non-reflection, as in "the lover of the slave-girl" (<s>dāsyāḥ kāmuka</s>) etc. But the compound there is formed for the purpose of single-word-hood etc. "Based on that" (<s>tannibandhanā</s>) means: based on superiority and inferiority. And thus, the fact that predicate-non-reflection follows the positive and negative concomitance of the non-hearing of the case-ending has been demonstrated through pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>).

body.text: evaṃ ca saptaprakāraṃ tatpuruṣaṃ nirūpyāvyayībhāvaṃ nirūpayati - avyayībhāva iti / samāpaṃ viśeṣyaṃ prati dayitasyeti yad viśeṣaṇaṃ tat tasya samīpasyeti yojanā / madhyevyometi "pāre madhye ṣaṣṭhyā vā" (PS_2,1.18) ity avyayībhāvaḥ / sa ceti prakarṣaḥ / evam iyatā dvandvavarjaṃ samāsavṛttir vicāritā / idānīm atideśamukhena kṛttaddhitavṛttir nirūpyate anenaivetyādinā / vivakṣāviśeṣād ity akārapraśleṣaḥ /

children.translated_text: [Section 52]

children.text: sarvaṃ kaṣatīti "sarvakūlābhrakarīreṣu kaṣaḥ" (PS_3,2.42) iti khaco 'yaṃ viṣayaḥ / bibhartti yaḥ iti "kukṣiṃbhariś ca" iti nipātitasya kukṣimbhariśabdasyāyaṃ gocaraḥ / vidhun tud iti "vidhvaruṣos tud" (PS_3,2.35) iti khaśpratyayasthānam / śīrṣacchedam iti "śīrṣacchedād yac ca" (PS_5,1.65) iti taddhitasya yat pratyayasyedaṃ padam / tair iti kaṣaṇādibhiḥ / sarvārthasyeti, kāyopalakṣaṇasya kukṣer iti, vidhoś ceti (vyakta sthitaḥ ?) utkarṣam ādadhatāṃ prādhānyena vivakṣety atra sāmastyena yojanīyam / śīrṣacchedasya ceti utkarṣam ādadhataḥ prādhānyena vivakṣeti saṃbandhanīyam / pūrvebhyo 'sya pṛthaṅnirdeśas taddhitavṛttiviṣayatvena bhinnajātīyatvāt / atra ca sarvārthādīnāṃ caturṇām utkarṣādhāne samanantaranirdiṣṭa bhuvanābhayetyādicatuṣṭayaṃ krameṇa hetutvena draṣṭavyam / tad apīti caritam / kaṣaṇādikartṛṣv iti khalaudarikarāhuṣv ity arthaḥ / rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ saha iti / "pūssarvayor dārisahoḥ" (PS_3,2.41) iti khaco 'yaṃ viṣayaḥ / daśarathasya hi prasūtir asāv iti ("tasyāpatyam" iti stracpratyaye)
children.translated_text: 'Scratches everything' (<s>sarvaṃ kaṣati</s>) — this is the domain of the <s>khac</s> [suffix] by the rule '<s>sarvakūlābhrakarīreṣu kaṣaḥ</s>' (PS 3.2.42). 'He who bears' (<s>bibharti yaḥ</s>) — this is the domain of the irregularly formed word <s>kukṣimbhari</s> [by the rule] '<s>kukṣiṃbhariś ca</s>.' '<s>Vidhun tud</s>' (striking the moon) — this is the place of the <s>khaś</s> suffix by the rule '<s>vidhvaruṣos tud</s>' (PS 3.2.35). '<s>Śīrṣaccheda</s>' (head-cutting) — this is the domain of the <s>yat</s> suffix, a <s>taddhita</s>, by the rule '<s>śīrṣacchedād yac ca</s>' (PS 5.1.65). 'By those' — by scratching etc. 'Of the whole purpose' — of the belly, which is a metonymy for the body — and of the moon — [these are] being intended principally as conveying excellence; this should be construed together here. 'And of head-cutting' — should be connected as conveying excellence principally being intended. The separate mention of this from the preceding [examples] is because it belongs to a different class, being in the domain of <s>taddhita</s> formation. And here, in the conveyance of excellence for the four [terms] — 'the whole purpose' etc. — the four [examples] just stated, '<s>bhuvanābhaya</s>' etc., should be seen as the respective causes in order. 'That too' — [refers to] the behavior [described]. 'Among the agents of scratching etc.' — the meaning is: among <s>Khala</s>, <s>Udarika</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, etc. 'I am <s>Rāma</s>, enduring all' — this is the domain of the <s>khac</s> [suffix] by the rule '<s>pūssarvayor dārisahoḥ</s>' (PS 3.2.41). For he is the offspring of <s>Daśaratha</s>, so [by applying the rule 'his offspring']

children.text: taddhite kṛte dāśarathiśabdasyāyaṃ gocaraḥ / vākye tu yady apīti tad uktam - "kriyāpradhānaṃ guṇavad ekārthaṃ vākyam iṣyate" iti / anya iti vakṣyamānanyāyena śabdakṛtasāmarthyoktiḥ / sa iti pradhānabhāvenety atra nirdiṣṭaḥ pradhānabhāvaḥ śabdārthasāmarthyavivakṣākṛtānāṃ trayāṇām apīti śabdakṛtaṃ śabdasaṃskāramahimnā niṣpannaṃ yathā karmadhārayād uttarapadasya / arthasāmarthyakṛtaṃ vastuvṛttaniṣpāditaṃ yathā "grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭī"tyādau grahādeḥ / tasya saṃskāryatvena vastutaḥ prādhānyam / vivakṣākṛtaṃ prayoktṛyadṛcchāpratipāditaṃ yad anyasyotkarṣāpakarṣādhānatayā vivakṣitaṃ yathā "rāmasya pāṇir asi" ityādau rāmādeḥ / tatra triṣu prādhānyeṣu vivakṣākṛtam eva grādhānyaṃ
children.translated_text: when the <s>taddhita</s> is applied, this is the domain of the word <s>Dāśarathi</s>. But in the sentence, 'even if' — that has been stated: 'A sentence is considered to be action-predominant, possessing attributes, and having a single meaning.' 'Another' — by the principle to be stated, this is a statement of capacity created by word-[formation]. '<s>Sa</s>' — the predominant status stated here as 'in the principal mode' [applies to] all three — created by word, by the capacity of meaning, and by intention. 'Created by word' (<s>śabdakṛta</s>) means produced by the power of grammatical formation, as the latter member [has primacy] from a <s>karmadhāraya</s> [compound]. 'Created by the capacity of meaning' (<s>arthasāmarthyakṛta</s>) means accomplished by the nature of things, as in '<s>grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes the vessel) etc., where the vessel [is primary] because it is the thing to be acted upon — its primacy is factual. 'Created by intention' (<s>vivakṣākṛta</s>) means established by the speaker's free will — that which is intended as conveying the excellence or inferiority of another, as in '<s>rāmasya pāṇir asi</s>' (you are <s>Rāma</s>'s hand) etc., where <s>Rāma</s> etc. [is primary]. Of these three types of primacy, it is the primacy created by intention that is

children.text: / tatkṛtatvāt kāvyārthacamatkārasya / ata evoktaṃ tayoḥ samaśīrṣikābhāvād iti / tayor iti śabdārthasāmarthyakṛtayoḥ vivakṣākṛtena sahety arthāt / nanu pūrvaṃ śābdasyaiva prādhānyasya vaivakṣikatvam uktam anyasya tu vāstavatvam / tat katham iha śābdavaivakṣikayor anyatvam ucyate / anyatve vā prādhānyatrayapratipādane 'rthasāmarthyakṛtavivakṣākṭayoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ / śabdakṛtād dhi prādhānyād anyadarthasāmarathyakṛtam ucyate / tena vivakṣākṛtasya uktatvāt / tat kim arthasāmarthyakṛtam avaśiṣyata iti / naiṣa doṣaḥ / pūrvaṃ hi śābdikaikagocarasya śābdikavivakṣākṛtatvād vaivakṣikatvam / anyasya tu kavigocarasya vāstavatvaṃ tad evārthatvam / iha punaḥ sahṛdayaikagocarasya kavivivakṣāvaśād vaivakṣikatvam ucyate / śābdikaikaviṣayasya śābdatvam ity apekṣābhedāt pūrvas tāvan na virodhaḥ / yad api prādhānyatrayapratipādane 'rthasāmarthyavivakṣākṛtayor bheda uktas tatrāyaṃ bhāvaḥ - iha śābdaṃ vāstavaṃ ceti dvividham eva prādhānyam / vāstavatvasya ca vivakṣānapekṣatvena vastusāmarthyaprayojaka+++darthasā
children.translated_text: because the poetic charm (<s>camatkāra</s>) of the literary meaning is created by that. Therefore it has been said: 'Because there is no equality of standing between those two.' 'Of those two' — of those created by word and by the capacity of meaning — with the one created by intention, this is the implicit meaning. Now, earlier, only the verbal type of primacy was stated to be a matter of intention (<s>vaivakṣika</s>), while the other [type was said to be] factual. So how can the verbal and the intentional be said to be different here? Or, if they are different, what is the distinction between that created by the capacity of meaning and that created by intention in the exposition of the three types of primacy? For what is created by the capacity of meaning is said to be different from primacy created by word; while the intention-created was already stated. So does the meaning-capacity-created remain? There is no fault. For earlier, what pertains solely to the domain of grammarians — because it is created by the grammarians' intention — was called intentional. But the other, pertaining to the poet's domain, was called factual — that itself is 'semantic.' Here, however, what pertains solely to the domain of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), by force of the poet's intention, is called intentional; while what pertains solely to grammarians' domain is called verbal — because there is a difference in the basis, there is first no contradiction.

children.text: marthyakṛtatvam uktam / saty api śabdakṛtād anyatva utkarṣāpakarṣapratipādanaprayuktakavivivakṣākṛtatve vāstavam eva vivakṣākṛta pratipāditam / tathā ca "grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭī"ti vaidikaṃ vivakṣānapekṣam arthasāmarthyakṛtasyodāharaṇaṃ dattam iti viṣayavibhāgavyavasthiter na dvitīyo 'pi virodha iti samañjasaṃ sarvam / evaṃ kṛttaddhitavṛttiviṣaye ātideśikaṃ guṇapradhānabhāvaṃ vicārya samā(sa)gatatvenaupadeśikaṃ prakṛtam anusandhatte tad idam atreti / sarūpāṇām iti dvandvasamāsasamānanyāyatvād ekaśeṣavṛttir api svīkṛtā / viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvābhāve 'pīti samāsoṭṭaṅkanikāyāṃ prāyagrahaṇaprayojanaṃ prakāśayati / rūpaṃ ca kāntiś ca vidagdhatā ceti, amṛtena viṣeṇeti cābhihitānābhihitakartṛvibhāgenodāharaṇadvayam / rūpam ityādau hi gamyamānabhavanakriyāpekṣaṃ rūpādīnāṃ kartṛtvam / etena tatpuruṣasya kartrudāharaṇaprastāve kartrādīnāṃ (kārakāṇām) aneke(ṣām i)ti yad uktaṃ, tat samīhitam.
children.translated_text: Even though there is otherness from word-created [primacy], when [primacy is] created by the poet's intention in order to convey excellence or inferiority, the factual itself has been established as intention-created. And so, '<s>grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes the vessel), a Vedic [example] independent of intention, has been given as an illustration of meaning-capacity-created [primacy] — thus, by the arrangement of distinct domains, there is no second contradiction either, and everything is consistent. Having thus examined the principal-subordinate status by extension in the domain of <s>kṛt</s> and <s>taddhita</s> formation, he reconnects with the instructional principal-subordinate status as originally given in the context of compounds — 'this is here.' 'Of identical forms' — since the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single remainder) formation is governed by the same principle as the <s>dvandva</s> compound, it too is accepted. 'Even in the absence of a qualifier-qualified relationship' — he reveals the purpose of the word '<s>prāya</s>' (generally) in the collection of compound rules. '<s>Rūpaṃ ca kāntiś ca vidagdhatā ca</s>' (beauty and grace and refinement) and '<s>amṛtena viṣeṇa</s>' (with nectar and with poison) — these are two examples with the distinction of expressed and unexpressed agent. In '<s>rūpam</s>' etc., the agenthood of beauty etc. is dependent on the understood action of 'being.' By this, what was said about agents etc. — 'many of the <s>kārakas</s>' — in the context of illustrating the agent in <s>tatpuruṣa</s>, is settled.
[Section 53]

children.text: kaś ca kaś ceti / atraikaśeṣo na kṛtaḥ / kṛtaikaśeṣam iti kāv iti prayoge / adhunā pradhānetarabhāvāpattiṃ darśayati yatra punar iti / bhavata iti ripustrīṇāṃ saṃbandhitvena, ripustrīṇām iti stanayugasya saṃbandhitveneti yojanā / ripustrīṇām iti samāsasyodāharaṇam / na cātra saṃbandhamātrād atiriktaṃ pratīyate / tadartham eveti upamotprekṣādayo 'py alaṅkārāḥ upamotprekṣādīnām utkarṣam apakarṣaṃ vā pratipādayituṃ vidhīyante / anyathā tadviracanaṃ niṣprayojanaṃ syāt / tau vidheyeti / utkarṣāpakarṣau / (samāsa iti ?) sā samāsa iti vivakṣā parāmṛśyate / vaidarbhīti yady api vāmanamate asamāsā pāñcālī, madhyamasamāsā tu vaidarbhī, tathāpi matāntare viparyayaḥ sthita iti tadabhiprāyeṇehāsamāsā vaidarbhī kathitā / kārikāmadhya eva saṃbandhamātrapratītau samāsasyodāharaṇam / "ūrdhvākṣitāpe"ti / atra caturthapādaikaśeṣa?(deśa)yuktasya pādatrayasya samāse saṃbandhamātraṃ pratīyate, notkarṣāpakarṣau / vākyāt tūbhayam iti ubhayaṃ saṃbandharūpam utkarṣāpakarṣarūpaṃ ca vastv ity arthaḥ / atrodāharaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaś ca kaś ca</s>' (someone and someone) — here the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> is not applied. 'When the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> is applied' — in the expression '<s>kāv</s>' (which two). Now he shows the arising of the principal-subordinate relationship — 'where again.' '<s>Bhavataḥ</s>' (yours) — should be construed as the relationship of the enemy's women, and '<s>ripustrīṇām</s>' (of the enemy's women) as the relationship of the pair of breasts. '<s>Ripustrīṇām</s>' is an example of a compound. And here, from the mere relationship, nothing beyond is cognized. 'For that purpose alone' — figures of speech such as <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), etc. are also employed to convey the excellence or inferiority of <s>upamā</s>, <s>utprekṣā</s>, etc. Otherwise, their composition would be purposeless. 'Those two are to be predicated' — excellence and inferiority. 'Compound' — that intention [regarding] 'it is a compound' is being considered. '<s>Vaidarbhī</s>' — although in <s>Vāmana</s>'s view, the <s>Pāñcālī</s> [style] has no compounds and the <s>Vaidarbhī</s> has moderate compounds, nevertheless in another view the reverse is established, and so, with that intent, the compoundless [style] has been called <s>Vaidarbhī</s> here. In the middle of the verse itself, '<s>ūrdhvākṣitāpe</s>' is an example of a compound where only mere relationship is cognized. In the compound of the three <s>pādas</s> joined with the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> in the fourth <s>pāda</s>, only mere relationship is cognized, not excellence or inferiority. 'But from the sentence, both' — 'both' means the reality of the relationship-form and the excellence-or-inferiority-form — such is the meaning. Here the example is:
[Section 54]

children.text: me yadaraya iti samāse hi madaraya iti syāt / na cāsmād atiśayaḥ pratītaḥ / nanu padād uttarapadayor yuṣmadasmadoḥ "temayāv ekavacanasya" (PS_8,9.22) iti temayāv ādeśāv uktau / na cātra padāt paro 'smacchabdaḥ / evaśabdaḥ padam iti cen na / tatprayoge "nacavāhāhaivayukte"(PS_8,1.24) iti niṣedhād bhinnavākyagatatvāc ca / samānavākye hi nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśāḥ / (etenaiva vyatiriktaṃ padāntaraṃ pratyuktam / utkarṣamātram eva śabdādeśaḥ?) atra ke cid āhuḥ vākye tāvad rasapratītir nirvyūḍhā / tām anupamaradayan kāvye yady asādhuśabdo 'pi syān na tadā sthūlaḥ kaś cid doṣaḥ / kāvye hi rasapratītiḥ pradhānam / tadanirvāhe kāvyam eva na syāt / apaśabdaprayoge tu lakṣaṇāsmaraṇamātram / tad uktaṃ -
children.translated_text: '<s>me yadaraya</s>' — for in the compound, it would be '<s>madaraya</s>.' And from this, no excellence is cognized. Now, in the rules, for the latter members '<s>yuṣmad</s>' (you) and '<s>asmad</s>' (I), '<s>temayāv ekavacanasya</s>' (PS 8.9.22) states the substitutions '<s>te</s>' and '<s>me</s>' [for the singular]. But here, the '<s>asmad</s>'-word is not after a word-boundary (<s>pada</s>). If one says '<s>eva</s>' is a <s>pada</s> — no, because the rule '<s>nacavāhāhaivayukte</s>' (PS 8.1.24) prohibits it, and because it belongs to a different sentence. For accent and '<s>yuṣmad</s>/<s>asmad</s>' substitutions [apply only] within the same sentence. Here some say: in the sentence, the cognition of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion) has already been accomplished. Without disrupting that, if even an incorrect word occurs in poetry, there is no gross fault. For in poetry, the cognition of <s>rasa</s> is primary. Without its accomplishment, there would be no poetry at all. But in the use of an incorrect word, there is merely a failure to recall grammatical rules. It has been said —

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the seven types of <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compound], he examines the <s>avyayībhāva</s> [compound] — '<s>avyayībhāva</s>.' The qualifier 'of the beloved' with respect to 'proximity,' which is the qualified term, should be construed as 'of that proximity.' '<s>Madhyevyoma</s>' (in the midst of the sky) — this is an <s>avyayībhāva</s> by the rule '<s>pāre madhye ṣaṣṭhyā vā</s>' (PS 2.1.18). 'And that' indicates excellence. Thus far, compound formation (<s>samāsavṛtti</s>) has been examined to this extent, excluding the <s>dvandva</s>. Now, by way of extension (<s>atideśa</s>), the formation of <s>kṛt</s> and <s>taddhita</s> [derivatives] is examined, beginning with 'by this very' etc. 'By a particular intention' (<s>vivakṣāviśeṣāt</s>) — the <s>a</s>-vowel [functions as] a coalescence (<s>praśleṣa</s>).

children.text: "nīrasas tu prabandho yaḥ so 'paśabdo mahān kaveḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A composition that is devoid of <s>rasa</s> — that is the great incorrect word of a poet;'

children.text: sa tenākavir eva syād anyenāsmṛtalakṣaṇaḥ //"
children.translated_text: 'By that, he would indeed be a non-poet; by the other [fault], merely one who has forgotten grammatical rules.'

children.text: kākuḥ kākvadhyāyalakṣito (Nā.Śā. 17) dhvanivikārarūpo vā / vācikābhinayo vāgvikārarūpo 'nubhāvaḥ / ardhāntāvadhir iti ślokāpekṣayā ardham antāvadhiḥ / nyūneti padyāpekṣayā nyūnaṃ rasābhivyaktihetutvam ity arthaḥ / yathā pūrvokta

Vocal acting (<s>vācikābhinaya</s>) is a <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) in the form of voice-modification. 'Half as the limit' means, with reference to a verse, that half [a verse] is the upper limit. 'Less' means, with reference to a stanza, that less [than half] serves as the cause for the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> — this is the meaning. As stated earlier —

children.text: tadā tasya samāsasya madhye vicchedo na kārya ity arthaḥ / avyabhicārād iti vidheyatvaṃ hi prādhānyāvinābhāvaḥ / sneham iti / atra pānādīnām prakāśanasya ca (vidhyanuvādalopitvaikakartṛkāṇāṃ prādhānyabhāvo nāpasmṛtam?) atra ca yo 'yam iti yacchabdena dīpasya padārthasya parāmarśopakrame tattamasa iti tacchabdena vākyārthasya parāmarśo duṣṭa ity upapāditaṃ prāk / śaktiḥ sāmarthyam āyudhabhedaś ca / tārakāḥ jyotīṃṣi daityaviśeṣaś ca tārakaḥ / adho nistejastvena vāhanatvena ca / śikhīvahnir
children.translated_text: then no break should be made in the middle of that compound — this is the meaning. 'Because of invariable concomitance' — for predicatedness (<s>vidheyatva</s>) is the inseparable concomitant of predominance. Regarding '<s>sneha</s>' (affection/oil): here, of drinking and the like, and of illumination — [the question of whether] the predominance-status of those having a single agent with injunctive and descriptive [functions] has [not] been forgotten. And here, the <s>yat</s>-pronoun in '<s>yo 'yam</s>' (this which) begins the reference to the word-meaning of the lamp, while the <s>tat</s>-pronoun in '<s>tattamasi</s>' (that, in the darkness) refers to the sentence-meaning — this has been previously established as faulty. '<s>Śakti</s>' means power and also a type of weapon. '<s>Tārakāḥ</s>' means stars and also a specific class of demons (<s>Tāraka</s>). 'Below' — in the sense of being without radiance and in the sense of being a vehicle. '<s>Śikhī</s>' means fire
