children.text: mayūraś ca / candrasya suvarṇasya saṃbandhī kāntāvabhāso lasan dedīpyamāno yasmin / candrakāṇāṃ mecakānām avabhāso lasanaṃ sphurad yasya / andhakāre tamasi andhakārer harasya / guhaḥ kumāraḥ / apara iveti atrāparaśabdasāmarthyād bhūpe dvitīyaguhatvapratītau vastutas tadasaṃbhave tatsaṃbhāvanāyām utprekṣā / aparaśabdābhāve tu svasvarūpasthitasyaiva vāstavasya guhasya pratītāv iyam upamā syāt / evam "apara iva pākaśāsano", "maurvīṃ dvitīyām" ityādau ca mantavyam / aharpater iti / "aharādīnāṃ patyādiṣu" iti vacanād rephaḥ / atra dhāraṇādīnāṃ guṇabhāvaḥ / ādhārasya tu prādhānyam / karttā hi guṇakriyā niṣpādayan pradhānakriyām aidamparyeṇa niṣpādayati, na tu tāsv aidamparyam / yatra sarvāsv aidamparyaṃ tatra bhavaty eva sarvāsām ākhyātavācyatvam / yathā
children.translated_text: and also a peacock. '[The compound] in which the beautiful radiance related to gold (<s>candra</s>) shines' — [means that] in which the appearance (<s>avabhāsa</s>) of golden beauty gleams. '[The compound] in which the radiance of dark spots (<s>candraka</s>) sparkles' — [means that] in which the appearance of dark marks flashes. 'In darkness' means in obscurity. '<s>Andhakāri</s>' [means] of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) [as the destroyer of the demon <s>Andhaka</s>]. '<s>Guha</s>' means <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Skanda</s>). 'Like another' — here, by the force of the word '<s>apara</s>' (another), when the perception of a second <s>Guha</s>-hood arises regarding the king, [but] in reality that is impossible, [then] from the supposition of its possibility there is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). But without the word '<s>apara</s>', when the actual <s>Guha</s> himself, established in his own form, would be perceived, this would be <s>upamā</s> (simile). The same should be understood in '<s>apara iva Pākaśāsanaḥ</s>' (as if another <s>Indra</s>), '<s>maurvīṃ dvitīyām</s>' (a second bowstring), and the like. Regarding '<s>aharpati</s>' — by the rule '<s>aharādīnāṃ patyādiṣu</s>' (of <s>ahar</s> etc. before <s>pati</s> etc.), the <s>r</s> [appears]. Here the qualities such as sustaining have subordinate status, while the substratum has predominance. For an agent, in accomplishing a subordinate action, incidentally accomplishes the principal action — but there is no incidental [relation] in those [subordinate actions]. Where all [actions] have incidental [relation], there indeed all of them are expressible by the verb. For example:

children.text: saudhād ityādi / itarad aprādhānyam / ādyā pradhānabhūtā / aparā aprādhānyavatī / bahulagrahaṇam iti "viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam" (PS_2,1.57) ity atra / kva cid ityādi / "kva cit pravṛttiḥ kva cid apravṛttir" iti bahulagrahaṇaprayojanasya vyavasthitatvāt / utargeti samāsavidhiḥ sāmānyarūpatvād utsargaḥ prādhānyādivivakṣānimittaś ca tatpratiṣedho viśeṣarūpatvād apavādaḥ / apavādasyaiveti / "apavādaviṣayaparihāreṇotsargasya pravṛttir" iti nyāyāt / kartum aśakya iti / avyavasthitaviṣayatvāt / yathā "utsargasya ghañy amanuṣye bahulam" (PS_6,3.122) ity atra / pariśabde tv ayaṃ bhavati / parivādaḥ parīvāda iti / vivāda ity atra naiva bhavati / tadviṣayaḥ syād iti "kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam" (PS_3,3.113) ityādigatasya bahulagrahaṇasya vidhyanuvādabhāvaviṣaye sāmarthyābhāvāt samāsābhāva iti bhāvaḥ / tadabhiprāyam iti ācāryābhiprāyam / sāpekṣatā(mi)dīti / ṛddhasya rājñaḥ puruṣa ityādau / tat samarthagrahaṇam / etadvyāvṛttīti etacchabdena pradhānetarabhāvaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ / tasyehārthatvam apīti samarthagrahaṇaṃ pradhānetarabhāvaviṣayanivṛttyartham apīty arthaḥ / vidheyoddeśyeti uddeśyo 'trordhvanirdeśārhatvād anuvādyaḥ / yat teneti / yacchabdaḥ pūrvārthasaṃbaddhaḥ / tenāpāraṇena / anabhidhānaṃ veti abhidhānalakṣaṇā hi kṛttaddhitasmāsā iti / samarthagrahaṇaṃ ca veti / caśabdo 'trātiriktaḥ, samuccayavikalpayor virodhāt / evaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: '<s>Saudhāt</s>' (from the palace) and so forth. The other [interpretation] is subordination. The first [interpretation] is the principal one. The second has subordination. 'The word <s>bahula</s>' refers to [the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule] '<s>viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam</s>' (the qualifier [is compounded] with the qualified, variously) (<s>PS</s> 2.1.57). 'In some cases' and so forth — since the purpose of the word <s>bahula</s> is established as 'sometimes application, sometimes non-application.' '<s>Utsarga</s>' (general rule) — the compound-rule, being of a general nature, is the general rule; and the prohibition of that, being occasioned by the intention to express predominance and the like, being of a specific nature, is the exception (<s>apavāda</s>). 'Of the exception alone' — by the principle that 'the general rule operates by excluding the domain of the exception.' 'Impossible to make' — because the domain is unsettled. As in [the rule] '<s>utsargasya ghañy amanuṣye bahulam</s>' (the general rule with <s>ghañ</s> in the non-human domain, variously) (<s>PS</s> 6.3.122). With the word <s>pari</s>, however, this happens: '<s>parivādaḥ</s>' [and] '<s>parīvādaḥ</s>.' But with '<s>vivāda</s>' it never happens. [When] the domain of the <s>bahula</s> usage found in rules like '<s>kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam</s>' (<s>PS</s> 3.3.113) concerns the injunctive-descriptive distinction, there is absence of compound due to lack of semantic capacity — this is the purport. 'His view' means the teacher's view. '<s>Sāpekṣatā</s>' — as in '<s>ṛddhasya rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ</s>' (the man of the prosperous king) and the like. That is the <s>samartha</s>-condition. 'The exclusion of this' — by the word 'this,' the non-predominant status is referred to. 'Its relevance here too' — the <s>samartha</s>-condition is also for the purpose of excluding the non-predominant domain — this is the meaning. 'Predicate and subject' — the subject here, being fit to be stated first, is the topic (<s>anuvādya</s>). 'By what, by that' — the <s>yat</s>-pronoun is connected with the prior meaning. 'By that' means by that conclusion. 'Or non-designation' — for designation is defined as <s>kṛt</s>, <s>taddhita</s>, and <s>samāsa</s>. 'And the <s>samartha</s>-condition' — the particle <s>ca</s> here is superfluous, since conjunction and disjunction would be contradictory. Thus —

body.translated_text: Thus. Others, however, say: granted that a grammatical irregularity (<s>apaśabda</s>) is a minor fault in relation to <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), nevertheless the use of irregular forms by great poets is a great fault. Therefore here, by the rule '<s>temeśabdau nipāteṣu</s>' (the words <s>te</s> and <s>me</s> are among the particles), such a <s>me</s>-word is a particle that resembles a case-ending, just as the word <s>aham</s> in '<s>ahantā</s>', '<s>ahaṃyuḥ</s>' and so forth. Therefore there is no distinction here. Is it then entirely the case that the usage is faulty? No, he says, 'but' (<s>kim tu</s>) — of this compound. 'Without' means because <s>vīra</s>, <s>raudra</s> and such [<s>rasas</s>] are manifested through the compound. '<s>Vṛtta</s>' refers to meters such as <s>Vasantatilaka</s>. '<s>Vṛttayaḥ</s>' means styles such as <s>Kaiśikī</s> and types such as <s>Upanāgarika</s>.

body.text:
"dṛṣṭir nāmṛtavarṣiṇī smitamadhuprasyandi vaktraṃ na tan
  nārdrārdraṃ hṛdayaṃ na candanarasasparśāni cāṅgāni vā"
body.translated_text: "Her gaze is not one that showers nectar; nor is that face dripping with the honey of a smile; nor is her heart tender and moist; nor are her limbs like the touch of sandalwood paste."

children.text: [Page 31]
children.translated_text: [Page 31]

children.text: ity atra cavāśabdadvayaṃ pratyuktaṃ, cavāśabdārthayor ekatra virodhāt / khaṇḍiketi khaṇḍo granthasaṃbandhī na tu samasto granthaḥ / sa vidyate yeṣām / anavagatatadabhiprāyair iti samarthagrahaṇaṃ praty ācāryasya hi tair abhiprāyo nāgataḥ / abhidhānādhānoddhāreti / abhidhānānāṃ śabdānām ādhānam abhinavānāṃ nyasanam / uddhāraḥ pūrvakāṇām uddharaṇam / śālīnā adhṛṣṭā avicārakā ity arthaḥ / aparam apīti punaruktādikam / taccinteti / prādhānyetarabhāvena samāsāsamāsacintā /
children.translated_text: Here the two words <s>ca</s> and <s>vā</s> have been accounted for, since the meanings of <s>ca</s> and <s>vā</s> would be contradictory in the same [place]. '<s>Khaṇḍikā</s>' means a section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) related to the text, not the entire text. [Those] in whom it [such sectional knowledge] exists. 'By those who have not understood his intent' — for, with respect to the <s>samartha</s>-condition, the teacher's intent was not grasped by them. '<s>Abhidhānādhānoddhāra</s>' — '<s>ādhāna</s>' is the depositing of designations, i.e., the placing of new words; '<s>uddhāra</s>' is the extraction, i.e., the removal of earlier ones. '<s>Śālīna</s>' means shy, i.e., those who do not examine — this is the meaning. 'And furthermore' means repetition and the like. 'That deliberation' means the deliberation concerning compounding and non-compounding based on the predominant-subordinate relation.

children.text: prakaraṇeti / yatrārthaprakaraṇādinā śabdasya vācyo 'rthaḥ prakarṣāpakarṣādikam arthāntaraṃ prakāśayati, tatrābhipretārthavināśabhayāt samāso na karttavyaḥ / yathā "rāmasya pāṇir asi" iti / prakaraṇaśabdādisakha iti pāṭhe "śabdasyānyasya sannidhir" iti svīkṛtam / yadā prakaraṇakākvādisakha iti pāṭhaḥ, tadā kākugrahaṇena svaraviśeṣa ucyate yaḥ "kālo vyaktisvarādayaḥ" iti kāvyagatatvena svīkṛtaḥ / evaṃ prasaktānuprasaktikayā samāsagatatvena tadatideśena samagra(pra?)vṛttigatatvenāpi guṇapradhānabhāvavivakṣāṃ mahatā prapañcena parighaṭayya prakṛtodāraṇe ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣagatatvena yojayitum āha ittham avasthita iti / ambikāyā upādānam iti saṃbandhaḥ / tat kim iti / viśeṣaṇasyānyakesarivyāvṛttir vā, kesarigataprakarṣapratipādanaṃ vā phalam / ādye pakṣe nirdiṣṭacamatkārasambhāvanā / dvitīye tu samāsānupapattir iti tātparyam / vivakṣitapadaṃ camatkārātiśayapadena yojanīyam / tasyā ity ambikāyās sakāśāt / jātyantaraṃ viśiṣṭāvāntarakesarijātiḥ / tayāvacchinno viśiṣṭaḥ / viśiṣṭa eveti lokottaraḥ / mohantv iti harer vihaṅgamo garuḍaḥ / moham ajñānaṃ hantv ity arthaḥ / garuḍajātyavacchinna iti / saugatadṛśā garuḍānāṃ bahutvād iti bhāvaḥ / vihaṅgamaviśeṣatvaṃ tu jātyādivailakṣaṇyāt / svābhiprāyāviṣkaraṇam iti / sādṛśyamūlayāprastutapraśaṃsayeti bhāvaḥ / tasyāś ceti tacchabdena sarasvatī parāmṛṣṭā / sarasvatyā ambikā pratibimbam ātmanaś ca kesarīty arthaḥ / dvitīyapakṣa iti / kesarigataprakarṣapratipādanapakṣe /
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>prakaraṇa</s>' (context): Where, through the context, meaning, and the like, the denoted meaning of a word reveals a further meaning such as excellence or inferiority, there, out of fear of destroying the intended meaning, no compound should be made. As in '<s>Rāmasya pāṇir asi</s>' (you are the hand of <s>Rāma</s>). In the reading '<s>prakaraṇaśabdādisakha</s>' (accompanied by context, word, etc.), it is accepted that 'the proximity of another word' [is a factor]. When the reading is '<s>prakaraṇakākvādisakha</s>' (accompanied by context, vocal intonation, etc.), then by the word <s>kāku</s>, a particular intonation is meant, which is accepted as pertaining to poetry in the [rule] '<s>kālo vyaktisvarādayaḥ</s>' (time, manifestation, intonation, etc.). Thus, through connected and subsidiary [discussions], having elaborated at great length the intention to express the predominant-subordinate relation in compounds, by extension to [cases of] collective application, [the author] now applies it to the illustrative example under discussion as pertaining to the genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, saying 'thus established.' The adoption of '<s>Ambikā</s>' is the relation. 'What then?' — The qualifier either serves to distinguish from another lion, or to convey the excellence inherent in the lion — [these are the two] results. In the first alternative, there is the supposition of the wonder [already] indicated. In the second, the compound becomes unjustifiable — this is the purport. The word 'intended' should be connected with the word 'excessive wonder.' 'Of her' means from <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>). 'Another species' means a distinguished sub-species of lion. '[The lion] determined by that' means distinguished. 'Distinguished indeed' means transcendent. Regarding '<s>mohantva</s>' — <s>Hari</s>'s bird is <s>Garuḍa</s>. 'May it destroy delusion' — may it destroy ignorance, this is the meaning. 'Delimited by the <s>Garuḍa</s>-species' — the purport is that from the Buddhist perspective, <s>Garuḍas</s> are numerous. But the status of being a particular bird [is distinguished] by difference in species and the like. 'The revelation of one's own intent' — the purport is that this is [an instance of] <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (indirect praise) based on similarity. 'And of her' — by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun, <s>Sarasvatī</s> is referred to. <s>Ambikā</s> is a reflection of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and [he himself] is the lion — this is the meaning. 'The second alternative' — in the alternative where the excellence inherent in the lion is being conveyed.

children.text: samāsād asāv iti ambikākesariśabdād unmiṣaty eva sa camatkāra ity arthaḥ / udayāstamayeti / vṛttau camatkārasyātiśayo
children.translated_text: From the compound of that [word], i.e., from the words <s>Ambikā</s> and <s>kesarin</s> (lion) [in compound], that very wonder springs forth — this is the meaning. Regarding '<s>udayāstamaya</s>' (rising and setting) — in the [metrical] composition, there is an intensification of wonder.

children.text: ⟨°astamaya conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: '<s>astamaya</s>' conjectured by the editor]

children.text: vākye udaya iti cūlikākrameṇa yogaḥ / upadarśitam eva prāg iti udāharaṇapratyudāharaṇapradarśanadvāreṇa / iṣṭaṃ hīti abhipretasyāprāptir yā, sā codanārhā iṣṭam etan na sidhyatīti / yat tu nābhipretaṃ tasyāprāptir bhūṣaṇaṃ, na tu dūṣaṇam ity arthaḥ / asmābhir asāv iti asau camatkāraḥ / sā bhrāntir eveti nirvikalpavikalpabhedena dvividhā bhrāntiḥ / tatrādyā timirādyupaplutendriyasya dvicandrādipratītirūpā / dvitīyā tv abhimānarūpā śuktirajatādipratītisvarūpā / seti camatkārāvagatiḥ / vyākhyāvākyād eveti ambikāyāḥ kesarīti samāsavivaraṇavākyāt / teṣām iti pratītivaicitryānabhyupagamavādinām / tatrāropiteti tatra samāse śuktisthānīye rajatam ivāropitāvāstavīty arthaḥ / udayāstamayapakṣau kramād vākyasamāsagatau / udyoga iti / saṃrambhapadaṃ nirasyodyogapadakaraṇaṃ prakramyamānodyuktavat padakramābhedāya / yo 'sāv ity adaḥśabdaḥ prasiddhiparāmarśakaḥ yacchabdapratinirdeśasya tacchabdena kariṣyamāṇatvāt / pratipāditeti / ārtho hi kevalatacchabdasya prayoganibandhana upakramopasaṃhārakramaḥ pratipādita
children.translated_text: In the sentence, '<s>udaya</s>' (rise) is connected by the sequence of <s>cūlikā</s> (crest-device). 'Already demonstrated' means by way of showing examples and counter-examples. '<s>iṣṭaṃ hi</s>' means that the non-attainment of what is desired is worthy of injunction, i.e., 'this desired end is not achieved.' But the non-attainment of what is not desired is an ornament, not a blemish—that is the meaning. 'By us, that' means that <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder). '<s>sā bhrāntir eva</s>' means <s>bhrānti</s> (illusion/error) is of two kinds through the distinction of non-conceptual and conceptual [cognition]. The first is the cognition of a double moon and the like by one whose senses are afflicted by an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>) and the like. The second has the form of a mistaken identification, such as the cognition of silver in a mother-of-pearl shell. '<s>sā</s>' refers to the apprehension of aesthetic wonder. 'From the explanatory sentence itself' means from the analytical sentence [stating] that <s>Ambikā</s>'s [son is] a lion. 'Of those' refers to those who do not accept the variety of cognition. 'Superimposed there' means that in that compound, something unreal is superimposed like silver upon what stands in the place of a shell—that is the meaning. The positions of rise and setting correspond respectively to the sentence and the compound. '<s>Udyoga</s>' (exertion): the replacement of the word '<s>saṃrambha</s>' (impetus) with the word '<s>udyoga</s>' is for the purpose of maintaining the same word-sequence as in 'one who is being undertaken, exerting oneself.' '<s>Yo 'sāv</s>': the word '<s>adaḥ</s>' is one that refers back to what is well-known, since the reciprocal indication of the <s>yat</s>-word will be made with the <s>tat</s>-word. '<s>Pratipāditā</s>': the sequence of introduction and conclusion, which is the basis for employing the bare <s>tat</s>-word, has indeed been established

children.text: [Page 32]
children.translated_text: [Page 32]

children.text: eva / rajaś chaleneti / chalevaśabdaprayoge sāpahnaveyam utprekṣā / kevalacchalaśabdaprayoge 'py apahnutiḥ / kevalevaśabdaprayoge ca sambhāvanapratītāv utprekṣā / dvayaprayoge tu śabalā pratītiḥ / na cātrāpahnutyutprekṣayoḥ saṅkaraḥ / utprekṣā hy apahnutyavinābhāvinī / so 'pahnavaḥ kva cid garbhīkṛto yathā "nakhakṣatānīva vanasthalīnām" ity atra, na palāśāni, kin tu sambhāvayāmi nakhakṣatānīti pratīteḥ / kva cit tu śabdena pratipādyate yathā "adhyāruroheve"ti / evaṃ cāsyā apahnutyavinābhāvinyā apahnutibādhakatvaṃ, na tayā saha saṅkaraḥ / bhinnavākyatāyām eveti / tatra hi vidhyanuvādabhāva āñjasyena krameṇa pratīyate / tad eva veti viśeṣaṇam / tac ca vidhyanuvādabhāvavivakṣāyāṃ vidheyam / anyatreti / utkarṣāparṣayor vidheyatvasya cābhāve / kāmacāra iti samāsāsamāsayoḥ / tadartham iti utkarṣādiviṣaye samāsaniṣedhārtham /
children.translated_text: already. '<s>Rajaś chalena</s>': when both '<s>chala</s>' (pretext) and '<s>iva</s>' (as if) are used, it is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) with <s>apahnava</s> (denial). When '<s>chala</s>' alone is used, it is <s>apahnuti</s> (denial). When '<s>iva</s>' alone is used, and the cognition is of possibility, it is <s>utprekṣā</s>. When both are used, the cognition is mixed. And there is no <s>saṅkara</s> (confusion/intermixture) of <s>apahnuti</s> and <s>utprekṣā</s> here, for <s>utprekṣā</s> is inseparable from <s>apahnuti</s>. That denial is sometimes implicit, as in '<s>nakhakṣatānīva vanasthalīnām</s>' ('as if nail-marks of the forest-grounds')—where the cognition is: 'not <s>palāśa</s> leaves, but I fancy they are nail-marks.' Sometimes, however, it is expressed verbally, as in '<s>adhyāruroheva</s>' ('as if it mounted'). Thus, since [<s>utprekṣā</s>] is inseparable from <s>apahnuti</s>, it can override <s>apahnuti</s>, but there is no intermixture with it. 'Only when there are separate sentences': for there the <s>vidhi-anuvāda</s> (injunction-restatement) relation is understood directly in natural sequence. 'That very <s>vi</s>' is a qualifier, and it is what is to be predicated (<s>vidheya</s>) when the <s>vidhi-anuvāda</s> relation is intended. 'Elsewhere': when neither superiority nor inferiority has the status of <s>vidheya</s>. '<s>Kāmacāra</s>': [refers to the freedom of choice] between compound and non-compound forms. 'For that purpose': for the prohibition of compounds in the context of superiority and the like.

children.text: sāpekṣeti sāpekṣam asamarthaṃ bhavatīty etāvanmātrapratītaye / pitroḥ svateveti yathā pitarau vandanīyāv iti nityasaṃ(ba)ndhanyāyād nijāv eva pitarau pratīyete, tadvat sāpekṣāṇām anabhidhānākhyena nyāyena samāsābhāvaḥ pratyeṣyate / svatā ātmīyatvam iva / (sā) doṣaprakāranivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāpekṣā</s>' (syntactically dependent): this is merely for the understanding that what is syntactically dependent is <s>asamartha</s> (incapable [of forming a compound]). '<s>Pitroḥ svata eva</s>' (of the parents, inherently): just as when [we say] 'parents are to be venerated,' by the rule of natural relationship, one's own parents alone are understood—similarly, the absence of compound formation for syntactically dependent [words] will be understood through the principle called 'non-denotation' (<s>anabhidhāna</s>). '<s>Svatā</s>' (inherent nature) is like 'being one's own.' This is the cessation of the type of defect [described].

body.text: adhunā svotkarṣaśālitāprakaṭanārthaṃ svapariśramaṃ piṇḍīkṛtya ślokena darśayitum āha kāvyakāñcaneti / kāvyam eva parīkṣaṇīyatvāt suvarṇaṃ tatra parīkṣāsthānaṃ nikaṣopalam ātmānaṃ manyate, na punar uktakrameṇa parāmarthas san nikaṣopalaḥ / ata eva kuntakeneti khyātasyāpy ulluṇṭhanavacanam / śloka eṣa iti / yaḥ sarvasāratayā pradarśitas tatreyatī dūṣaṇavṛṣṭir muktā / tatrānyasya granthasya kā gaṇeneti sūcitam / nidarśitaḥ sthālīpulākanyāyenodāhṛtaḥ / atra śloke vakṣyamāṇaitadīyanyāyānusāreṇa kaṣeṇa niyamena kāñcanākṣepāt kāñcanapadaṃ paunaruktyadoṣaduṣṭam / nijakāvyalakṣmaṇīty atra nijārthasya saṃrambhāspadatvena vidheyatvāt samāsakaraṇaṃ vidheyāvimarśadūṣitaṃ ke cid ācakṣate vicakṣaṇāḥ / tattvenaiva granthakṛtā "svakṛtiṣv ayantrita" ityādinā dattottaram eva / asya ca vidheyāvimarśasyānantetaraprasiddhalakṣyapātitvenāsmābhir nāṭakamīmāṃsāyāṃ sāhityamīmāṃsāyāṃ ca teṣu teṣu sthāneṣu prapañcaḥ pradarśita iti granthavistarabhayād ita evoparamyate /
body.translated_text: Now, in order to demonstrate his own labor in condensed form through a verse, for the purpose of displaying his own excellence, he says '<s>kāvyakāñcana</s>' (poetry-gold). Poetry itself, being something to be tested, is [like] gold; the touchstone for testing it, he considers to be himself—not that he is actually a touchstone in the manner described. For this very reason, '<s>kuntakena</s>' (by <s>Kuntaka</s>): even of the famous one, there is the statement of overturning. 'This is the verse': the point is that where [a verse] has been presented as the essence of everything, such a shower of criticism has been unleashed upon it. 'What account then of another work?'—this is implied. '<s>Nidarśitaḥ</s>': illustrated by the maxim of '<s>sthālīpulāka</s>' (testing rice by a single grain from the pot). In this verse, following the principle about to be stated by the author, by the rule of testing, since the word '<s>kāñcana</s>' (gold) is used redundantly [with '<s>kaṣa</s>' already implying gold-testing], the word '<s>kāñcana</s>' is vitiated by the defect of <s>paunaruktya</s> (repetition). In '<s>nijakāvyalakṣmaṇī</s>' (the characteristic of one's own poetry), some discerning critics point out that the compounding is vitiated by failure to highlight the <s>vidheya</s>, since the meaning of '<s>nija</s>' (own) is the <s>vidheya</s> as the object of emphasis. The author himself has indeed given the reply with '<s>svakṛtiṣv ayantrita</s>' ('in one's own compositions, unrestricted') and the like. And this [defect of] <s>vidheyāvimarśa</s> (failure to highlight the predicate), having been recognized as falling under well-known exemplary instances not [previously] established elsewhere, has been elaborated by us in the <s>Nāṭakamīmāṃsā</s> and the <s>Sāhityamīmāṃsā</s> in various places; but for fear of expanding this work, we desist here.

body.text: evaṃ vidheyāvimarśaṃ prakāravaicitryeṇa lakṣayitvā prakramabhedaṃ lakṣayitum āha - prakramabhedo 'pīti / pratipattṛpratīter iti rathasthānīyā pratipattṛpratītiḥ / utkhāto viṣamonnataḥ pradeśaḥ / enam iti śabdārthavyavahāram / tadviṣayabhāvaḥ prakramabhedaviṣayatvam / anabhibhāṣaṇaṃ tatkartṛkabhāṣaṇābhāvaḥ / evam anālapanaṃ jñeyam / analam asamarthā / vidhyanuvādabhāvaprakāratopagamād iti prakāraḥ sādṛśyam / upakrāntaṃ hy anuvādasthānīyam / nirvāhakaṃ ca vidheyaprakhyam / tatra spaṣṭaṃ vidheyānuvādyaprakāram udāharati yatheti /
body.translated_text: Having thus characterized <s>vidheyāvimarśa</s> through its variety of types, [the author] proceeds to characterize <s>prakramabheda</s> (breach of sequence), saying '<s>prakramabhedo 'pi</s>.' '<s>Pratipattṛpratīteḥ</s>': the cognition of the recipient [of the meaning] is like the chariot [that must travel on a smooth road]. '<s>Utkhātaḥ</s>': a spot that is uneven and elevated. '<s>Enam</s>': this word-meaning convention. '<s>Tadviṣayabhāvaḥ</s>': being the subject matter of <s>prakramabheda</s>. '<s>Anabhibhāṣaṇam</s>': the absence of speech by that agent. '<s>Anālapanam</s>' should be understood similarly. '<s>Analam</s>': incapable. 'By the acceptance of the <s>vidhi-anuvāda</s> relation as a type': <s>prakāra</s> here means resemblance. For what has been introduced is analogous to the <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement) position, and what brings [the verse] to completion resembles the <s>vidheya</s> (predicate). He then illustrates clearly the type of <s>vidheya-anuvādya</s> (predicate-restated) with '<s>yathā</s>':—

children.text: "tadā jāyante guṇā yadā tais sahṛdayair gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: "Then do [poetic] qualities come into being, when they are apprehended by those connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>);

children.text: ravikiraṇānugṛhītāni bhavanti kamalāni kamalāni //"
children.translated_text: lotuses become [truly] lotuses when graced by the rays of the sun."

children.text: "evam eva janas tasyā dadāti kapolopamāyāṃ śaśibimbam /
children.translated_text: "Thus people indeed give the moon-orb as a comparison for her cheek;

children.text: paramārthavicāre punaś candraś candra iva varākaḥ //"
children.translated_text: but upon investigation of the ultimate truth, the moon is a poor thing, [merely] like a moon."

body.text: utkarṣāpakarṣamātreti kamalānām utkarṣavivakṣā / candrasya punar apakarṣavivakṣā / ata evodāharaṇadvayaṃ dattam / prakramabhedaprakāra iti prakāro 'tra viśeṣaḥ / paryāyaprakrameti / candraśabdārthasya śaśiśabdena paryāyāntaranirdeśo na yukto vakṣyamāṇaprakramabhedaprasaṅgāt /

children.text: na cai
children.translated_text: 'Nor thus'—

children.text: [Page 33]
children.translated_text: [Page 33]

children.text: vam iti tenaiva śabdenopasaṃhāra ity arthaḥ / tayor iti prakramabhedapunaruktayoḥ / asyeti prakramābhedasya parāmarśaḥ / tatra hi yathoddeśaṃ pratinirdeśe na paunaruktyam, aikarasyena pratītiprasaraṇāt / uddeśyapratinirdeśyabhāvo na paunaruktyasya viṣayaḥ / yathā -
children.translated_text: means that the conclusion should be made with that very [same] word—that is the meaning. 'Of those two' refers to <s>prakramabheda</s> and <s>paunaruktya</s> (repetition). 'Of this' is a reference back to the absence of <s>prakramabheda</s>. For when the reciprocal indication corresponds to the original designation, there is no repetition, because the cognition flows as a unity. The relation of what is designated and what is reciprocally indicated is not the domain of [the defect of] repetition. As in—

body.translated_text: '<s>Utkarṣāpakarṣamātra</s>' means: with the lotuses, the intention is to express superiority; with the moon, on the other hand, the intention is to express inferiority. For this very reason, two examples were given. '<s>Prakramabhedaprakāra</s>': <s>prakāra</s> here means a specific type. '<s>Paryāyaprakrama</s>': indicating the meaning of the word '<s>candra</s>' by the synonym '<s>śaśin</s>' is not appropriate, because of the incurrence of the <s>prakramabheda</s> (breach of sequence) about to be discussed.

body.text:
"kṣāmāṅgyaḥ kṣatakomalāṅguligaladraktaiḥ sadarbhāḥ sthalīḥ
  pādaiḥ pātitayāvakair iva galadbāṣpāmbudhautānanāḥ /"
body.translated_text: "With emaciated bodies, the grounds with <s>darbha</s> grass [reddened] by the dripping blood from their tender scratched fingers, as if [stained] with <s>yāvaka</s> dye cast by their feet; their faces washed by falling tears..."

body.text: iti / atra galacchabdadvayaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ yathoddeśaṃ pratinirdeśo 'sya viṣaya iti samañjasam / [tayor iti prakramābhedapaunaruktyayoḥ / asyeti prakramābhedasya parāmarśaḥ /] nanu "vrajataḥ kva tāta! vajasī"ty atra vrajinā prakrame vajinā ca nirvāhe kathaṃ na prakramabhedaḥ / vajatir api dhātur asti / "vaja vraja gatāv" iti pāṭhād ity āśaṅkyoktaṃ vrajata iti / uditaṃ śiśuneti uditam ity asya viśeṣaṇaṃ paricayagatārtham iti / asphuṭam iti ca / bhāve cātra pratyayaḥ / kāryārthaṃ pathi gacchataḥ paścān nāmodīraṇaṃ viruddham iti śiśunā lalitavacasā nāmany udīrite jananyāsya bhartsanaṃ kṛtam iti tato 'sya manyur vivṛddha ity atra tātparyārthaḥ / evaṃ dhāturūpāyāḥ prkṛte prakramabhedaṃ pradarśya saṃprati prātipadikarūpāyās tasyā madhye ca sarvanāmādīnāṃ prakāravaicitryeṇa taṃ darśayati sarvanāmeti / kva cit punaḥ pustakeṣu prakṛtiprakramabhedād anantaraṃ pratyayaprakramabhedodāharaṇaṃ tat paścāt sarvanāmaprakramabhedanirdeśo dṛśyate / tatra ca prkṛter anantaraṃ pratyayasyaiva nirdeśa ucita iti sa eva kathita iti saṅgatiḥ / tataḥ paraṃ prakṛtiviśeṣāṇāṃ pratyayaviśeṣāṇāṃ tatsamudāyānāṃ ca tatprakramabhedo nirūpayiṣyate / uktarītyeti / "yas tv ekavākye kartṛtvenokto yaś cedamādibhir" ity atroktena krameṇety arthaḥ / nanu yacchabdena prakrame tacchabdenedamādibhir vā (prakrame yacchabdena vā?) katham upasaṃhāra ity āha na caivam iti / anyonyāpekṣe iti / yattador nityābhisaṃbandha ity uktam / evaṃ tacchabdādūraviprakṛṣṭārtheṣv idamādiṣu prāg ukte "yo 'vikalpam" ityādau jñeyam / teneti prakṛtopasaṃhāraḥ / idamādīnāṃ parasparāvāntaravaicitrye 'pi sthūladṛṣṭyā ekārthatvam / atra hīti atra hi kartṛviśeṣaṇadvāreṇaikasya hetutvam aparasya sākṣād iti prakramabhedaḥ / yaśodhigantum iti atra hi tṛtīyātumunoḥ pratītivaiṣamyajanakatvam / vāśabdasyeti / vakṣyati hi "tulyakakṣyatayā yatra padārthāḥ" iti /

children.text: apatyavato 'pīti yuktaḥ pāṭha iti / atra ke cit samarthayante - (viśeṣataḥ snihyanto dṛśyante?) tat putraśabdasyāpatyaviśeṣavācitve apatyaśabdasya ca sāmānyavācitve 'pi sarvanāmavaśād viśeṣaparyavasāne bhavaty eva prakṛtārthaparipoṣa iti / tad etad asya granthakārasya hṛdayam anālokyaiva, yasmād dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikabhāvenātra vākyārthadvayam upanibaddham / tatra ca dvayor bimbapratibimbabhāvena nirdeśo yujyate / dṛṣṭānte cātra sāmānyopakramaḥ, viśeṣopasaṃhāraḥ, puṣpaśabdasya sāmānyavācitvāc cūtaśabdasya viśeṣābhidhāyakatvād / viśeṣasya cotkṛṣṭatayaivātṛptiviṣayatvam / dārṣṭāntike (akaṣṭaṃ?)
children.translated_text: The reading '<s>apatyavato 'pi</s>' (even of one having offspring) is appropriate — [this is argued as follows:] Here some justify [the alternative reading]: (In particular, affection is seen?) Since, even though the word '<s>putra</s>' denotes a particular kind of offspring and the word '<s>apatya</s>' is a general term, through the force of the pronoun (<s>sarvanāma</s>) there is ultimately a particular reference, the nourishment of the intended meaning does indeed occur. / But this is [said] without examining the heart of this author, since here a pair of sentence-meanings is composed in the relation of illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) and thing illustrated (<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>). And of those two, a specification in the manner of image and reflection (<s>bimbapratibimba</s>) is appropriate. / In the illustration here: a general beginning, a particular conclusion — because the word '<s>puṣpa</s>' (flower) is a general term and the word '<s>cūta</s>' (mango) denotes the particular. And the particular, precisely because of its excellence, is the object of insatiable [desire]. / In the thing illustrated, [the result would be] (undesirable?)

children.text: ⟨aniṣṭam conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>aniṣṭam</s> (undesirable) (Ed.)]

children.text: viśeṣopakramaḥ / sāmānyopasaṃhāraḥ / sarvanāmavaśād vā viśeṣāntaranirdeśo nyāyyaḥ / sthitapāṭhe putraśabdasya viśeṣavācitvam apatyaśabdasya sāmānyavācino viśeṣaparyavasānam / yadā tv apatyavato 'pīti pāṭhas tadāsya sāmānyopakramo viśeṣopasaṃhāraḥ / dvitīyasyāpatyaśabdasya sarvanāmasaṃbandhena viśeṣaparyavasānād yathaikīyamate "tasminn adrau kati cid bale"ty atra / (ādi)
children.translated_text: a particular beginning, a general conclusion. Or, through the force of the pronoun, the specification of another particular is appropriate. / In the established reading, the word '<s>putra</s>' (son) denotes the particular, while the word '<s>apatya</s>' (offspring), though a general term, ultimately refers to the particular. / But when the reading is '<s>apatyavato 'pi</s>' (even of one having offspring), there is a general beginning and a particular conclusion. Through the relation with the pronoun of the second [occurrence of] the word '<s>apatya</s>,' the ultimate reference is to the particular — as in the view of some regarding '<s>tasminn adrau kati cid bale</s>.' / (The word's)

children.text: ⟨api conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>api</s> (Ed.)]

children.text: śabdasyārthasaṅgatiś ced dṛśyeva bhrājate / yasya naivāpatyasaṃbandhas tasya mā bhūt kanyāyām ekasyām atṛptiḥ yasya tv anekāpatyayogas ta
children.translated_text: semantic coherence, if [present], shines forth like sight itself. For one who has no connection with offspring at all, there should be no insatiable [attachment] to a single daughter; but for one who has the connection of many offspring —

children.text: [Page 34]
children.translated_text: [Page 34]

children.text: sya katham ekasminn apatye snigdhatvam iti vismayaḥ / etadartha evāpiśabdo jīvati / atṛptikāraṇatvaṃ ca kanyāyāḥ parasamarpaṇīyatvena / guṇagauraveṇa ca snehapātratā / etadartham asyāś cūtena pratibimbanam / tad ittham apatyavato 'pīty eṣa eva pāṭhaḥ śreyān / samāsānupapattīti (adhikaraṇasiddhāntanyāyena?)
children.translated_text: how can there be tender affection toward one offspring? — this is the wonder. For this very purpose the word '<s>api</s>' (even) is meaningful. And the cause of insatiable [attachment] to the daughter is her being one who must be given away to another. And through the weight of [her] qualities, she becomes a vessel of affection. For this purpose, her reflection in the mango [tree is described]. / Thus, the reading '<s>apatyavato 'pi</s>' (even of one having offspring) is indeed the better one. / 'Impossibility of compound' — (by the principle of the topic-and-conclusion method?)

children.text: ⟨adhikaṃ na tu taddhānir iti nyāyena conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: 'an addition, not a loss of that, by the principle' (Ed.)]

children.text: guṇāntaralābha ity arthaḥ / varaṃ kṛteti / kṛtāḥ śikṣitāḥ santo dhvastā naṣṭā guṇā yasya / amaṇir avidyamānamaṇir alaṅkāraḥ / upalaśabdenātra maṇir eva vivakṣitaḥ / tannātra maṇiśabdaḥ prayukta iti paryāyaprakramabhedatvam / kham iveti / "haṃsaś candra iva candra iva haṃsa" iti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ / maghona indrasya sute 'rjune / vīryaṃ ca vidvatsv iti / vīryavedanaṃ cety eva hetutvena vivakṣitam / samuccayo vikalpo veti / vikalpo yaśo 'dhigantum ity atrodāhṛtaḥ / samuccayasya tv idaṃ vīryaṃ cety udāharaṇam / "vidvatsu vīryaṃ tanaye" iti pāṭhe na vedanaṃ hetutvena vivakṣitam, api tu vastusvarūpapratipādanaparatvenety ayaṃ manyate / evaṃ ca vidvatsv iti viśeṣaṇasya nairarthakyam āpadyata iti nānena vicāritam /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the gain of another quality. / '<s>Varaṃ kṛta</s>' (better [if] accomplished) — '<s>kṛtāḥ</s>' means 'educated'; '<s>dhvastā naṣṭā guṇāḥ</s>' — whose qualities are destroyed, ruined. / '<s>Amaṇi</s>' — an ornament without a gem. / By the word '<s>upala</s>' (stone), a gem (<s>maṇi</s>) is intended here. / [The objection is:] the word '<s>maṇi</s>' is not used here — this is a sequence-break of synonyms (<s>paryāyaprakramabheda</s>). / '<s>Kham iva</s>' (like the sky) — The correct reading is '<s>haṃśaś candra iva candra iva haṃsa</s>' ('the goose is like the moon, the moon is like the goose'). / '<s>Maghona</s>' — of <s>Indra</s>; his son <s>Arjuna</s>. / '<s>Vīryaṃ ca vidvatsu</s>' (and valor among the learned) — 'and the knowledge of valor' is intended as the reason. / 'Aggregation (<s>samuccaya</s>) or disjunction (<s>vikalpa</s>)' — the disjunction has been illustrated in '<s>yaśo 'dhigantum</s>' (to attain fame). The aggregation, however, is illustrated by '<s>vīryaṃ ca</s>' (and valor). / In the reading '<s>vidvatsu vīryaṃ tanaye</s>,' knowledge is not intended as the reason, but rather [the intention] is to convey the essential nature of the thing — this is his view. And thus the qualifier '<s>vidvatsu</s>' (among the learned) would become purposeless — but this has not been examined by him.

children.text: duṣkūlabhāva iti / sāmānādhikaraṇyenopakrame vaiyadhikaraṇyena pratinirdeśaḥ prakramabhedāvahaḥ atra caturthe pāde / "kapālam evāmalaśekharaśrīr" ity atra kapālānāṃ bahutve vācye yad ekatvavacanam amalaśekharaśrīr ity atra ca śekharamātre dharmiṇi vaktavye yacchekharaśrīr iti dharmavacanaṃ tad anupapannam eva gantavyam / evaṃ ca pūrvokteṣu vakṣyamāṇeṣu codāharaṇeṣu saṃbhavann api vicāro granthavistarabhayān na niravaśeṣatayā kṛta iti tatraivābhiyogaḥ kartavyaḥ / tadupetam iti / svaśabdena sarvanāmnā vā nirdeśas tulyaphala iti pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt / bhagavati yuṣmatprasādeneti / (anena) nyāyena "paśyata mātaḥ" iti vārttike dharmakīrteḥ prayogaḥ pratyuktaḥ / prādhānyābhāvād ity uktam iti / "yatraikakartṛkānekā prādhānyetarabhāk kriyā" ity atra / anenijur akṣālayan / jakṣur akhādan / bisaprasūnaṃ padmam / nejanādāv iti liṭā bhūtānadyatanaparokṣaprakrame anenijur iti tu bhūtānadyatanena nirvāhaḥ / tathā "dhṛtavikāsī"ty atra bhūtamātre ktapratyaya ity atrāpi kālaprakramabhedaḥ / tatropari tiṅantaprakramabhedo dvitīyo 'tra na sthitaḥ / evaṃ cehādigrahaṇena dhṛtavikāsīti gṛhyate / [vikacam asya dadhuḥ prasūnam iti / anenijur ity atra?]
children.translated_text: 'The state of fine garments' (<s>duṣkūlabhāva</s>) — In the beginning [there is] co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), but in the back-reference [there is] non-co-referentiality (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>) — this produces a sequence-break here in the fourth quarter. / In '<s>kapālam evāmalaśekharaśrīḥ</s>' — here, when the plurality of skulls is to be expressed, the use of the singular number; and in '<s>amalaśekharaśrīḥ</s>' — where only the crown (<s>śekhara</s>) as the property-bearer is to be stated, the expression of the property [instead as] 'crown-glory' — this must be understood as improper. / And thus, in the examples already stated and those to be stated, even though examination is possible, it has not been done exhaustively out of fear of excessive length of the treatise — so the effort should be directed there. / '<s>Tadupetam</s>' (accompanied by that) — because it will be demonstrated that specification by one's own word or by a pronoun yields the same result. / '<s>Bhagavati yuṣmatprasādena</s>' (by your grace, O Blessed One) — by (this) principle, the usage of <s>Dharmakīrti</s> in the <s>vārttika</s> '<s>paśyata mātaḥ</s>' (Look, mother!) is answered. / 'Because of the absence of predominance' — this was said in '[the verse] where the actions of a single agent are many, some predominant and others [subordinate].' / '<s>Anenijuḥ akṣālayan</s>' — they washed. '<s>Jakṣuḥ akhādan</s>' — they ate. '<s>Bisaprasūnaṃ padmam</s>' — lotus as a stalk-flower. / 'In <s>nejana</s> etc.' — when the sequence is the past non-contemporary witnessed (<s>parokṣa</s>) by the perfect tense (<s>liṭ</s>), '<s>anenijuḥ</s>' concludes with the past non-contemporary. Likewise in '<s>dhṛtavikāsī</s>' — where the <s>kta</s>-suffix is in the sense of past in general — here too there is a temporal sequence-break. / The second [type,] namely the finite-verb sequence-break above, does not apply here. / And thus, by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) here, '<s>dhṛtavikāsī</s>' is included. / [<s>vikacam asya dadhuḥ prasūnam</s> — '<s>anenijuḥ</s>' here?]

children.text: ⟨anenijur iti atra vikacam asya dadhuḥ prasūnam iti conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: '<s>anenijuḥ</s>' here — '<s>vikacam asya dadhuḥ prasūnam</s>' (they gave him a blossomed flower) (Ed.)]

children.text: samādhānaṃ na kṛtaṃ prakārāntareṇa samarthayiṣyamāṇatvāt / yadi vetyādināmuṃ prakramabhedaṃ nirākaroti / ajayad iti atra parokṣo 'pi jayo darśanārhatvāt parokṣatvena na vivakṣita iti liṭprayogo na kṛtaḥ / vidyamānasyāsyāvivakṣāyāṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha
children.translated_text: A resolution is not made, because it will be justified in another manner. / By '<s>yadi vā</s>' etc., he removes this sequence-break. / '<s>Ajayat</s>' (he conquered) — here, even though the victory was witnessed from a distance (<s>parokṣa</s>), since it is worthy of being seen, it was not intended as distant — hence the perfect tense (<s>liṭ</s>) was not used. / He gives an example for the non-expression of what [actually] exists —

children.text: anudarā kanyeti / na hi kasyāś cit kanyāyā udarābhāvaḥ kṛśatvāt punas tad api vivakṣyate / evaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: '<s>Anudarā kanyā</s>' (a slender-bellied maiden) — For no maiden is actually without a belly; but since she is slender, that [absence] too is intended [poetically]. And thus —

body.translated_text: Thus, here the two occurrences of the word '<s>galat</s>' (flowing) are specified — '[since] the back-reference (<s>pratinirdeśa</s>) follows the original mention (<s>yathoddeśa</s>),' this is consistent. / ['Of those two' — of sequence-break (<s>prakramābheda</s>) and repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>). / 'Of this' — refers to the sequence-break.] / Now, in '<s>vrajataḥ kva tāta vajasī</s>,' with '<s>vraja</s>' in the beginning and '<s>vaja</s>' at the conclusion, how is this not a sequence-break? Because the root '<s>vajati</s>' also exists, from the reading '<s>vaja vraja gatāv</s>' (both <s>vaja</s> and <s>vraja</s> mean 'going') — anticipating this objection, he says '<s>vrajataḥ</s>.' / '<s>Uditaṃ śiśunā</s>' — 'uttered' is a qualifier whose meaning belongs to familiar context, and also 'indistinct' (<s>asphuṭam</s>). / And here the suffix is in the sense of the action (<s>bhāva</s>). / The purport is: when the father, going on the road for some task, afterwards calls out names — which is incongruous — and when the child, in charming speech, utters the names, the mother rebukes him, and from that his anger increases. / Having thus demonstrated the sequence-break of a verbal-root form in the topic at hand, he now shows that [sequence-break] in nominal-stem forms, and among those, the variety of types in pronouns (<s>sarvanāma</s>) etc. — hence '<s>sarvanāma</s>.' / Moreover, in some manuscripts, after the root-sequence-break, the examples of suffix-sequence-break are seen, and thereafter the specification of pronoun-sequence-break. And there, since after the root the specification of the suffix alone is appropriate — that alone is stated — this is the connection. / Thereafter, the sequence-break of particular roots, particular suffixes, and their combinations will be examined. / 'By the stated method' — by the order stated in 'he who is mentioned as the agent in a single sentence, and he [who is referred to] by <s>idam</s> etc.' / Now, how can there be a conclusion with the <s>tat</s>-word when the beginning was with the <s>yat</s>-word, or with <s>idam</s> etc.? — to this he says 'na caivam' (not so). / 'Mutually dependent' — it is said that <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> are always correlated. Similarly for <s>idam</s> etc. when used for meanings remote [in the text], as stated earlier in '<s>yo 'vikalpam</s>' etc. — this should be understood. / 'By that' (<s>tena</s>) — the conclusion with the topic at hand. / Of <s>idam</s> etc., although there is internal variety among themselves, from a broad perspective they are of one meaning. / 'Here indeed' — here indeed, through the qualifier of the agent, one [thing] has the status of cause and the other directly — hence the sequence-break. / '<s>Yaśodhigantum</s>' (to attain fame) — here the [conjunction of] the instrumental case and the infinitive (<s>tumun</s>) produces an inequality of comprehension. / 'Of the word <s>vā</s>' — for he will say 'where the meanings of words are of equal status' etc.

children.text: "abhūdabhūmiḥ pratipakṣajanmanāṃ bhiyāṃ tanūjas tapanadyutir diteḥ /
children.translated_text: "He became the non-ground (<s>abhūmi</s>) for the birth of enemies, [their] fears; the body-born son of <s>Diti</s>, of the sun's radiance —

children.text: yam indraśabdārthaniṣūdanaṃ harer hariṇyapūrvaṃ kaśipuṃ pracakṣate //" ityādeḥ,
children.translated_text: whom they call <s>Kaśipu</s> (<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>), the slayer of the meaning of the word '<s>Indra</s>' [i.e., sovereignty] of <s>Hari</s>, unprecedented [in his enmity]" — from such [verses],

children.text: "tāta tvaṃ nijatejasaiva gamitaḥ svargaṃ yadi svasti te
children.translated_text: "O father, if you have gone to heaven by your own splendor alone, may it be well with you;

children.text: kiṃ tv anyena hṛtā vadhūr iti kathāṃ mā sakhyur agre kṛthāḥ /
children.translated_text: but do not tell your friend the story that your bride was carried off by another.

children.text: rāmo 'haṃ yadi rāghavas tad akhilaṃ vrīḷānamatkandharaṃ
children.translated_text: If I am <s>Rāma</s>, if I am a <s>Rāghava</s>, then all [this is cause for] shame, with neck bowed —

children.text: sārdhaṃ bandhujanena sendravijayī vaktā svayaṃ rāvaṇaḥ //"
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself, having conquered along with <s>Indra</s>, will tell it together with the kinfolk."

body.text: ityādeś ca mahataḥ kāvyapravāhasya na kiṃ cid duṣṭatvam / arthasyeti tadbhāvo 'rthatvaṃ sattā atadbhāva asattvam / yatreti pūrvārdhaśeṣaḥ / yatheti / na prakramabheda ity anvayaḥ / tatra kālaviśeṣo darśitaḥ /

children.text: [Page 35]
children.translated_text: [Page 35]

children.text: yathā bhūtasya bhāvinaś ca kālasyādyatanānadyatanatve parokṣāparokṣatve ca vaivakṣike eveti / (te) śīlādayo 'rthāḥ "ā kves tacchīlataddharmatatsādhukāriṣu" (PS_3.2.135) ity atra nirdiṣṭāḥ / teṣāṃ ca vaivkṣike sattvāsattve / evaṃ ca kva cit tācchīlikādipratyayaprayoge 'py anyatra tadakaraṇam aduṣṭam / yathā -
children.translated_text: Namely: that the past and future tenses have the quality of being today and not-today, and being remote and non-remote, is merely a matter of the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). The meanings such as habitual disposition (<s>śīla</s>) etc. are specified in the rule "up to <s>kvi</s>, [suffixes are applied] in the senses of that-disposition, that-nature, and that-well-performing" (PS 3.2.135). And their existence and non-existence are [also] a matter of speaker's intention. And thus, even when in some place the suffix expressing habitual disposition etc. is used, its non-use elsewhere is not faulty. For example —

body.translated_text: And in such [examples] from the great flow of poetry, there is no faultiness whatsoever. "Of the meaning" (<s>arthasya</s>) — its being (<s>tadbhāva</s>) is meaningfulness (<s>arthatva</s>), i.e., existence (<s>sattā</s>); its non-being (<s>atadbhāva</s>) is non-existence (<s>asattva</s>). "Where" (<s>yatra</s>) completes the first half. "As" (<s>yathā</s>) — the construal is: "[there is] no breach of sequence" (<s>na prakramabheda</s>). There, the particular [aspect of] time has been shown.

children.text: "jugopātmānam atrasto bheje dharmam anāturaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He protected himself, fearless; he practiced <s>dharma</s> (duty), free from distress;

children.text: agṛdhnur ādade so 'rtham asaktaḥ sukham anvabhūt //"
children.translated_text: without greed, he acquired wealth; unattached, he experienced happiness."

body.text: ity atrāgṛdhnur iti tācchīlyādyarthapratyayaprayoge 'py atrasta ity atrātrasnur ity akaraṇe 'pi na duṣṭatvam atrasnur iti vā nirdeśe agṛdhnur iti nirdoṣam eva / kartuḥ phalavattā kartrabhiprāyatvam / tad api vaivakṣikam eva / evaṃ ca "dṛṣṭā dṛṣṭim adho dadāti kurute nālāpam ābhāṣitā" ity atra yadi kartrabhiprāyatvaṃ kriyāphalasya, tadā dadātīti parasmaipadānupapattiḥ / na cet tadā kuruta ity atra parasmaipadaprasaṅga iti prakramabhedaparyanuyogo niravakāśa eva / evam anyatra boddhavyam / tena te iti / te kālaviśeṣādayaḥ tena vivakṣāprayuktatvena kāraṇena na darśitā ity arthaḥ / gāhantām iti / atra kartur ākhyātenābhidhānaṃ karmaṇaś cānabhidhānaṃ prakrāntaṃ visrabdhair ity anyathākṛtam iti kārakaprakramabhedaḥ / vihṛtiṃ viharaṇaṃ bhaṅgibhājanatvam ity arthaḥ / vivṛtam iti pāṭhe vistaraśālitvam ity arthaḥ / ratau vigraho virodhaḥ stanatair vyavahitas tatprasādād virodhasya kartum aśakyatvāt / vitene iti bhāve pratyayaḥ / stanitāni vitatībhūtānīty arthaḥ / śābdaḥ prakramabheda iti śabdaviṣayatvāc chābdaḥ / śābdaprakramabheda iti tu prakṛtiprakramabhedasyānukrameṇa ye paṭhanti taiḥ śābdaś cārthaś cottaro grantho nālocita ity upekṣyam etat / saṅgamabhūṣeti / atra buhuvrīhāv anyapadārthopasarjanenārthena krameṇopasaṃhṛtam iti / bhidyamānaśabdaviṣayatvāc chābdaḥ prakramabhedaḥ / evam ārthaḥ prakramabheda ity atra prathamaprakrāntabhidyamānārthaviṣayatvād ārtha iti vyākhyeyam / dhṛtavikāsīti pūrvaṃ kālaprakaraṇenodāhṛtam, saṃprati śābdaviṣayatvenodāhriyate, tiṅantagatatvenāpy ūhyate / (na hīyam?) ārthaḥ prakramabheda iti atrodāharaṇadvitayaṃ dattaṃ mattateti samatayeti / tatra mattatety atra saṅgamabhūṣety ārthena krameṇa prakramaḥ, bhūṣayatīty atra tu śābdarūpatayā pratinirdeśa ity ārthaḥ prakramabhedaḥ / kiṃ tu tadvapus tad api cārutaratvam iti pāṭhaḥ sthitaparipāṭhyānuguṇyābhāvān na nyāyyaḥ / "cārutā sa khalu sāpi śarīram" iti tu pāṭhaḥ śreyān / evaṃ ca dayitasaṅgatir eṣety etacchabdaḥ paṭhanīyaḥ, na punar āsām iti pāṭhaḥ / tatra hi mattatā kena śabdena parāmṛśyate / "samataye"ty etat prāyeṇādarśeṣu śābdaprakramabhede udāharaṇatayā dṛśyate / ārtha prakramabhedaprastāve (vā? ca) "anantarodāharaṇayor ādyam āhitaviparyayam" iti pāṭhaḥ / etac cāyuktaṃ yojanagranthe varuṇasyārthaprakrama iti granthavirodhāt / kiṃ tu niyamayann iti vidagdhamanyatayā datto 'pi no hṛdayaṅgamaḥ pāṭhaḥ, varuṇenaiva tat saṃbaddham ity atra pramāṇābhāvāt / na hi varuṇasyānyopasarjanatvena sthitasya svātantryam asti / tasya naivaṃvidhasaṃbandhaḥ puṣṭatvaṃ dhatte / ārthaprakramabhedaprastāve idam evodāharaṇam āhitaviparyayam iti pāṭhaḥ śreyān /

children.text: parihṛtau bhavata iti / vibhaktiprakramabhedacaśabdayor dvitvād dvivacanam / caśabdasyobhayathā duṣṭatā ca / caśabdasya ca samuccayo viṣayaḥ / tadbhāvaḥ (uktaḥ / yena tulyakakṣyatvābhāvākyatvena?) nivāritaḥ / prakramabhedas tv asatām ity asamuccetavyani
children.translated_text: "Have been avoided" (<s>parihṛtau bhavatah</s>) — the dual number is because there are two [items]: breach of case-ending sequence and the <s>ca</s>-particle ("and"). And the faultiness of the <s>ca</s>-particle is of both kinds. And the domain of the <s>ca</s>-particle is aggregation (<s>samuccaya</s>). Its being [an aggregate] is prevented (by the absence of equal status and sentencehood). But the breach of sequence is "of the non-existent ones" — meaning they should not be aggregated.

children.text: [Page 36]
children.translated_text: [Page 36]

children.text: kaṭaprayogāt / sa hi "niyamanād" ity asyānantaraṃ paṭhanīyaḥ / loṣṭasaṃcāra ekaikasya bhedasya bhedāntaraiḥ saha saṃyojanaprakārākhyo gaṇanāviśeṣaḥ / prakṛtipratyayayor iti laghuśabdaḥ prakṛtiḥ / tasyāṃ guruśabdena bhedaḥ / guruśabde ceyasunn adhikaḥ prayukto, yo laghuśabde na prayuktaḥ / tatpratyayasya ca pratinirdeśo na kṛta iti pratyayaprakramabhedo 'pi / abhinavapāṭhe tu tatpratyayarahitasyaiva laghuśabdasya pratinirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ / krameti ya uddeśakramaḥ prakrāntaḥ, so 'nudeśe vaiparītyād na kṛta iti pratīter aikyasya vigamād duṣṭatvam / tava kusumaśaratvam iti / idaṃ kramaprakramabhedodāharaṇaṃ na yuktaṃ cūlikākramasyaivātrocitatvam / tathā hy uddeśaḥ / smaraṃ prati sāṃmukhyenābhidhānaṃ vihāya nenduṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ pratyayathārthajñānam ucitam iti smarasya tāvat prathamanirdeśo nyāyyaḥ / (anirdeśe)
children.translated_text: Because of the usage of <s>kaṭa</s> (mat). For that should be read immediately after "because of restriction" (<s>niyamanāt</s>). <s>Loṣṭasaṃcāra</s> (movement of clods) is the particular mode of enumeration called the manner of combining each individual variety with other varieties. "Of base and suffix" (<s>prakṛtipratyayayoḥ</s>) — the short word (<s>laghu</s>) is the base; in it, a variety is [introduced] by the heavy word (<s>guru</s>). And in the heavy word, <s>iyasuṇ</s> is additional.

children.text: ⟨anudeśe conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>anudeśe</s> (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: tv idaṃ viṣayaṃ tyaktvā na prāsaṅgikena vākyārthaparisamāptiḥ śobhate iti pāryavasānikena smareṇaiva saṃmukhīkriyamāṇena vākyārthaḥ parisamapanīya iti pāṭhakramāpekṣayā cūlikākrama eva sahṛdayahṛdayarañjaka iti kuśāgrīyadhiṣaṇair nipuṇaṃ nirūpaṇīyam etat / tathā ca "yuṣmadasmadoḥ padasya padāt ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vānnāvau" (PS_8,1.20) iti cūlikākrameṇa vyavahāro dṛśyate / kramaprakramabhedasya punar udāharaṇaṃ vastuprakramabhedavicāraprastāve nirūpayiṣyate / pradhānabhūtasyety arthapratipādanāya śabdaprayogāc chabdasyopāyamātratvād upāyānāṃ ca niyamābhāvāt / tad uktaṃ -
children.translated_text: However, abandoning this domain, the completion of sentence-meaning by an incidental [element] is not elegant — rather, the sentence-meaning should be completed by the concluding remembrance alone, being directly presented. And with regard to the reading-order, the <s>cūlikā</s>-order (epilogue-order) alone is delightful to the hearts of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) — this should be carefully examined by those of the sharpest intellect.

body.translated_text: Here, even though in <s>agṛdhnuḥ</s> (without greed) the suffix expressing habitual disposition etc. is used, in <s>atrastaḥ</s> (fearless), the non-use of <s>atrasnuḥ</s> is not faulty — or, [even] if <s>atrasnuḥ</s> were specified, <s>agṛdhnuḥ</s> is entirely faultless. The result-bearing quality of the agent is the intention of the agent (<s>kartrabhiprāyatva</s>). And that too is merely a matter of the speaker's intention. And thus, in "having been seen, she casts her gaze downward; when addressed, she does not engage in conversation" — if the fruit of the action is intended from the agent's perspective, then the use of the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) in <s>dadāti</s> (gives) would be inappropriate. If not, then in <s>kurute</s> (does, middle voice), the <s>parasmaipada</s> would apply — thus the objection of breach of sequence is entirely without scope. Similarly, this should be understood elsewhere. "Therefore those" (<s>tena te</s>) — "those" refers to the particular [aspects of] time etc.; "therefore" means: because they are motivated by the speaker's intention, they have not been shown — this is the meaning. Regarding <s>gāhantām</s> (let them dive) — here, the expression of the agent by the finite verb and the non-expression of the object have been initiated; [but] <s>visrabdhaiḥ</s> (by the confident ones) has altered it — thus there is a breach of <s>kāraka</s>-sequence (case-relation sequence). <s>Vihṛti</s> means roaming, meaning being a receptacle of playfulness — this is the meaning. In the reading <s>vivṛtam</s>, the meaning is: possessing extensiveness. In love (<s>ratau</s>), conflict (<s>vigrahaḥ</s>) means opposition; interrupted by thunderings (<s>stanitaiḥ</s>); through its grace, because the opposition cannot be brought about. <s>Vitene</s> — the suffix is in the abstract sense. The meaning is: the thunderings have become extended. "Verbal breach of sequence" (<s>śābdaḥ prakramabhedaḥ</s>) — it is verbal because its domain is language. But regarding those who read "verbal breach of sequence" as a continuous heading for the subsequent text following "breach of base-sequence" — they have not examined the subsequent verbal and semantic text — so this should be disregarded.

children.text: "upādāyāpi ye heyās tān upāyān pracakṣate /
children.translated_text: "Even those means which, though adopted, are to be abandoned — they are called expedients (<s>upāyas</s>);

children.text: upāyānāṃ ca niyamo nāvaśyam avakalpate //"
children.translated_text: and a restriction upon the means does not necessarily obtain."

body.text: iti / prakramabheda iti / prakramabhedaviṣayasya vidhyanuvādabhāvaprakāratvāt prakramabhedo 'py upacārād vidhyanuvādaprakāra ity arthaḥ / anenaiva nyāyena śābdaś cārthaś ceti prakramabhedasya bhedadvayaṃ śābdārthaviṣayatvād boddhavyam / śabdabhedam iti / ekaśabdā(bhedatvā?)bhidheyatvenārthasya pratyabhijñāyamānatvopapattaye / śabdabhede tasyaivārthasyānyasyeva pratīteḥ nāñjasena prakāreṇa vidhyanuvādabhāvaviṣayatvam / kāvyagatatvena hi cintā prastutā / na ca kāvye śāstrādivad arthapratītyarthaṃ śabdamātraṃ prayujyate, sahitayoḥ śabdārthayos tatra prayogāt / sāhityaṃ tulyakakṣyatvenānyūnānatiriktatvam / astv evam iti sāmānyena prakramabhedābhyupagamo viśeṣe tu paryanuyoga iti bhāvaḥ / prakrama(bheda?)niyamaṃ pratīti hṛdayaṅgamaḥ pāṭhaḥ / yadbhedābhedābhyām iti hi yacchabdena prakramaḥ parāmṛśyate / prakramabhedaniyamaṃ pratīti tu pāṭhe yadbhedābhedābhyām iti prakramasyaivoddhṛtasya yathākathaṃ cit parāmarśo vyākhyeyaḥ /

children.text: śuci bhūṣayatīti / atra bhūṣayatīti śābdaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ prakrāntam alaṅkriyetyādāv ārthena rūpeṇa pratinirdiṣṭam / atra ca paryāyaprakramabhedaḥ sthito 'pi sāṃprataṃ na cintitaḥ śabdārthaprakramabhedacintanaprastāvāt / atra vibhāgasyaiveti / (atra vety arthād upameyam?) tadabhisaṃbandhaḥ śabdābhisaṃbandhaḥ / viparyayād iti sākṣāc chabdasaṃbandhābhāvāt / udāharaṇadvaye "śuci bhūṣayati" iti "cārutā vapur" iti ca / yādṛśam iti sthitapāṭhābhiprāyeṇānaucityaṃ dattapāṭhāśayena tv aucityam ity arthaḥ / tacchabdenānye parāmṛśyante / sādṛśyam eveti / (tadā yacchabdasya napuṃsakatā syāt / tasmāt surārivety atra parāmṛśyata iti?) avivekākṣamaprajñatvāt / tadapahṛteti bhaṅgibhaṇitivaicitryaṃ parāmṛṣṭam / utkaṭena bhaṇitivaicitryeṇa varṇanīyam ācchāditam ity arthaḥ / tad uktaṃ vakroktikṛtā laukikālaṅkārān upamānīkṛtya
children.translated_text: '<s>Śuci bhūṣayati</s>' (it adorns what is pure): here '<s>bhūṣayati</s>' (adorns) is the verbal ornament that has been introduced; in '<s>alaṅkriyate</s>' (is ornamented) and the like, it is reciprocally indicated in a semantic form. Here the <s>paryāyaprakramabheda</s> (synonym-sequence-breach), though present, is not considered now, since the occasion is for considering the breach of sequence in word and meaning. '<s>Atra vibhāgasyaiva</s>': (here, the object of comparison is [to be inferred]?) its connection is the verbal connection. 'By reversal' means because of the absence of direct verbal connection. In the two examples: '<s>śuci bhūṣayati</s>' and '<s>cārutā vapuḥ</s>.' '<s>Yādṛśam</s>': with the intention of the established reading there is inappropriateness; but with the intention of the emended reading there is appropriateness—that is the meaning. 'By the <s>tat</s>-word, others are referred to.' '<s>Sādṛśyam eva</s>': (then the <s>yat</s>-word would be neuter. Therefore, in '<s>surāri</s>' etc., it is [<s>Murāri</s>] who is referred to?) Because of the inability to discriminate due to lack of wisdom. '<s>Tadapahṛta</s>': the variety of modes of expression (<s>bhaṅgibhaṇitivaicitrya</s>) is referred to; the meaning is that by a striking variety of expression, what is to be described is covered over. As stated by the author of the <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> (<s>Kuntaka</s>), taking the worldly ornaments as objects of comparison,

body.translated_text: Thus. "Breach of sequence" (<s>prakramabheda</s>) — since the subject-domain of breach of sequence has the nature of injunction, predication, and mode, breach of sequence too is, by figurative extension (<s>upacāra</s>), of the nature of injunction, predication, and mode — this is the meaning. By this very principle, the two varieties of breach of sequence — "verbal and semantic" — should be understood as having verbal and semantic domains respectively. The verbal variety —

children.translated_text: [Page 37]

children.text: "yadvat tadvad alaṅkārair bhāsamānair nijātmanā /
children.translated_text: "Just as by ornaments that shine with their own inherent brilliance,

children.text: svaśobhātiśayāntastham alaṅkāryaṃ prakāśyate //"
children.translated_text: the object to be ornamented, which contains within it a surplus of its own beauty, is revealed."

body.text: iti / aprādhānyaṃ

children.text: ⟨aprādhānyaṃ conj (Ed): prādhānyaṃ na syād⟩
children.translated_text: ⟨'<s>aprādhānyaṃ</s>' conj. (Ed.): '<s>prādhānyaṃ na syāt</s>' [would not be primary]⟩

children.text: syād iti / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - yadi śabdavyāpāraviṣayasya prādhānyam arthavyāpāraviṣayasya cāprādhānyam iti vyavasthā, tadā trividhasya pratīyamānasya parair dhvanyatvena vyapa(nirdi)diṣṭasyāsmābhir anumeyatvenopapāditasyāprādhānyaṃ prasajyeta tasyārthavyāpāraviṣayatvāt, śabdavyāpāraviṣayatvasya dūṣitatvāt / iṣyate ca prādhānyam / tat katham iyaṃ prādhānyāprādhānyapratītir ghaṭata iti / "cakrābhighāte"tyādau ca paryāyokte samāsoktivad gamyamānasyaiva prādhānyaṃ na vācyasyety upapāditaṃ prāk / "ekābhighāta" iti hayagrīvavadhe pāṭhaḥ sthitaḥ, sudarśanasya pulliṅgasya prakrāntatvād ya ity anena parāmarśāt / tat tv anavabudhya cakraṃ yadi parāmṛśyate, tadā yacchabdasya napuṃsakatā syāt / tan murārir evātra parāmṛśyata ity āśayena "cakrābhighāte"ti paṭhanti / na tv ayaṃ tatra prastāvaḥ / (tadapekṣayaiva?) prādhānyam aprādhānyaṃ ceti iha gamakam apradhānam upāyatvāt / gamyaṃ pradhānam upeyatvāt / tena pratīyamānasya gamyatvāt prādhānyavyavahāraḥ / na pratītyapekṣayeti / śabdenārthena ca yā pratītis, tadapekṣayā na prādhānyāprādhānyavyavahāra ity arthaḥ / tayas tv iha gamyagamakabhāvaviviktaviṣayatvena cintā kṛtā / tadapekṣayaiva ceti / vācyasyāpi yaḥ śābdatvena prādhānyavyavahārayogas tasyāpi / tadapekṣayā gamyagamakatvāpekṣayā / kva cid yatra pratīyamānasadbhāvas tatrāprādhānyam ity arthaḥ / vācyaṃ hi pratīyamānaṃ prati gamakatvena vyavasthitaṃ tena tadapekṣatvenāprādhānyam iti tātparyam / vicitrā bhaṅgibhiṇitaya
children.translated_text: The purport is this: if the established principle is that what falls within the scope of verbal function is primary and what falls within the scope of meaning-function is non-primary, then the three-fold <s>pratīyamāna</s> (suggested meaning), which others have designated as <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) and which we have demonstrated to be <s>anumeya</s> (inferable), would be rendered non-primary—since it falls within the scope of meaning-function, and since its being within the scope of verbal function has been refuted. Yet its primacy is accepted. So how does this understanding of primacy and non-primacy hold together? And in '<s>cakrābhighāte</s>' (at the blow of the discus) and the like, it was previously demonstrated—as in <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression)—that the primacy belongs to the suggested meaning alone, not the expressed. In '<s>ekābhighāta</s>' (single blow), the established reading is in the context of the slaying of <s>Hayagrīva</s>, since the masculine <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus] has been introduced, and is referred to by the [masculine] '<s>yaḥ</s>.' But without understanding this, if the discus is referred to, then the <s>yat</s>-word would have to be neuter. So with the intention that <s>Murāri</s> himself is referred to here, [some] read '<s>cakrābhighāte</s>.' But this is not the topic under discussion. With reference to that very [distinction], primacy and non-primacy [are determined] thus: here the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>) is non-primary, since it is the means; the indicated (<s>gamya</s>) is primary, since it is the end. Therefore, since the <s>pratīyamāna</s> (suggested meaning) is what is indicated, the designation of primacy [applies to it]. 'Not with reference to cognition': the meaning is that with reference to the cognition [produced] by word and meaning, the designation of primacy and non-primacy does not apply. Rather, here the investigation has been conducted with reference to the distinct domains of the indicated-indicator relationship. 'With reference to that very [relationship]': even the designation of primacy that the expressed meaning has by virtue of being verbal—that too, with reference to the indicated-indicator relationship—wherever the suggested meaning is present, [the expressed has] non-primacy. For the expressed meaning is established as an indicator in relation to the suggested, and therefore, being dependent upon it, [it has] non-primacy—that is the purport. '<s>Vicitrā bhaṅgibhiṇitayaḥ</s>' (various modes of expression):

body.translated_text: "A defect arising from lack of learning is concealed by the poet's power."

body.text: iti / vākyabhedāc ceti vākyāntarāpekṣayā hi vākyāntarasya bhaṅgibhaṇitivaicitryam ity aṃśena pratītivaidūryān na prakramabhedadoṣaṃ prakāśayati /

children.text: nyāyasiddhatvād iti / nyāyo 'tra bhaṇitivaiṣamyam / kāraṇabhedasyāpīti na kevalaṃ pratītibhedo bhedahetuḥ, yāvat kāraṇabhedo 'pi / pratītibhedo vijñaptyapekṣayā bhedahetuḥ, kāraṇabhedaḥ punar utpattyapekṣayeti viśeṣaḥ / tad uktam -
children.translated_text: 'Because it is established by reasoning': the reasoning here is the disparity of expression. '<s>Kāraṇabhedasyāpi</s>': not only is the difference of cognition a cause of distinction, but so too is the difference of cause. The difference of cognition is a cause of distinction with reference to notification, while the difference of cause [is such] with reference to origination—this is the distinction. As stated:

body.translated_text: 'And because of the separation of sentences': for with reference to another sentence, the variety of modes of expression in that other sentence is such that, in that respect, due to the distance of cognition, it does not manifest the defect of <s>prakramabheda</s> (breach of sequence).

body.text: "ayam eva bhedo bhedahetur vā bhāvānāṃ yo 'yaṃ viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇabhedaś ca"
body.translated_text: "This very difference, or the cause of difference among entities, is this superimposition of contradictory properties and the difference of causes."

body.text: iti / iha bhaṅgibhaṇitivaicitryāvaicitrye pratītipariskhalanāskhalanayoḥ kāraṇe / sa ceti prakramabhedaḥ / śābdaś cārthaś ceti pūrvaṃ prakṛtyādiprakramabhedavilakṣaṇau śābdārthaprakramabhedau lakṣitāv udāhṛtau ca / adhunā vācyapratīyamānārthāpekṣayā paryavasānābhiprāyeṇa sarvaprakramabhedavyāpakau sāmānyena śābdārthaprakramabhedāv uktāv iti viśeṣo boddhavyaḥ / vastuprakramabheda iti / vastu varṇanīyaṃ yathā varṇayituṃ prakrāntaṃ tasya tathā nirvāhābhāvād vastuprakramabhedaḥ / bhedeneti avayavasaṃbandhitvenety arthaḥ / prathame hi pāde avayavina eva svarūpeṇa varṇanaṃ prakrāntam ity avayavisaṃbandhitvena nirvāhaṇaṃ doṣaḥ / ubhayatrāpīti avayavivarṇane avayavavarṇane ca / tat svarūpaṃ nāyikāsvarūpam / aṅgena ity āmantraṇam / patatu adhastāt gacchatu / sādṛśyapratipādaneti dvicandram iti hi pāṭhe vadanena saha candro nabhaso dvicandratām āpādayati / tac ca vadanacandrayoḥ sādṛśyamūlam iti vyatirekaprakrame sādṛśyanirvāhāt prakramabhedaḥ / vastusargapaunaruktyasyeti punaruktavastuvirasa ity atra hi punaruktavastubhir virasa iti vyākhyāne sādṛśyena nirvāhaḥ kṛtaḥ / vyatirekeṇa ca prakrama iti doṣa evāyam

children.text: vimukha iti / ke cit punaruktavastuṣu virasaḥ punaruktāni vastūni (na) karotīti vyākhyānena vyatirekanirvāhād yathāsthitapāṭhaṃ samarthayāṃ cakre / arthadoṣāṇām iti prakramātikramarūpāṇām ity arthaḥ / tapena varṣā iti
children.translated_text: '<s>Vimukha</s>' (averse). Some, by the explanation 'weary with respect to repeated things, [meaning] he does not create repeated things,' supporting the established reading through completion by contrast, argued [for the absence of defect]. '<s>Arthadoṣāṇām</s>' means those having the form of transgression of sequence. '<s>Tapena varṣāḥ</s>':

body.translated_text: Here the variety and non-variety of modes of expression are the causes of the stumbling and non-stumbling of cognition. '<s>Sa ca</s>' refers to <s>prakramabheda</s>. '<s>Śābdaś cārthaś ca</s>': previously, the verbal and semantic <s>prakramabhedas</s>, distinct from <s>prakṛti</s> (stem) and similar [linguistic] <s>prakramabhedas</s>, were characterized and illustrated. Now, with reference to expressed and suggested meaning, with a conclusive intention, the verbal and semantic <s>prakramabhedas</s> are stated generally as pervading all [types of] <s>prakramabheda</s>—this distinction should be understood. '<s>Vastuprakramabheda</s>' (breach of subject-sequence): the <s>vastu</s> (subject matter) that is to be described, [when] the manner in which it was begun to be described is not carried through—that is <s>vastuprakramabheda</s>. '<s>Bhedena</s>' means by connection with parts (<s>avayava</s>). For in the first <s>pāda</s> (verse-quarter), the description of the whole in its own form was commenced, so completing it by connection with parts is a defect. '<s>Ubhayatrāpi</s>' means in both the description of the whole and the description of parts. '<s>Tat svarūpam</s>' is the form of the heroine. '<s>Aṅgena</s>' is a vocative. '<s>Patatu</s>': let it fall, let it go below. '<s>Sādṛśyapratipādana</s>': for in the reading '<s>dvicandram</s>' (two moons), the moon together with the face produces a state of two moons in the sky; and that is based on the similarity of the face and the moon; so when completion is through similarity in a context where <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) was introduced, there is <s>prakramabheda</s>. '<s>Vastusargapaunaruktyasya</s>': for in '<s>punaruktavastuvirasaḥ</s>' ('one who is weary of repeated things'), when explained as 'weary by reason of repeated things,' the completion is through similarity; but the sequence was through contrast, so this is indeed a defect—

children.text: "tapena varṣāḥ śaradā himāgamo, vasantalakṣmyā śiśiraḥ sametya ca /
children.translated_text: "Summer with the Rains, Autumn with the onset of Winter, Spring's beauty with the Cool season, having come together,

children.text: prasūnakṛtyaṃ dadataḥ sadartavaḥ pure 'sya vāstavyakuḍumbitāṃ dadhuḥ //"
children.translated_text: the seasons, performing the work of flowers, bestowed upon the residents of his city the status of householders."

body.text: atra hi strīpuruṣayugalatrayarūpatayā ṛtūnāṃ varṇane prastute strīrūpāṇām ṛtunāṃ tṛtīyāsaṃbandhād aprādhānye vivakṣite yat tapena varṣā ity atra viparyayaḥ kṛtaḥ, kṛte vā tathā nirdeśe śaradā himāgama ityādau yad anyathākaraṇaṃ, sa prakramabheda eva / yadi paraṃ strīpuṃsayor atra yena krameṇa prakramaḥ tasyānyathā nirvāhāt kramaprakramabhedam imaṃ vidmaḥ / tena pūrvaṃ kramaprakramabhedasyedam evodāharaṇaṃ deyam / tena varaṃ "ghanaśriyoṣṇaḥ śaradā himāgamaḥ" iti pāṭhaḥ kartavyaḥ / kartṛprakramabhedo 'pīti / yatra yuṣmadasmadarthagataṃ kartṛtvaṃ śeṣe 'tra cetane 'cetane vā vaktrā buddhipūrvakam evāropyate, tatra kartur anyasyāropaś cārutvāya vyatyāso guṇa evety arthaḥ /

children.text: tayor iti / (yatra?) kartṛvyatyāsaprakramabhedayoḥ / na prakaraṇāvasita iti / yuṣmadasmadarthasya hi kva cit kartṛtvaṃ prakaraṇādyavasitaṃ na śabdenābhidhātuṃ prakrāntam iti nāyaṃ prakramabhedadoṣasya viṣayaḥ / anyatrāropyaivam uktam iti śeṣatvena vivakṣite rāmabhadre / evam uttaratra bhārgave vaṭau cānyatvaṃ yojanīyam / nanu yuṣmadasmadarthasya cetanatvāt tadapekṣayācetanasyaivānyatvam ucitam iti kathaṃ cetanasyaivānyatvam ity āha - dvividho hīti / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ / na yuṣmadasmadarthagatacetanatvāpekṣayā vastvantarasyānyatvam, api tu yuṣmadasmadarthatvāpekṣayaiva / yuṣmadasmadarthau ca kramāt saṃbodhyamānavastuniṣṭhaḥ parabhāvo 'smitākhyā pratyaktā ca / tataś ca tadapekṣayā śeṣasyānyatvam / tasya ca cetanatvācetanatvād dvaividhyam iti na virodhaḥ kaś cit / paraśunā candrahāsa iti krameṇa dvayor api yuṣmadasmadarthayor acetanaviṣayakartṛtāvyatyāsa udāharaṇam / bho laṅkeśvara iti / atra rāmaḥ svayaṃ yācata iti asmadarthakartṛtvasya cetanaviṣayavyatyāsasyānyat sthitam apy udāharaṇīyaṃ na cintitaṃ, pūrvam udāharaṇāntare cintitatvāt, cintāntaraprastāvāc ca /
children.translated_text: 'Of those two' — of the two [types], namely agent-transposition and sequence-disruption (<s>prakramabheda</s>). 'Not ascertained from context' — for the agent-status of the second-person/first-person referent is sometimes ascertained from context, not introduced verbally — so this is not the domain of the fault of sequence-disruption. 'Elsewhere, it is stated with superimposition' — regarding <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, who is intended as subordinate. Similarly, in the subsequent [examples], the otherness should be construed for <s>Bhārgava</s> and the banyan tree. Now, since the second-person/first-person referent is sentient, it would be proper for only the non-sentient to be 'other' in relation to it — so how is the sentient itself 'other'? He says: 'for it is twofold.' The meaning is this: the otherness of another entity is not in relation to the sentience belonging to the second-person/first-person referent, but only in relation to being the second-person/first-person referent [itself]. And the second-person/first-person referents are, respectively, the state of being the other (<s>parabhāva</s>), established in the thing being addressed, and the sense of self (<s>asmitā</s>), which is subjective. And therefore, the rest is 'other' in relation to that. And its twofold [nature] arises from [its being either] sentient or non-sentient — so there is no contradiction. '<s>Paraśunā candrahāsa</s>' (with the axe Candrahāsa) is an example of agent-transposition with a non-sentient referent for both the second-person and first-person referents in order. '<s>Bho Laṅkeśvara</s>' (O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>) — here, although another illustration of sentient-domain transposition, where <s>Rāma</s> himself requests (a first-person-referent agent-status), exists to be cited, it is not considered, because it was considered earlier in another example, and because the occasion calls for a different consideration.

body.translated_text: Here, when the description of the seasons in the form of three couples of man and woman was commenced, with the female-form seasons intended as non-primary due to their third-case (instrumental) connection—the reversal in '<s>tapena varṣāḥ</s>' (Summer with Rains [feminine first]) is [a defect]; or, given that such a designation was made, the alteration in '<s>śaradā himāgamaḥ</s>' (Autumn [fem.] with Winter [masc.]) and so on constitutes <s>prakramabheda</s> itself. If, however, we recognize this as <s>kramaprakramabheda</s> (breach of order-sequence) because the sequence in which male and female were introduced is not maintained—then this very [verse] should be given as the example of <s>kramaprakramabheda</s> stated earlier. Therefore the better reading would be '<s>ghanaśriyoṣṇaḥ śaradā himāgamaḥ</s>' ('the hot season with the beauty of clouds, Autumn with Winter'). '<s>Kartṛprakramabhedo 'pi</s>' (breach of agent-sequence too): where agency belonging to the second and first persons is deliberately superimposed by the speaker on the remaining [third person], whether animate or inanimate—there the transference of agency to another is a virtue, for the sake of beauty—that is the meaning.

body.text: tad evam iyatā prabandhena prakramabhedaṃ vicārya kramaprāptaṃ kramabhedaṃ vicārayitum āha kramebhedo yatheti / nanu yadi smṛtiparāmarśakasya tacchabdasyānubhūta evārtho viṣaya ity ucyate, ye 'tyantaparokṣā rāmādayas teṣāṃ kavinā kāvye tacchabdena kathaṃ parāmarśaḥ kriyate teṣām atīndriyatvād ity āha

children.text: atra ca pratītimātram iti / ayam atrābhiprāyaḥ / yena vinā yan nopapadyate, tasya tadapekṣā nyāyyā / smṛtiś ca pratītimātram antareṇānupapadyamānā tadapekṣiṇī syāt, naindriyikapratītyapekṣiṇī aindriyakapratītiṃ vināpi śabdādibhyaḥ pratītau tasyāḥ saṃbhavadarśanāt / rāmādīnāṃ ca yadi naindriyikī pratītis tadā śabdāt prasiddher vā pratītir astu / tannibandhanaś ca smṛtiparāmarśakena tacchabdena parāmarśa iti na kaś cid virodhaḥ / nanv iti / ayam atrārthaḥ / padārthavimarśapurassaro vākyārthavimarśa iti na padārthavimarśavelāyāṃ bhavatv iyam āśaṅkā / vākyārthavimarśasamaye tv akhaṇḍapratītau pūrvāparabhāvaniyamāvabhāsanābhāvān nāsya doṣasyāvakāśaḥ / uddeśyatvāc ca vākyārthapratīter antaraṅgatvam iti tadāśrayeṇaiva vyavasthopapattau na kramadoṣacintā kā cid iti / pratirūpaḥ pratibimbarūpaḥ tatsaṃcāro vaktrabhiprāyasaṃkramaṇam / śabdavyavahārasyeti / śabdavyavahāramukhena śrotṛgṛhīto vākyārthavimarśaḥ svīkṛtaḥ / vaktur iti yadi śortṛvimarśaparyavasāyī śabdavyavahāro vaktṛvimarśapraticchandakarūpo na syāt, tadā śabdair vaktṛvimarśasyāsaṃbandhitvād anumānaṃ na syād ity arthaḥ / tatra cāsā
children.translated_text: 'Here, mere cognition' — the intent here is this: that without which something is not possible properly has a justified expectation of that [thing]. And memory (<s>smṛti</s>), being impossible without mere cognition, would be dependent on it — not dependent on sensory cognition, because memory is seen to be possible even without sensory cognition, from words etc. And if the cognition of <s>Rāma</s> etc. is not sensory, then let the cognition arise from words or from common knowledge — and based on that, reference by the '<s>tat</s>'-word, which refers to what is remembered, is made — so there is no contradiction. 'But' (<s>nanu</s>) — the meaning here is this: the examination of sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthavimarśa</s>) is preceded by the examination of word-meanings (<s>padārthavimarśa</s>) — so let this objection arise at the stage of word-meaning examination. But at the time of sentence-meaning examination, in the undivided cognition, since there is no appearance of a fixed order of prior and posterior cognitions, there is no scope for this fault. And because sentence-meaning cognition is the intended [goal], it is the more intimate — and since the [correct] determination is established on that basis alone, there is no concern about the fault of sequence whatsoever. '<s>Pratirūpa</s>' means having the form of a reflection; 'its transmission' (<s>tatsaṃcāra</s>) means the transfer [from the speaker's] to [the hearer's] mind. 'Of verbal usage' — the sentence-meaning examination grasped by the hearer through verbal usage is accepted. 'Of the speaker' — if the verbal usage, which culminates in the hearer's examination, were not a replica of the speaker's examination, then because of the words' non-relatedness to the speaker's examination, inference would not be possible — such is the meaning. And in that case,

children.text: v iti vaktṛśrotṛgate vākyārthavimarśe sūkṣmatvenāsphuṭarūpo 'sty eva paurvāparyapratibhāsa iti yāvat / padārthabuddhāv iti vākyārthapūrvabhāsinyām / tatrāpīti / vaktṛśrotṛgatavākyārthavimarśe 'pi sūkṣmaḥ padārthāśrayo doṣo durnivāraḥ padārthān atikrameṇaiva vākyārthavimarśasya vyavasthitatvād ity arthaḥ / pramādaja iti / evaṃ sati pra(kramyyamāna++)
children.translated_text: 'that' — in the sentence-meaning examination occurring in both speaker and hearer, there is indeed, in subtle form, an indistinct appearance of sequential order — this is the meaning. 'In the word-meaning cognition' — in that which precedes the sentence-meaning. 'There too' — even in the sentence-meaning examination of both speaker and hearer, the subtle fault based on word-meanings is hard to prevent, because the sentence-meaning examination is established only through transcending word-meanings — such is the meaning. 'Born of carelessness' — this being the case, the fault of reference to what is [to be presented next]
