children.translated_text: [Editorial conjecture: 'the thing to be presented next']

children.text: parāmarśadoṣas tāvat parigṛhītā bhavati / pratīpagamanahetor iti gajasetubandhād ity asya / śābdasyeti pañcamyantatvāt / tadīyatīrthābhidhāneti hetuhetumatos tadīyatīrthaśabdena vyavadhāne satīty arthaḥ / gaṅgāviśeṣaṇamukheneti gajasetubandhām iti pāṭhe / ayam atrāśayaḥ - śābdo yatra hetuhetumadbhāvas tatra hetutvenāpanyāsān na tayor vyavadhānaṃ kiṃ cit kāryam, pratītiviprakarṣaprasaṅgāt / ārthe hetuhetumadbhāve upanyastasya hetutvād viśeṣaṇabhūtasya hetor viśeṣyasvarūpavarṇanena caritārthatvāt saty api vyavadhāne na pratītiviprakarṣaḥ kaś cit, paryālocanasāmarthyād dhetutvapratīteḥ / atra ca śloke tīrthe tadīye iti padadvayākaraṇe 'pi vākyārthasya nirākāṅkṣtvāt tatkaraṇam apuṣṭārtham eva / tadeti tacchabdena / (iti tacchabdaḥ?) āropanivṛttāv iti āropo bhramo 'nyasyānyatvena pratītiḥ, yathā navajaladharasya sannaddhadṛptiniśācaratvena / tannivṛttāv atra vakṣyamānāyām āropaviṣayasya jaladharāder vastusataḥ prakāśamānasyedamādinā nyāyye nirdeśe tasya parāmṛśyasamīpa eva prayogeṇa bhāvyam / yas tv avastusadāropyamāṇanikaṭe prayogaḥ sa kramabhedam āvahati / yas tv atraivāropaviṣayasvarūpatayā vidyuto nikaṭa idam ādyaprayogaḥ, tatra dūṣaṇāntarāvakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: is thereby accepted. 'Because of the cause of retrograde movement' — meaning because of the 'elephant-bridge' [construction]. 'Verbal' — because it ends in the fifth case [ablative]. 'By the designation of his sacred bathing place' — the meaning is: when there is intervention with the word '<s>tadīyatīrtha</s>' (his sacred bathing place), between cause and effect. 'By way of qualifying the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' — in the reading '<s>gajasetubandhām</s>.' The intent here is this: where the cause-effect relationship is verbal, because [the cause] is presented as the cause, no intervention between the two should be made, since there would be an over-extension of the distance in cognition. In a semantic cause-effect relationship, because the presented cause, being a qualifier, has its purpose fulfilled by the description of the nature of the qualified, even with intervention there is no distance in cognition whatsoever, because the cognition of causality [arises] from the power of reflection. And in this verse, even without making the two words '<s>tīrthe tadīye</s>' (in his sacred place), the sentence-meaning is free of expectation, so making them is without support. '<s>Tat</s>' — by the '<s>tat</s>'-word. 'When superimposition is removed' (<s>āropanivṛttau</s>) — superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) is an error, the cognition of one thing as another, as [the cognition] of a new rain-cloud as an armored arrogant night-demon. When that is removed, in the proper indication with '<s>idam</s>' etc. of the real thing that appears as the locus of superimposition — cloud etc. — the usage must be in the vicinity of the thing being referred to. But usage near the unreal superimposed [entity] causes a breach of order (<s>kramabheda</s>). And when the usage of '<s>idam</s>' etc. is near the lightning in its true nature as the locus of superimposition in this very [passage], there is scope for another fault.

body.translated_text: Thus, having examined sequence-disruption (<s>prakramabheda</s>) to this extent with this exposition, he says, in order to examine the next [topic], breach of order (<s>kramabheda</s>), which follows in sequence — '<s>kramabhedo yathā</s>' (breach of order is as follows). Now, if it is said that the '<s>tat</s>'-word, which refers to what is remembered, has as its domain only what has been [directly] experienced, how does the poet make reference with the '<s>tat</s>'-word in poetry to <s>Rāma</s> etc. who are utterly remote — since they are beyond the senses? He says —

children.translated_text: [Section 68]

children.text:
utkhātadrutam iva śailaṃ himahatakamalākaram iva lakṣmīvimuktam /
  pītamadiram iva caṣakaṃ bahulapradoṣam iva mugdhacandrarahitam //
children.translated_text:
'Like a mountain uprooted and set in motion, like a lotus-lake deprived of <s>Lakṣmī</s> by the snow,
like a drinking-cup whose wine has been drunk, like a dark evening without the naive moon.'

body.text: itīveti / atropalambharūpaḥ pūrvavākyārtha itiśabdāvacchinna utprekṣyata ity upālabdhety ataḥ pūrvam itīvaśabdau prayojyau / viṣayāntare tu prayogāt kramabhedaḥ / prāpipayiṣupadeneti pūrvavākyārthasthitena / tadadhīnatvaṃ puruṣāyattatvam / stambaram iti pīnonnatastanadvayadarśanād ayaṃ praśaṃsoktiḥ / ṣidgāḥ viṭāḥ / pratītivaicitryam iti vākyārthasya tilatuṇḍalīkṛtasyāvagamānavagamau / uktisvarūpeti / uktiḥ "stamberamaḥ pariṇinaṃsur asāv upaiti" ity eṣā / tasyā viṭasaṃbandhinyāḥ svarūpam itiśabdenopalakṣaṇatvād evaṃśabdādinā vyavacchettum iṣṭam / ataś ca tatra tasmād itiśabdād itiśabdopalakṣitād evamādayaś ca prāk pūrvam ukteḥ pūrvapradarśitāyāḥ / anyat kiṃ cit padaṃ ṣidga ityādi na kathanīyam ity arthaḥ / evam udāharaṇāntare 'pi yojanīyam /

children.translated_text: [Section 69]

children.text: upādhibhāvād iti itiśabdasya svā śaktiḥ pūrvavākyāvacchedarūpā / tāṃ pūrvatra vākye samarpayaṃs tasyopādhir itiśabdaḥ saṃpadyate / ataś ca na tasyānyatra prayogaḥ karttavya ity arthaḥ / padasyānyasyeti ṣidgair ityādeḥ / anyatheti (viparyayāntaraprayoge?)
children.translated_text: 'Because of being a limiting condition' (<s>upādhibhāvāt</s>) — the '<s>iti</s>'-word's inherent power is the form of delimiting the prior sentence. Delivering that [power] to the prior sentence, the '<s>iti</s>'-word becomes a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>). And therefore it should not be used elsewhere — such is the meaning. 'Of another word' — such as '<s>ṣidgaiḥ</s>' (by libertines) etc. 'Otherwise' — in the use of a different domain,

children.text: ⟨viṣayāntaraprayoge conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [Editorial conjecture: 'in the use of a different domain']

children.text: āsamañjasyaṃ viśarārupratītitvam / ānantaryaniyama iti
children.translated_text: there is inconsistency, i.e., confused cognition. 'The rule of contiguity' (<s>ānantaryaniyama</s>) —

body.translated_text: '<s>Iti-iva</s>' — here the prior sentence-meaning, which has the form of a reproach, being delimited by the word '<s>iti</s>,' is the object of poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>) — therefore '<s>iti</s>' [meaning 'thus thinking'] and '<s>iva</s>' (as if) should be employed before '<s>upālabdha</s>' (reproached). But because of their use in a different referential domain, there is a breach of order. 'With the word that wishes to cause [her] to drink' — by the [word] standing in the prior sentence-meaning. 'Dependence on that' means dependence on a person. '<s>Stambera</s>' — from seeing the pair of plump, upraised breasts, this is a statement of praise. '<s>Ṣidgāḥ</s>' means libertines. 'Variety of cognition' — the understanding and non-understanding of the sentence-meaning compressed like a sesame-ball. 'The nature of the statement' — the statement is '<s>stamberamaḥ pariṇinaṃsur asāv upaiti</s>' (that one approaches desiring to embrace the large-breasted woman). Its nature, as related to the libertine — because the '<s>iti</s>'-word serves as an indicator — is intended to be distinguished by '<s>evam</s>' etc. And therefore, from that '<s>iti</s>'-word, indicated by the '<s>iti</s>'-word, '<s>evam</s>'-beginning [words] etc. [should come] before, prior to, the previously shown statement. No other word, such as '<s>ṣidga</s>' etc., should be stated — such is the meaning. The same should be construed in other examples too.

children.text: "yasya yenābhisaṃbandhā dūrasthasyāpi tena saḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who has a connection with something — even if distant, by that [connection he is near];'

children.text: arthato hy asamānānām ānantaryam akāraṇam //"
children.translated_text: 'For the contiguity of things that are semantically dissimilar is not a cause [of connection].'

body.text: iti nyāyenārthaucityavaśād vyavahitānām apy ānantaryaniyamo bhaviṣyatīty arthaḥ / anyatas tarhīti / anyato 'rthaucityavaśāt / tatkāryasiddheḥ ityādikarttavyasiddheḥ / iti teṣāṃ prayogo niyataḥ syād ity uktam / nanu "yasya yenābhisaṃban(dho nyāyyaḥ?) kutrāvatiṣṭhatām" ity āha kaiś cid eveti /

children.text: [Page 40]
children.translated_text: [Page 40]

children.text: ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - ityādiśabdavarjanenoktakrameṇa śabdahetvādivarjanena cānyeṣāṃ śabdānām ayaṃ nyāyaḥ / ityādīnām ayaṃ punar niyataprayogaviṣaya iti / nānyathā teṣāṃ prayogaḥ karttavya iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: for other words, excluding the '<s>iti</s>'-word etc., and excluding verbal causality etc., this principle [of free placement according to semantic fitness] applies, as stated in the given order. But for '<s>iti</s>' etc., this is the domain of fixed usage — they should not be used otherwise.

body.translated_text: By this principle, even for things that are [textually] separated, the rule of contiguity will [apply] by force of semantic fitness (<s>arthaucitya</s>) — such is the meaning. 'Then from another [source]' — from another [source], by force of semantic fitness. 'Because that purpose is accomplished' — because of the accomplishment of what needs to be done. 'Thus their usage would be fixed' — this has been stated. Now, 'where does the principle that one should be connected with whatever is appropriate stand?' — he says: 'by some [authorities] indeed.'

body.text: evam uddeśakrameṇa kramabhedaṃ vimṛśya paunaruktyaṃ vicārayitum āha paunaruktyam iti / iha khalu dvividhaṃ paunaruktyaṃ śabdapaunaruktyam arthapaunaruktyaṃ ceti / tad uktam akṣpādamuninā - "śabdārthayoḥ punarvacana[ṃ] punaruktam anyatrānuvādād" iti / tatra śabdapaunaruktyam arthāpaunaruktye na doṣaḥ, arthapaunaruktyena duṣṭatva[ṃ] arthasyaiva prayojakatvāt / arthapaunaruktyam evaikaṃ paunaruktyaṃ na śabdapaunaruktyam iti samudāyārthaḥ / ārtham iti arthāśritam / evaṃ śābdam ity atrāpi vācyam / yad uktam iti vādanyāye / hasatīti eko hasatiśabdaḥ śatrantaḥ svāmiviśeṣaṇam, aparaḥ kriyāpadam / evam uttaratra vācyam / yantram iti / abhedopacāreṇa bhṛtyasya nirdeśaḥ kṛtānukāritvāt / anyatra tātparyabhedād iti tātparyabhede hi svarūpārthāviśeṣe lāṭānuprāsa iṣṭaḥ / tad uktaṃ -
body.translated_text: Having thus examined the distinction of sequence by the order of enumeration, [the author] says '<s>paunaruktya</s>' (repetition) in order to discuss repetition. Here indeed repetition is twofold: verbal repetition (<s>śabdapaunaruktya</s>) and semantic repetition (<s>arthapaunaruktya</s>). This has been stated by the sage <s>Akṣapāda</s> (<s>Gautama</s>): 'The re-statement of word or meaning is repetition, except in the case of reiteration (<s>anuvāda</s>).' There, verbal repetition without semantic repetition is not a fault, [but] faultiness through semantic repetition [arises] because meaning alone is the operative [factor]. The collective meaning is: only semantic repetition is [true] repetition, not verbal repetition. '<s>Ārtha</s>' means meaning-based. The same should be said regarding '<s>śābda</s>' (word-based). 'As stated' refers to the <s>Vādanyāya</s>. Regarding '<s>hasati</s>' — one '<s>hasati</s>'-word, ending in the <s>śatṛ</s> suffix, is a qualifier of the master; the other is a verb. The same should be said for what follows. Regarding '<s>yantra</s>' (instrument) — the servant is designated by a metaphor of non-difference, because he is one who acts as directed. 'Elsewhere, due to the distinction of purport' — for when there is a distinction of purport, the <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (a figure of speech involving repetition with different purport) is accepted when there is no difference in literal meaning. As stated —

children.text: "svarūpārthāviśeṣe hi punaruktiḥ phalāntarāt /
children.translated_text: "When there is no difference in the literal meaning, repetition [that gains significance] from a different result

children.text: śabdānāṃ vā padānāṃ vā lāṭānuprāsa iṣyate //"
children.translated_text: of words or of phrases is considered <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with different purport)."

body.text: iti / śakrasaṅkāśeti śrīnadīhaṃseti medinīcandreti vidviṣāṃ kāleti ca catvāryāmantraṇāṇi / atra tātparyabhedaḥ sphuṭa eva / tathā caikaḥ kāśaśabdo vastrāṇām upameyatvena sthitaḥ, anyas tu hasānām upamānatveneti bhinnaṃ tātparyam / evam anyad api yojanīyam / ubhayābhāve iti arthabhedasya tātparyabhedasya cābhāva ity arthaḥ / na ca ghāseti karmatvena saṃbandhitvena cāstu tātparyabheda ity arthaḥ / etan na ceti niṣidhyate / svārtham iti / etad uktaṃ bhavati - na svārthābhidhānam eva tātparyam, api tu saty eva svārthābhidhāne 'dhikam arthāntaronmukhatvaṃ tātparyaṃ, yathā kāśaśabdayoḥ / tatra kāśajātyavacchinnadravyapratipādanād atirikta upamānopameyabhāvaḥ pratipādyate / na caivaṃbisaśabdayoḥ / na hy atra bisajātyavacchinnadravyātiriktaṃ kiṃ cid vastu pratīyate / yat tu karmatvaṃ saṃbandhitvaṃ ca tadabhidheyasyaiva tathāvasthānaṃ nodrekeṇānyatām āvahatīti svaśabdaparihāreṇa sarvanāmaparāmarśasyaiva viṣayo nyāyya iti / nanu punaruktaṃ kim ucyate yatra tat prayogaṃ vinārthapratītiḥ yatra ca tatsamānapadāntaraprayogo 'vaśyam upayujyate, tatra kathaṃ punaruktatvam / yatraikārthena pratītir na tātparyabhedaḥ, tatra punaruktatvaṃ pratītivairasyāpādānāt / (yatra tu tatsthānena?)

children.text: ⟨yatra tu tat samānaṃ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: 'but where that is the same' (conjectured by the editor)]

children.text: padāntaram upayujyatāṃ mā vā / sarvathā tatprayogakṛta vairasyaṃ paunaruktyaprayojakam iti tadāśrayeṇāyaṃ doṣa uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: whether or not another word is employed — in every case, the distaste produced by that usage is what constitutes the ground for [the fault of] repetition. Thus this fault is stated on that basis.

body.translated_text: Thus. '<s>Śakrasaṅkāśa</s>' (resembling <s>Indra</s>), '<s>Śrīnadīhaṃsa</s>' (swan of the river of <s>Śrī</s>), '<s>Medinīcandra</s>' (moon of the earth), '<s>Vidviṣāṃ Kāla</s>' (death of enemies) — these are four vocative addresses. Here the distinction of purport is quite clear. Likewise, one word '<s>kāśa</s>' (luster/reed-grass) is established as the object of comparison for garments, while the other serves as the standard of comparison for laughter — thus the purport is different. Other [cases] too should be construed similarly. 'In the absence of both' means in the absence of both a difference of meaning and a difference of purport. 'Not with <s>ghāsa</s>' — the meaning is: let there be a distinction of purport through the objecthood and the relatedness. This is rejected by 'not so.' 'Its own meaning' — what is said is this: the direct expression of one's own meaning alone is not purport; rather, purport is, over and above the expression of one's own meaning, an additional orientation toward a further meaning, as with the two uses of '<s>kāśa</s>.' There, beyond the conveying of the substance delimited by the <s>kāśa</s>-species, an additional relation of comparison-object and standard-of-comparison is conveyed. But this is not the case with the two uses of '<s>bisa</s>' (lotus-stalk). For here no thing is perceived beyond the substance delimited by the <s>bisa</s>-species. As for the objecthood and relatedness — that is merely the [word's] referent remaining in such a condition; it does not bring about a distinct status through excess. Therefore the domain of pronominal reference, avoiding the word's own [repetition], is the proper [course]. Now, what is called repetition? Where without that usage the meaning would be understood, and where the use of another word with the same meaning necessarily serves — how can there be repetition? Where there is perception through a single meaning without distinction of purport — there, repetition [is a fault] because it produces distaste in perception. But where in its place —

children.text: sarvanāmeti "jakṣur bisam" ity atra nirdiṣṭaṃ bisam uttaratra prasūnasaṃbandhitvena sarvanāmaparāmarśārhaṃ sad yat svaśabdenoktaṃ, tat śabdapunaruktam / yady apy arthapunaruktam evaikaṃ punaruktaṃ (prayuktaṃ, tat?)
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>sarvanāma</s>' (pronoun): In '<s>jakṣur bisam</s>' (the eating of the lotus-stalk), the '<s>bisa</s>' (lotus-stalk) specified there, being worthy of pronominal reference in the sequel by virtue of its relation to the flower, when it is stated again by its own word — that is verbal repetition. Even though semantic repetition alone is the single [true] repetition —

children.text: ⟨prāg uktaṃ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: 'as previously stated' (conjectured by the editor)]

children.text: tathāpi śabdasya punaruktatety uktam arthamukhenaiva śabdasyāpi punaruktatety abhiprāyeṇa / "sarvanāmaparāmarśayogyasye"ti nirdiṣṭāṃ yogyatāṃ vibhaktum āha - prādhānyam iti / dvividhaṃ parāmarśayogyatvaṃ śābdam ārthaṃ ceti / tatra yasmin parāmṛśyasya svātantryeṇa kartṛtvādinā nirdeśena prādhānyaṃ tatra śābdam / yatra punaḥ parāmṛśyasyānyaḥ kaś cit saṃbandhitvena nirdiśyate, tatrārtham / tatra hi saṃbandhinaṃ prati asyopayoga eva yogyatvam / tathā caikam udāhṛtam / saṃbandhipratītimukheneti / atra saṃbandhī haraḥ tasya maulidvāreṇa śaśāṅkasaṃbandhitvāt / tatpratītimukhena cātra śaśāṅkaḥ pratīyate, na tu "cārutā vapur" ityādau cārutāder iva sākṣād eva śaśāṅkasya pratītiḥ / śaśāṅkasaṃba
children.translated_text: nevertheless it was said that the word is [also] repeated — the intent being that through meaning, the word too is repeated. In order to analyze the fitness specified in '[a word] worthy of pronominal reference,' he says 'predominance.' The fitness for pronominal reference is twofold: word-based (<s>śābda</s>) and meaning-based (<s>ārtha</s>). There, where the referent has predominance through independent specification as agent and the like — there it is word-based. Where, on the other hand, some other entity is specified as related to the referent — there it is meaning-based. For there, the very usefulness [of the referent] to the related entity constitutes its fitness. And thus one example has been given. 'Through the perception of the related entity' — here the related entity is <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and through [his] crown, there is a relation to the moon. Through that perception the moon is perceived here — but not directly, as with beauty and the like in '<s>cārutā vapur</s>' (beautiful body). The moon-related —

children.text: [Page 41]
children.translated_text: [Page 41]

children.text: ndhinām iti / atra "saṃbandhinibandha" iti kārikāyāṃ yaḥ saṃbandhī yuktaḥ, sa nirdiṣṭaḥ / tathā cātrāṃśavaḥ saṃbandhitvena nirdiṣṭāḥ / tatparāmarśayogyateti tacchabdena parāmṛśyaḥ śaśāṅko nirdiṣṭaḥ / sā hi guṇībhūtasyeti / haramanyapadārthaṃ prati niśāpatir guṇībhūtaḥ / tasyāpi niśā guṇībhūtā / sā ca bhuvaneti / atra na nagendratanayāyāḥ saṃbandhī nirdiṣṭaḥ / api tu sā cety anena svarūpeṇa
children.translated_text: 'of the related entities' — here, the related entity appropriate to the verse '<s>saṃbandhinibandha</s>' (dependent on the related entity) is what is specified. And thus here the rays are specified as related entities. 'That fitness for reference' — the moon, which is to be referred to by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun, is specified. 'For, of the one that has become subordinate' — the lord of night (<s>Niśāpati</s>, the Moon) is subordinate to <s>Hara</s> and other word-meanings. Night too is subordinate to him. 'And she [is related] to the world' — here, the related entity of the daughter of the mountain-lord (<s>Pārvatī</s>) is not specified. Rather, by 'and she,' in her own form —

children.text: ⟨svarūpam conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: '<s>svarūpam</s>' (own form) conjectured by the editor]

children.text: nirdiṣṭam / vihasto na kva cic chaktaḥ / samāsagatasyeti parāmṛśyasyeti saṃbandhaḥ / tatra hi parāmṛśyasya samāse guṇībhāvāt saṃbandhinaś cānirdeśāt parāmarśo na nyāyyaḥ /
children.translated_text: is specified. 'Handless, nowhere capable.' 'Of the one in the compound' is to be connected with 'of the referent.' For there, since the referent becomes subordinate in the compound and the related entity is not specified, the [pronominal] reference is not proper.

body.text: na sarvajanasaṃvedanīya iti / asyārthaḥ - "yathāsmai rocate viśvaṃ tathedaṃ parivartate" iti nyāyenātrātiprauḍhatayā granthakāro nijāyattāṃ padārthavyavasthāṃ karttum ārabdhaḥ, yena "tadaṃśunicitaḥ" iti "tat tamasām" iti

children.text: ⟨tat tu samāsam eti ca sam iti Ms.⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: '<s>tat tu samāsam eti ca sam</s>' (manuscript reading)]

children.text: ca śaśāṅkasya niśāyāś ca tacchabdena parāmarśam aghaṭamānam api samarthayate, "jakṣur bisaṃ ghṛtavikāsibisaprasūnā" ity atra ca bisaprasūnaśabdasya saṃjñāpadasyāpi bisaśabdāśrayeṇa sūkṣmekṣikayā paunaruktyaṃ doṣam udbhāvayati / na caitat samarthanaṃ hṛdayahāri, yasmāc chaśāṅkamaulir iti ca niśāpatimaulir iti ca saṃjñāśabdāv etau / saṃjñāśabdānāṃ ca vidyamānasyāpy arthānugamasya na prayojakatvaṃ rūḍheḥ prādhānyāt / tataś cātra na śaśāṅkārtho na niśārthaḥ kaś cit / kiṃ tūpāyamātreṇaitāv arthāv āśritya saṃjñiviśeṣa evātra vivakṣitaḥ / evaṃ ca saṃjñyantargatayoḥ śaśāṅkaniśayos tacchabdaparāmarśena sahṛdayahṛdayāny āvarjayatīti haṭhasarmathanam
children.translated_text: and even the [pronominal] reference to the moon and to night by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun, though impossible, he justifies. And in '<s>jakṣur bisaṃ ghṛtavikāsibisaprasūnā</s>' (the eating of the lotus-stalk, the lotus-flower blooming in ghee), he raises the fault of repetition even regarding the word '<s>bisaprasūna</s>' (lotus-flower), which is a proper name, on the basis of [its containing] the word '<s>bisa</s>', by a subtle examination. But this justification is not heart-captivating, since '<s>Śaśāṅkamauli</s>' (Moon-crested one) and '<s>Niśāpatimauli</s>' (Night-lord-crested one) are both proper names. And for proper names, even when there is actual semantic correspondence, it has no operative force, because conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) has predominance. Therefore, here there is no moon-meaning nor any night-meaning. Rather, relying on these meanings merely as a means, only the specific named entity is intended here. And thus, in [claiming that] pronominal reference to the moon and night, which are subsumed within the proper name, captivates the hearts of the sensitive — this is a forced argument.

children.translated_text: This [is the case]. Moreover, in '<s>Śaśāṅkamauli</s>' (Moon-crested), it would be better for the pronominal reference to be to the moon, since the moon's curved form is present there. But in '<s>Niśāpatimauli</s>' (Night-lord-crested), the reference to night is even worse than bad — since only the Night-lord is present there by the stated order. Night, being useful only as a mere indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), has no possibility [of reference] there. And where night itself has no possibility, what need is there to speak of 'the darknesses'? This amounts to the maxim: 'A blind man found a jewel; a fingerless one picked it up.'

body.text: granthakarttuḥ punar ayam āśayaḥ - iha tu dvividhāḥ saṃjñāśabdāḥ rūḍhā yogarūḍhayaś ca / tatra rūdḥānām arthānugamābhāvāt tadanusaraṇaṃ na karttavyam / ye tu yogarūḍhayas teṣāṃ yadi yoga utkaṭatāṃ bhajate tadāśrayo vyavahāro na duṣyati / ata eva nimittabalena pravṛttasya śabdasya nimittāntarbhāve prayogaḥ saugatair niṣiddha eva / yad āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: The intention of the author of the text is as follows: here there are two kinds of proper-name words (<s>saṃjñāśabda</s>): conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>) and etymologically motivated-yet-conventional (<s>yogarūḍha</s>). Among those, for conventional ones, since there is no etymological transparency, one should not follow etymological analysis. But for those that are <s>yogarūḍha</s>, if the etymological element becomes prominent, then usage based on it is not faulty. For this very reason, the use of a word that has arisen through a particular ground (<s>nimitta</s>), when the ground is absorbed [into another], has been prohibited by the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>). As they say —

children.text: bahuvrīhīti matvarthe bahuvrīhividhānam / karmadhārayamatvarthīyābhyām iti / karmadhārayamatvarthīyau samuccayenāvasthitau vṛttilāghavād bahuvrīhiṇā bādhyete ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Bahuvrīhi</s>" — the prescribing of <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) in the sense of <s>matup</s> (possessive suffix). "By <s>karmadhāraya</s> and <s>matvarthīya</s> [suffix]" — the <s>karmadhāraya</s> and the <s>matvarthīya</s> suffix, standing together in aggregation, are overridden by the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> due to the economy of formation — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Thus. This being the case, in usage based on etymology, if some invariable concomitant of the meaning that constitutes a component of the proper name is intended to be conveyed, then the pronominal reference to that component for the purpose of connecting with that [concomitant] is not faulty. As stated: "by a pronoun, whose operation conceals the connection" (<s>Kāvya Sūtra</s> 5.1.11). In <s>mauliḥ</s> (crest) here, the rays that invariably accompany the moon (<s>śaśāṅka</s>) are conveyed as a related entity. In <s>niśāpatimauliḥ</s> (one whose crest is the lord of night), the darknesses that invariably accompany the night are [conveyed]. And even the non-reality of those is not so faulty, because they are conveyed as the domain of poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>). The only distinction is that in the former case, a relative of the named entity is referred to; in the latter, a relative of the relative. Thus, in the case of etymologically motivated proper-name words, the usage motivated by etymology is well-established in various instances. But as for the passage "I would do even to <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the <s>Pinākapāṇi</s> (trident-bearer)" — there, the etymological transparency of the proper-name word <s>pinākapāṇi</s> will be resisted, for which reason the word <s>Hara</s> is employed for the purpose of identifying the named entity. This is not for the purpose of demonstrating the absence of etymological transparency, but rather, the intention is that the intended meaning's being the locus of intensity, the etymologically transparent meaning, cannot be sustained without a separate use of the proper-name word, since both the proper-name meaning and etymological transparency cannot simultaneously have predominance — hence the use of both words is recommended in such contexts. In the present case, when the mere intrinsic nature of the thing is being conveyed, even though it is a proper-name word, following the etymological transparency is unobstructed. "Otherwise" (<s>itarathā</s>) means: in the absence of suitability of both kinds, because of the absence of apprehension of the referent — this is the meaning. "But here" (<s>atra tu</s>) — in "it eats the lotus-stalk" (<s>jakṣur bisam</s>). "In the employment of the related flower" — in its being taken up. "Semantic" (<s>ārtha</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'Of others': the plural indicates that in such contexts, since the purpose is already served by a single '<s>iva</s>'-word, the employment of additional ones is fruitless—that is the intention. 'Of the third too': when the resemblance at the sentence-meaning level is intended, only one '<s>iva</s>'-word should be used. But when resemblance at the word-meaning level is intended, as many '<s>iva</s>'-words as there are qualified word-meanings should be used. One should not create a half-and-half affair—that is the meaning. This is stated as a position for argument's sake. His actual position is that when a sentence-level simile is possible, word-level similes should not be made. And accordingly, he will critique with '<s>dine dine</s>' and so on. '<s>Dine dine</s>': here the crescent of the moon is the object of comparison for <s>Pārvatī</s>, while the particulars [compared to] are the other <s>kalās</s> (digits/arts). The qualifier of the particulars is 'consisting of <s>lāvaṇya</s> (charm).' In place of those, the counterpart of the other digits is 'other splendors of moonlight.' For the explanation is: 'those whose other splendors [of moonlight].' '<s>Dine dine</s>' etc. is a common property of both <s>Pārvatī</s> and the crescent moon. The explanation that 'the other digits nourish other splendors of moonlight' is not correct, because of the defect of change of grammatical construction and the like. Here, since the purpose is served by the single '<s>iva</s>'-word in '<s>cāndramasīva lekhā kalāntarāṇi puṣṇāti</s>' ('the crescent, like the moon's, nourishes the other digits'), the second '<s>iva</s>'-word is a case of <s>paunaruktya</s> (repetition). '<s>Yaṃ sametya</s>': here the object of comparison for '<s>yam</s>' is a 'fierce wind,' and for 'the <s>Cedi</s> [king]' it is a 'lamp.' The suffix '<s>vat</s>' has the sense of similarity. The abandonment of <s>Śambhu</s>'s play of eyebrows follows from the calming of the eyes. Here, even with the given reading, the inclusion of heterogeneous words like '<s>lalāṭalekhayā</s>' (forehead-line) etc. in the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) and <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) that are in the object case, the use of anomalous words, and the resulting harshness are indeed difficult to remedy. Therefore the reading '<s>caṇḍamārutanavapradīpavat</s>' ('like a fierce wind and a new lamp') is better. For thus, by merely replacing '<s>mi</s>' with '<s>na</s>'—a slight transposition with ease—both the removal of the defect and beauty are achieved. '<s>Malayajārdram iva</s>' (as if moist with sandalwood): although this is composed as the object of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) for the moon-fragment, it ultimately functions—through syntactic expectancy, proximity, and capability—as a qualifier of the 'expanse of the forehead': this is the poet's intention. But in reality, since the desired meaning is achieved even without the '<s>iva</s>'-word, the '<s>iva</s>'-word is redundant. There is no purpose in fancying that the moon-fragment is moist with sandalwood. Where this qualifier is useful, the '<s>iva</s>'-word is pointless. '<s>Tadabhinnārthena</s>': because the meaning of '<s>iva</s>' is absorbed into the compound. 'In reverse order': because its proper place of employment is near 'the surface of the forehead.' '<s>Varam</s>': because the displacement of the '<s>iva</s>'-word's sequence cannot be remedied, there is dissatisfaction. Only because '<s>hārī</s>' is not compounded, and hence the '<s>iva</s>' meaning is not conveyed, the '<s>iva</s>'-word is not [strictly] repeated—thus the avoidance of repetition is achieved. '<s>Aho aparyanta</s>': '<s>od</s>' is designated as <s>pragṛhya</s> (PS 1.1.15). By <s>upamā-rūpaka</s> etc.:

body.translated_text: Thus, the many meanings like abundance etc., following the meaning of existence (<s>astyartha</s>), have been stated as the domain of <s>matvarthīya</s> [suffixes]. Why then are they not stated as expressible by the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>? — he answers with "of <s>matup</s>" (<s>matoḥ</s>). The mention of <s>matup</s> is indicative of all <s>matvarthīya</s> [suffixes]. For the meanings like abundance etc.

"alaṅkārasya kavayo yatrālaṅkaraṇāntaram /
  asaṃtuṣṭā nibadhnanti hārāder maṇibandhavad"
body.translated_text: "Where poets, unsatisfied with one ornament, bind upon it yet another ornament—as a gem-setting upon a necklace."

children.text: iti / vakroktijīvitakṛtas tu tam alaṅkārapuṣṭhapātinam alaṅkāraṃ dūṣayati / nirmokam uktim iveti atropamārūpakatvaṃ paraprasiddhyoktam / na tv idam upamārūpakam / utprekṣārūpakaṃ tu syāt, nirmokam uktas saṃbhāvyamānatvena pratīteḥ / tathā hi nirmokānuguṇyāt tāvat gaganasyorageṇa rūpaṇam / nirvyūḍhe ca rūpake nirmokam uktir na tāṭasthyena pratīyate, kiṃ tu gaganoragasaṃbandhitvena / (gaganoragasaṃbandhitvena) ca pratītau na sādṛśyam api tv adhyavasāyaḥ / tasya ca pravṛttamānatvam ity utprekṣaiva jyāyāsī pratītau / ataś ce(yaṃ?)(daṃ)muktipadaṃ kṛtam / anyathā śuddhasādṛśyapratipādane dharmy eva viśiṣṭo nirmoka upamānatvena nirdeśyaḥ syāt / bhinnaliṅgayor upamāyā duṣṭatvān na nirdiṣṭa iti cen na / sādhāraṇadharmasyānirdeśe nirdiṣṭasyāpi vā dvairūpyābhāve bhinnaliṅgasaṅkhyayor api "strīva gacchati ṣaṇḍo 'yam" ityādau "hantāvahanti doṣā iva nṛpatīnāṃ guṇa iha(sahaiva?)durvinayam" ityādau copamānopameyabhāvasyeṣṭatvāt / tasmād upamāyāṃ nirmoka iveti syāt / utprekṣāyāṃ kriyāmātrotprekṣaṇam upapadyata ity utprekṣārūpakam etat paramārthataḥ / etad asmābhir harṣacaritavārttike vistṛtya pratipāditaṃ tata evāvaseyam / evaṃ paraśur ivetyādau vācyam / "tamoraṇyavahner ivārcir" iti / atra tamaso 'raṇyena rūpeṇa vahnir arcissaṃbandhitayā vivakṣitaḥ (samāse na niveśanīyaḥ kaś cid atra nirdiṣṭo?)
children.translated_text: But the author of the <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> (<s>Kuntaka</s>) criticizes that ornament which falls upon the back of [another] ornament. '<s>Nirmokam uktim iva</s>' (like speech [is] a slough): here the characterization as <s>upamā-rūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) is stated according to others' view. But this is not <s>upamā-rūpaka</s>. It would rather be <s>utprekṣā-rūpaka</s> (fancy-metaphor), since '<s>nirmokam uktiḥ</s>' ('speech is a slough') is understood as something being imagined. For thus: first, by analogy with a slough, the sky is metaphorically identified with a serpent. And when the metaphor is fully developed, '<s>nirmokam uktiḥ</s>' is not understood in a detached manner, but rather as connected with the sky-serpent. And when understood as connected with the sky-serpent, it is not [mere] similarity but rather identification (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). And since that [identification] is in the process of being established, <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy) is indeed the stronger element in the cognition. For this reason the word '<s>mukti</s>' (release) was used. Otherwise, in a straightforward presentation of similarity, the qualified entity itself—namely the slough—should be indicated as the standard of comparison. If [one objects that] the simile of different genders is defective, hence it was not indicated—no, [that is wrong]. When no common property is specified, or when the specified one has no dual form, simile between [entities of] different gender and number is accepted, as in '<s>strīva gacchati ṣaṇḍo 'yam</s>' ('this eunuch walks like a woman') and '<s>hantāvahanti doṣā iva nṛpatīnāṃ guṇa iha durvinayam</s>' ('alas, the virtues of kings carry ill-conduct, as [their] faults [would]') and the like. Therefore, if it were a simile, it would be '<s>nirmoka iva</s>' ('like a slough'). In <s>utprekṣā</s>, only the action is fancied, hence it is <s>utprekṣā-rūpaka</s> in the ultimate analysis. This has been explained by us at length in the <s>Harṣacaritavārttika</s>, and should be gathered from there. Similarly, in '<s>paraśur iva</s>' ('like an axe') and the like, the same should be said. '<s>Tamoraṇyavahner ivārciḥ</s>' ('like the flame of the fire of the forest of darkness'): here, darkness in the form of a forest, and fire in connection with flame—that is the intended meaning (in the compound, one should be placed [who is] not indicated here)

children.text: ⟨samāse niveśanīyaḥ, yato na kaś cid atra nirdiṣṭaḥ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: ⟨[One] should be placed in the compound, since no one is indicated here: conj. (Ed.)⟩

children.text: yo vahninā rūpyeta / tasmāt tamoraṇyasya vahnyarcir iti vaktavyam ity atra vācyāvacanaṃ doṣaḥ / ālānam iti saty eva sādṛśye āropyāropakabhāvasya nidarśanam /
children.translated_text: who might be metaphorically identified with fire. Therefore one should say '<s>tamoraṇyasya vahnyarciḥ</s>' ('the fire-flame of the forest of darkness'): the failure to state what should be stated is the defect here. '<s>Ālānam</s>': this is an illustration of the <s>āropa-āropaka</s> (superimposition and superimpositor) relation when similarity actually exists.

children.text: cumbatīveti / atroprekṣārthe prayuktasyevaśabdasya lakṣaṇāsamarthitenārthena kṛtārthatvāt punaruktatvam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Cumbatīva</s>' ('as if kissing'): here, the '<s>iva</s>'-word used in the sense of <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy) is rendered redundant, since the purpose is already served by the meaning enabled through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification).

body.text: a(tra) copamārūpakābhimate evaṃvidhe ca pradeśe granthakāro hevākitayaiva dūṣaṇam adāt / tathā śabdārthayor vicchittir alaṅkāraḥ / vicchittiś ca kavipratibhollāsarūpatvāt kavipratibhollāsasya cānantyād anantatvaṃ bhajamānā na paricchettuṃ śakyate / ata evoktaṃ dhvanikṛtā
body.translated_text: Here, in the case accepted as <s>upamā-rūpaka</s>, and in such passages, the author gave his criticism merely by way of an exclamation '<s>hevāki</s>' (alas!). Now, the <s>vicchitti</s> (charm/surprise) of word and meaning is the [true] ornament. And <s>vicchitti</s>, being of the nature of the flash of poetic genius, and since the flash of poetic genius is infinite, partakes of infinity and cannot be circumscribed. Therefore, as stated by the author of the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>:

children.text: "vācaspatisahasrāṇāṃ sahasrair api yatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even by thousands of <s>Vācaspatis</s> (lords of speech), even with effort,

children.text: nibaddhā sā kṣayaṃ naiti prakṛtir jagatām iva //"
children.translated_text: that [poetic practice] once established does not come to an end—like the nature of the world itself."

body.text: iti / anyatrāpy uktam -
body.translated_text: And elsewhere it has been said:

body.text: "ajjavi abhiṇṇam uddo pajaai vāāparipphando"
body.translated_text: "Even today, without interruption, the outpouring of speech's creative play rises forth" [Prakrit].

body.text: iti / evaṃ ca yadi vicchttyantarāpekṣayā tasya vicchittyantarasya paunaruktyaṃ tadopamāyā rūpakādyapekṣayā paunaruktyaṃ syāt / upamāpekṣayā hi rūpakam atiśayoktir vā balīyasī / na caivaṃ prayujyate, vivakṣāyā nānātvāt / tathā hi kva cit sādṛśyamātraṃ vivakṣitam / tatrāpi kva cid abhedaḥ / tasminn api kvacid āropaḥ / kvacid adhyavasāyaḥ / (adhyavasāye 'pi) kva cit sādhyatvaṃ kva cit siddhatvam ityādikrameṇānantaprakāraṃ vicchittivaicitryam / tatrāpi saṃyojanakrameṇa navaṃ vicchittivaicitryam anubhūyamānam āśritaṃ ca mahākavibhiḥ kathaṃ saṃkṣeparucitvenāpahnūyate / na hīdaṃ vākyaṃ lakṣaṇaśāstraṃ, yena mātrālāghavaṃ cintyate / tatrāpi vā na niyamena lāghavam āśritaṃ mahadbhiḥ / tathā hi vāgrahaṇasya sthāne 'nyatarasyāṃ grahaṇam api kṛtam / vicchittivaicitryaṃ tair apy āśritam eva / tad uktaṃ "vicitrā hi sūtrasya kṛtiḥ pāṇineḥ" iti / evaṃ cātra kṛte 'pi rūpake utprekṣādinibandhaḥ kam api guṇam utkarṣayati na doṣam iti sahṛdayair nipuṇaṃ nirūpaṇīyam / na tu hevākasya paścāl laganīyam ity āstāṃ tāvat / prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: And thus, if there were repetition of one type of <s>vicchitti</s> with respect to another type of <s>vicchitti</s>, then by the same logic there would be repetition of <s>upamā</s> (simile) with respect to <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and so on. For with respect to simile, metaphor or hyperbole is stronger. Yet this [objection of repetition] is not raised, because the expressive intentions are diverse. For sometimes mere similarity is intended; within that, sometimes non-difference; within that, sometimes superimposition; sometimes identification; within identification, sometimes it is something to be established, sometimes already established—and so on in this sequence, the variety of <s>vicchitti</s> is of infinite kinds. And even within that, the novel variety of <s>vicchitti</s> experienced through the sequence of combination, which has been adopted by the great poets—how can it be denied by one who delights in brevity? For this is not a grammatical treatise where economy of syllables is to be considered. And even there, the great [grammarians] did not invariably adopt brevity. For example, in place of the <s>vā</s>-mention, the mention of '<s>anyatarasya</s>' was also made. Variety of <s>vicchitti</s> was embraced even by them. As stated: 'For the composition of <s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtras</s> is variegated.' Thus, even when a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) has been composed, the composition of <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy) and the like highlights some virtue, not a defect—this should be carefully examined by connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>). One should not follow in the footsteps of carping critics. But enough of this digression; let us follow the main subject.

body.text: murmuraḥ aṅgāraḥ / āmravaṇasyeti "pranirantar" (PS_8,4.5) ṇatvam / pathika

children.translated_text: [Page 45]

children.text: vrajān parita iti / paritaśśabdayoge "abhitaḥ paritaḥ samayānikaṣā" iti dvitīyā / atra dadhur ivetīvaśabdaḥ punar ukta eva, vastvantarabhūtānāṃ rajaḥkaṇānāṃ vastvantarabhūtamurmuracūrṇatvadhāraṇena suṣṭhusādṛśyapratīteḥ / evaṃ -
children.translated_text: '<s>vrajān paritaḥ</s>': when '<s>paritaḥ</s>' is used, the accusative [is applied] by the rule '<s>abhitaḥ paritaḥ samayā nikaṣā</s>.' Here, the '<s>iva</s>'-word in '<s>dadhur iva</s>' is indeed redundant, since by the [metaphorical] attribution of being coal-powder (<s>murmuracūrṇa</s>) to the dust-particles, which are actually different substances, an excellent cognition of similarity is already achieved. Similarly:

body.translated_text: '<s>Murmura</s>' means 'embers.' '<s>Āmravaṇasya</s>': the <s>ṇatva</s> (cerebral nasal) [obtains] by the rule '<s>pra-nirantar</s>' (PS 8.4.5). '<s>Pathika</s>-'

children.text: "tat pātu vaḥ śrīpatinābhipadmaṃ svādhyāyaśālā kamalāsanasya /
children.translated_text: "May the lotus of the navel of the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) protect you—the study-hall of the Lotus-seated one (<s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: dīrghair ninādair dadhate 'nukāraṃ sāmadhvanīnām iva yatra bhṛṅgāḥ //"
children.translated_text: where bees, with their long hummings, produce an imitation of the sounds of <s>Sāman</s> chants."

body.text: ityādāv anukāraśabdaprayoge ivādiśabdaprayogasya paunaruktyam avaseyam / prativastvalaṅkārād iti "pūrṇaḥ śaśāṅkābhyudayam ākāṅkṣati mahārṇavaḥ" iti prativastūpamayā sādṛśyapratītau dṛṣṭāntaśabdoktir duṣṭā / na ca dṛṣṭāntālaṅkāratvaṃ pratipādayituṃ dṛṣṭāntaśabdaḥ, dṛṣṭāntaśabdād dṛṣṭāntālaṅkāratvāpratīteḥ / na hi ṣaṣṭhyādiparihāreṇa saṃbandhiśabdāt saṃbandhapratītiḥ rasaśabdād vā rasapratītiḥ / adūraviprakarṣeṇa tv abhidhānaṃ vastusaṃsparśi bhavatīti / nanu svakaṇṭhenābhidhānam apahāya kim iti sādṛśyapratītir āśrīyata ity āha vācyo hy artha iti / pūrvavad iti / pūrvaṃ yathā "ālānam" ity ādau rūpakamukhenopamānopameyabhāvaḥ kathitas tadvad iha dīpakamukhenety arthaḥ / atra ca dvayoḥ prabhādhenvoḥ prākaraṇikatvāt tulyayogitām adyatanā manyante / dvayor api prākaraṇikatve mahāprakaraṇāpekṣayā dhenoḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ prākaraṇikatvaṃ prabhāyās tv aprakrṣṭam ity etadapekṣayā cirantanair dīpakam etat sthāpitam / tadapekṣayātrānena tadvācoyuktiḥ kṛtā / evam alaṅkārāntareṣv api samāsoktyapastutapraśaṃsādiṣu / tatrāpy upamānopameyabhāvaḥ svakaṇṭhena nopanibandhanīyaḥ / tathā -
body.translated_text: In [verses] like those, when an onomatopoeic word is used, the use of the comparison-word '<s>iva</s>' etc. should be understood as repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>). / 'From the <s>prativastu</s> ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>)' — In '<s>pūrṇaḥ śaśāṅkābhyudayam ākāṅkṣati mahārṇavaḥ</s>' (The full ocean longs for the rising of the moon), when the cognition of similarity arises through the figure <s>prativastūpamā</s> (implied comparison through corresponding objects), the use of the word '<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>' (example) is faulty. / And the word '<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>' is not [used] to convey the figure called <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, since the figure <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> is not cognized from the [mere] word '<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>.' For it is not the case that from the word '<s>saṃbandhi</s>' (relative), dispensing with the genitive etc., the [actual] relation is cognized; nor is <s>rasa</s> cognized from the [mere] word '<s>rasa</s>.' Rather, designation that is not far-fetched touches the [actual] thing. / Now, abandoning direct expression, why is the cognition of similarity relied upon? — to this he says '<s>vācyo hy arthaḥ</s>' (for the meaning must be expressed). / 'As before' — Just as earlier, in '<s>ālānam</s>' etc., the relation of comparison-standard and comparandum was described through the medium of metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>), so here through the medium of <s>dīpaka</s> (condensed expression) — this is the meaning. / And here, since both radiance (<s>prabhā</s>) and the cow are contextually relevant, modern [scholars] consider it <s>tulyayogitā</s> (conjunction of equals). But since, when both are contextually relevant, the cow has stronger contextual relevance relative to the larger context while radiance has weaker [relevance] — with this consideration, earlier [scholars] established this as <s>dīpaka</s>. With that consideration, by this [author], the expression (<s>vācoyukti</s>) of that [figure] is made. / Similarly in other figures too — <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), etc. / There too, the comparison-standard and comparandum relationship should not be composed by direct statement. / Thus —

children.text: "draviṇam āpadi bhūṣaṇam utsave śaraṇam ātmabhaye niśi dīpikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Wealth in calamity, an ornament at a festival, a shelter in mortal fear, a lamp in the night —

children.text: bahuvidhārthyupakārabharakṣamo bhavati ko 'pi bhavān iva san maṇiḥ" //
children.translated_text: capable of bearing the load of many kinds of beneficial service — is there any gem like you, sir?"

body.text: ity atrāprastutapraśaṃsayā bhavadarthasya sadṛśatvena pratīteḥ punar vacanaṃ na karttavyam iti vakṣyate / asmābhiś caitat prapañco bṛhatyāṃ kariṣyate / itinaiveti itiśabdo hetvarthah prayujyamānaḥ svabhāvataḥ pūrvavākyārthasyocyamānatvaṃ bodhyamānatvaṃ vā garbhīkṛtya pravartate / varam iti uktadoṣadvayanivāraṇamātram etat / na tu sarvathā niravadyam idam, yataśśabdātaśśabdayor vaiyarthyāt /

children.text: anibandhanasyeti na hi pūraṇīyapūrakatvena duṣṭatvam / aviśeṣaṇa iti viśeṣaṇadānārtham avyabhicāriṇo 'pi prayogaḥ śasyata ity arthaḥ tathā cāha vāmanaḥ - "viśeṣaṇasya ca" (2 adhi. 18 sū.) iti / vyalokyateti vilokanakriyaiva lokitāraṃ lokam ākṣipatīti lokaśabdasya paunaruktyam / dvaya'rpāti prasthānavaśān nītivaśāc cāśrīyante / gām iti gośabdasya vākparyāyasya vacanakriyāyām avyabhicārāt prayogo na kāryaḥ / dṛṣṭa iti darśanakriyāyā dṛg eva karaṇatvenākṣipteti dṛkśabdaḥ punar uktaḥ / kārakāntareṣv apīti yathā "sthāne tiṣṭhati" ity atrādhikaraṇasya paunaruktyam / vivikte sthāne tiṣṭhatīti tu viśeṣaṇārthaṃ prayogo na duṣṭaḥ / ekaiveti ekaivopamādiḥ / śābdatvaṃ śrautatvaṃ yathevādiśabdaprayogāt / ārthatvaṃ sadṛśādiśabdaprayogāt / atisphuṭām iti sthūladṛṣṭyaiva dṛśyām ity arthaḥ / umāvṛṣāṅkāv iti / atra śarajanmanā yathetyādinā pratīto 'py upamānopameyabhāvas tatsadṛśenetyādinā punar uktaḥ / kaves tu nandananimittaḥ pūrva upamānopameyabhāvaḥ / pratīyamānaprabhāvādinimittas tv aparaḥ / tathā cāyaṃ "dilīpa iti rājendur induḥ kṣīranidhāv iva" ity evaṃvidham upamānopameyabhāvam ātanoti / granthakāras tu viśiṣṭopamānanirdeśān nāntarīyakatayā prabhāvādipratī
children.translated_text: 'Without basis' (<s>anibandhanasya</s>) — For it is not faulty merely by being a filler for what needs filling. / 'Non-qualifier' (<s>aviśeṣaṇa</s>) — The meaning is: even the use of an invariable [term] for the purpose of providing a qualifier is commended. And so <s>Vāmana</s> says: 'of a qualifier too' (2nd chapter, 18th <s>sūtra</s>). / '<s>Vyalokyata</s>' (was seen) — The very act of seeing (<s>lokana</s>) draws in the seer (<s>lokitāra</s>) and the world (<s>loka</s>) — hence the word '<s>loka</s>' is a repetition. / 'Twofold' — they are relied upon either by the force of convention or by the force of propriety (<s>nīti</s>). / '<s>Gām</s>' — Since the word '<s>go</s>' (cow), which is a synonym of speech (<s>vāc</s>), does not deviate from the action of speaking, it should not be used [again]. / '<s>Dṛṣṭa</s>' (seen) — Since the action of seeing already implies sight (<s>dṛś</s>) as an instrument, the word '<s>dṛk</s>' (sight) is a re-statement. / 'In other case-relations too' — As in '<s>sthāne tiṣṭhati</s>' (stands in a place), where the locative (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) is a repetition. / But '<s>vivikte sthāne tiṣṭhati</s>' (stands in a secluded place) — the usage for the purpose of qualification is not faulty. / 'One alone' — one alone [figure such as] simile (<s>upamā</s>) etc. / 'Verbal' (<s>śābdatva</s>) — that which is expressed (<s>śrauta</s>), as through the use of words like '<s>iva</s>' etc. / 'Based on meaning' (<s>ārthatva</s>) — through the use of words like '<s>sadṛśa</s>' (similar) etc. / 'Overly manifest' (<s>atisphuṭā</s>) — visible even at a cursory glance — this is the meaning. / '<s>Umā-Vṛṣāṅkau</s>' (Umā and the Bull-bannered One [Śiva]) — Here, the comparison-standard and comparandum relationship, although already cognized through '<s>śarajanmanā yathā</s>' etc., is stated again by '<s>tatsadṛśena</s>' etc. / But for the poet, the earlier comparison-standard/comparandum relationship is occasioned by [his] delight (<s>nandana</s>). / While the latter is occasioned by the cognized power (<s>prabhāva</s>) etc. / And thus this extends the comparison-standard/comparandum relationship of the type '<s>Dilīpa iti rājendur induḥ kṣīranidhāv iva</s>' (Dilīpa [was] like a royal moon, like the moon in the milk-ocean). / But the author of [this] treatise thinks that, from the specification of a distinguished comparison-standard, the cognition of power etc. follows of necessity — hence double mention should not be made.

children.text: ākārasādṛśyena palāśaṃ prati dīyamānād ārdranakhakṣatam ity asmāt / tadviśeṣaṇopādānam iti ramaṇadattam ity ārdranakhakṣataviśeṣaṇopādānaṃ madayāpitalajjayeti pramadāviśeṣaṇopādānaṃ cety arthaḥ / yata iti nakhakṣatam ivety upamopakṛtāt surabhivanamālādīnāṃ puṃstvastrītvanirdeśād ity arthaḥ / strīpuṃsatvānumitir iti prathamavimarśoktaprakāreṇa vyakter anumitirūpatvenopapāditatvāt / aindraṃ dhanur iti atyanteti ābhogīti codāharaṇatrayaṃ vaidharmyakrameṇoktam / upapannakramasyā(sya?) sadbhāvāt / nāyakatvapratināyakatve iti / anumīyate iti śeṣaḥ / evam aṅganeva maṇistambhāv iti anumīyata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: From '<s>ārdranakhakṣatam</s>' (fresh nail-mark), which is given [as a comparison] for the <s>palāśa</s> (leaf/flame of the forest) through similarity of form. / 'The adoption of its qualifier' — the adoption of '<s>ramaṇadattam</s>' (given by the lover) as a qualifier of the 'fresh nail-mark,' and '<s>madayāpitalajjayā</s>' (with modesty put to flight by passion) as a qualifier of the woman — this is the meaning. / 'Because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) — from the simile-assisted '<s>nakhakṣatam iva</s>' (like a nail-mark), the specification of masculine and feminine gender for <s>surabhivanamālā</s> (fragrant forest-garlands) etc. — this is the meaning. / 'The inference of female and male nature' — because it has been established in the manner stated in the first <s>vimarśa</s> that manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) has the form of inference (<s>anumiti</s>). / '<s>Aindraṃ dhanuḥ</s>' (Indra's bow = rainbow), '<s>atyanta</s>' (excessive), '<s>ābhogī</s>' (expansive) — these three examples are stated in order of dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>). / Because a proper sequence [in them] exists. / 'Hero-hood and antagonist-hood' — 'is inferred' is to be supplied. / Similarly, '<s>aṅganā iva maṇistambhau</s>' (like a woman, the gem-pillars) — 'is inferred' is to be supplied.

children.text: bhogī vāsukeḥ sa eva netram ākarṣaṇarajjus tasya ā samantād yat parivartanarūpo viśeṣeṇa bhramo bhramaṇaṃ, tena mandarasya mūrttiḥ nitambe madhyabhāge valanaṃ parivarttanaṃ tenākulā jātā / tathā ābhogi vistāravat yan netraṃ nayanaṃ tasya parivartanaṃ kaṭākṣīkaraṇaṃ sa eva vibhramo vilāsaḥ / mūrttyā samāropitanāyikāvyavahārayā / utkalikās taraṅgā ruhiruhikāś ca hṛdayaṃ madhyadeśāś cittaṃ ca / ārohārtha iti āroḍhum iti pūrvaślokabhāgagataḥ / hṛdayārthaś ceti / hṛdayam ambunidher ity atra sthitiḥ / tayor iti āroho jīvavyāpāraviśeṣaḥ / hṛdayaṃ jīvakāyaikadeśaviśeṣaḥ / alaṅkārāntaratvam iti sādṛśyāl lakṣaṇā vakroktir ityādiprakāreṇa / lākṣaṇikahṛdayādiśabdaprayoge svaśabdaṃ vināpy arthāntaraṃ pratīyata ity āha yadartheti / yatropameye 'mbunidhiprabhṛtau / yadarthaikāśrayo nāyakādirūpopamānaviṣayo dharmo hṛdayādir āropito lakṣaṇayā bhavet, tayor nāyakāder upamānasyāmbunidhyādeś copameyasyopamānopameyabhāvaḥ śābdo neṣyate / gamyamānas tv iṣṭa evety arthaḥ / atraiva aparāgetyādinā śābdatve doṣodāharaṇam āha / mūlāny amātyādiprakṛtivargaḥ vṛkṣāvabandhanāni ca unmūlayituṃ sukara iti yojanā / tad dhīti upamānopameyatvam / rūpakaṃ yatheti / "tasyopamā rūpakaṃ vā" ity anusaṃdhatte / anurāgo lauhityam api / apiśabdaḥ sukhādipadanikaṭe yojanīyaḥ / vasuśabdas tejodhanayoḥ / atra niṣkāsanam utkaṭatvena gaṇikādharmo rūpakasya sādhakaḥ pramāṇam / kāryataś ceti kāryam atra niṣkāsanam / tadviśeṣasya strītvaviśeṣasya gaṇikārūpasyeti / ubhayārtheti dvyarthapadaprayogaḥ "pāṇḍupayodhareṇa" ityādau / liṅgaviśeṣaḥ "śarad" "raveḥ" ityādau / guṇavṛtti padam "āroḍhuṃ" "hṛdayam" ityādau / upamānaviśeṣo yathā "ārdranakhakṣatābham" ityādau / ākrośo gālidānam / paryāyoktīti yena rāhustrīstanayoḥ kārkaśyalakṣmīr vṛ
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhogī</s>' — '<s>Vāsuki</s>'s body (<s>bhoga</s>); that very [body] is the rope (<s>netra</s>) for pulling (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>); of that, the all-around turning — the particular revolution (<s>bhrama</s>) — by that, the form (<s>mūrtti</s>) of <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] at the hip (<s>nitamba</s>), the middle part, [experienced] a turning (<s>valana</s>), a revolution, and by that became agitated (<s>ākulā</s>). / Likewise, '<s>ābhogī</s>' — expansive; '<s>netra</s>' means eye (<s>nayana</s>); its turning (<s>parivartana</s>), i.e., the side-glance (<s>kaṭākṣīkaraṇa</s>), that very thing is the amorous play (<s>vibhrama</s>, <s>vilāsa</s>). / 'By the form (<s>mūrtti</s>)' — by which the behavior of the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) is superimposed. / '<s>Utkalikāḥ</s>' — waves, and also exhilarations; '<s>hṛdaya</s>' — the central region, and also the heart/mind (<s>citta</s>). / 'In the sense of ascending (<s>āroha</s>)' — '<s>āroḍhum</s>' (to mount) belongs to the earlier part of the verse. / 'And in the sense of heart' — '<s>hṛdayam ambunidheh</s>' (the heart of the ocean) — this is the position. / 'Of those two' — '<s>āroha</s>' is a particular function of a living being; '<s>hṛdaya</s>' is a particular part of a living body. / 'Being another figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>)' — in the manner of metonymy (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) through similarity, oblique expression (<s>vakrokti</s>), etc. / When metonymic words like '<s>hṛdaya</s>' etc. are used, even without the [simile-]word, the other meaning is cognized — to this he says '<s>yadarthā</s>' (for whose purpose). / 'Where' — in the comparandum (<s>upameya</s>) such as the ocean etc. / Where the property (<s>dharma</s>) such as 'heart' etc. — which has its sole basis in the comparison-standard meaning such as the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) etc. — is superimposed by metonymy upon [the ocean], of those — the hero etc. as comparison-standard and the ocean etc. as comparandum — the comparison-standard/comparandum relationship that is verbal (<s>śābda</s>) is not desired. / But [the one that is] inferred is indeed desired — this is the meaning. / Right here, by '<s>aparāga</s>' etc., he gives an example of the defect in [making it] verbally [explicit]. / 'Roots' (<s>mūlāni</s>) — the class of ministers (<s>amātya</s>) and other officials; and also the foundations of trees — easy to uproot: this is the construction. / '<s>Tad dhi</s>' — [expresses] the comparison-standard/comparandum relationship. / 'Metaphor, as in' — he connects with 'for that, simile (<s>upamā</s>) or metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>).' / '<s>Anurāga</s>' — also [means] redness. / The word '<s>api</s>' should be construed near the word '<s>sukha</s>' etc. / The word '<s>vasu</s>' [means both] splendor and wealth. / Here, 'expulsion' (<s>niṣkāsana</s>), being prominently a property of a courtesan (<s>gaṇikā</s>), is the authority (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that establishes the metaphor. / 'And from the effect (<s>kārya</s>)' — the effect here is expulsion. 'Of its particular [form]' — of the female particular, the courtesan form — thus. / 'Double-meaning' (<s>ubhayārtha</s>) — the use of a word with two meanings, as in '<s>pāṇḍupayodhareṇa</s>' (with a pale/Pāṇḍu cloud/breast) etc. / 'Gender-particular' — as in '<s>śarat</s>' (autumn), '<s>raveḥ</s>' (of the sun) etc. / 'A word with figurative usage' — as in '<s>āroḍhum</s>' (to mount), '<s>hṛdayam</s>' (heart) etc. / 'Comparison-standard particular' — as in '<s>ārdranakhakṣatābham</s>' (resembling a fresh nail-mark) etc. / '<s>Ākrośa</s>' — abuse, invective. / 'By <s>paryāyokti</s> (circumlocution)' — by which the harshness regarding <s>Rāhu</s>, women, and sons —

body.translated_text: Here, it will be said that since the meaning 'you' is cognized through similarity by means of <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), re-statement should not be made. / And we shall elaborate this in our larger work (<s>Bṛhatī</s>). / '<s>Iti naiva</s>' (thus not at all) — The word '<s>iti</s>,' used in the sense of a reason, naturally functions by incorporating the fact that the meaning of the preceding sentence is being stated or understood. / '<s>Varam</s>' (better) — This merely removes the two stated defects. But it is not entirely faultless, since the words '<s>yataḥ</s>' and '<s>ataḥ</s>' become purposeless.

children.translated_text: when the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relationship is cognized, without the separate usage of the common property, the sentence-meaning cannot cohere — therefore separate usage is not faulty. 'That statement' — by the word '<s>sahaja</s>' (innate), the statement of naturalness. 'Of those having the same case-ending' — meaning the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. This is a genitive of selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). The meaning is: 'of one among these.' 'By synonyms' — by words like '<s>sahaja</s>-<s>pada</s>' etc., when applied among the group of natural-word etc. 'By resorting to another compound member' — the meaning is: by resorting to a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> preceded by a <s>dvandva</s>, as in '<s>umā ca mā ca, umāme, tayoḥ dhavau</s>' etc. 'Of the words <s>chāyā</s> and <s>nihata</s>' — the first is the word <s>chāyā</s> (shadow/beauty), the second the word <s>nihata</s> (struck/slain) — the two illustrations are stated in the order of the thing illustrated. 'Let it be' — the usage of the words <s>chāyā</s> and <s>nihata</s>. 'Of both' — of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> preceded by a <s>dvandva</s>, or the <s>dvandva</s> preceded by a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> — such is the meaning. And this, though stated with reference to the illustration, should be extended to the thing illustrated as well. For in the thing illustrated, the construal is: conformity to the definition of a <s>dvandva</s> preceded by a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>, or a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> preceded by a <s>dvandva</s>, is possible. 'Because of being for that purpose' — this was stated in the discussion of the predicate-examination. 'With as many [words]' — the meaning is: words. 'By resorting to the definition of <s>tatpuruṣa</s>' — in the present context, the precedence of the <s>dvandva</s>-definition should be known. Similarly, in 'thus not the <s>dvandva</s>-definition,' the precedence of the <s>tatpuruṣa</s>-definition should be understood. 'Of that' — of the <s>dvandva</s>. 'Not of that class' — where there is no suspicion of a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> — '<s>Pārvatī</s>-'
