children.text: rekhā hīti rekhā maryādā avadhiḥ sīmeti paryāyāḥ / tatra heyapakṣapratikṣepeṇa prayogo yathā saṃsāreti / atra saṃsārasaṃbhavasya nirākaraṇam iti heyasya pratikṣepaḥ / upādeyaparigraho yathā tvaṣṭur iti / atra saṃpadaḥ prasaro vistāra ity upādeyasya parigrahaḥ / indūdayasyeva saṃnibhā yasyeti atra saṃnibhāśabdaḥ prabhāparyāyo vyākhyātaḥ / yathā tu dāṇḍo granthas tathā saṃnibhaśabdaḥ sadṛśaparyāyo 'sti tad uktam -
children.translated_text: '<s>Rekhā</s>' means boundary, limit, border — these are synonyms. There, the usage by way of rejecting the undesirable side, as in '<s>saṃsāra</s>' (worldly existence) — here, the refutation of the possibility of worldly existence is the rejection of the undesirable. The acceptance of the desirable side, as in '<s>tvaṣṭuḥ</s>' (of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>) — here, the spread, the extension, of prosperity is the acceptance of the desirable. '<s>Indūdayasyeva saṃnibhā yasya</s>' (whose [beauty is] like the moonrise) — here the word '<s>saṃnibha</s>' is explained as a synonym of 'radiance' (<s>prabhā</s>). But just as the work of <s>Daṇḍin</s> [states], the word '<s>saṃnibha</s>' is a synonym of 'similar' (<s>sadṛśa</s>); it has been said —

body.translated_text: In such [cases], it is a counterpart-simile (<s>prativastūpamā</s>) — he says. For here, in the absence of the word '<s>iva</s>' etc., there is sentence-division. Through the status of being contextual and non-contextual,

body.text: "ivavad vāyathāśabdāḥ samānanibhasaṃnibhāḥ /"
body.translated_text: 'The words <s>iva</s>, <s>vā</s>, <s>yathā</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>nibha</s>, and <s>saṃnibha</s> [convey comparison].'

children.text: [Page 48]
children.translated_text: [Page 48]

children.text: iti / tadanusāreṇendūdayena sadṛśa indūdayasaṃnibha iti vyākhyeyam / taduktyaiveti avahitatvoktyety arthaḥ / mūḍhacetana iti
children.translated_text: Following that, it should be explained as: similar to the moonrise, i.e., <s>indūdayasaṃnibha</s>. 'By that very statement' — the meaning is: by the statement of being established. '<s>Mūḍhacetana</s>' (one of deluded consciousness) —
[Section 80]

children.text: mūḍhadhiya iti ca mohanāmno mūḍhatvasya buddhidharmatvāt cetanadhīśabdayoḥ paunaruktyam / tatsaṃbandhāt tadavagatir iti cetanasaṃbandhāc caitanyāvagatir ity arthaḥ / kṛpāmṛdur iti / kṛpā cetanadharma iti caitanyavācipadaṃ na kṛtam / evaṃ "mūḍhāḥ" "mūḍhaḥ" ity atrāpi vācyam / uditavapuṣīti paunaruktyam evānusaṃdhatte / (manaḥkartṛkatvaṃ pramodaḥ?) kriyākaraṇaśabdayor iti atra gauḥ śābaleya itivac chokakriyāśabdayoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvena prayogaḥ / granthakṛtas tu viśeṣasyaivopayogāt sāmānyāvyabhicārāc ca kriyāśabdasya vaiyarthyam karaṇaśabdasya kriyāvācitvān niṣphalatvam iti śokaśabda eva karttavya ity abhiprāyaḥ / anubhavaviśeṣātmatvopagama iti saugataprakriyayaitad uktam / vaiśeṣikās tu jaḍam evātmaguṇam ekārthasamavāyinā jñānena grāhyaṃ sukham āhuḥ / tatprakriyāyāṃ kartavyam evānubhavagrahaṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mūḍhadhī</s>' (of deluded intellect) — since delusion (<s>mūḍhatva</s>), being a property of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), [creates] redundancy (<s>paunaruktya</s>) between the words '<s>cetana</s>' (consciousness) and '<s>dhī</s>' (intellect). 'From its connection, the cognition of that' — from connection with consciousness, the cognition of consciousness — such is the meaning. '<s>Kṛpāmṛdu</s>' (tender with compassion) — because compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) is a property of the conscious, the word denoting consciousness is not [separately] made. Similarly, in '<s>mūḍhāḥ</s>' and '<s>mūḍhaḥ</s>' (deluded [ones]), this should also be stated. '<s>Uditavapuṣī</s>' (one whose body has risen/appeared) — he continues the discussion of redundancy. 'Of the words for action and instrument' — here, just as [in the relation of] 'cow' and '<s>śābaleya</s>' (the spotted one), the two words 'grief' (<s>śoka</s>) and 'action' (<s>kriyā</s>) are used in a general-particular relationship. But the text-author's intent is: since only the particular is useful, and since the general does not deviate [from it], the word 'action' (<s>kriyā</s>) is superfluous; and the word 'instrument' (<s>karaṇa</s>), being a conveyor of action, is fruitless — therefore only the word '<s>śoka</s>' (grief) should be used. 'The acceptance that [pleasure] is of the nature of a particular experience' — this is stated according to the Buddhist (<s>Saugata</s>) system. The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, however, say that pleasure is inert, a quality of the self (<s>ātman</s>), grasped by cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) co-inhering in the same entity. In that system, the inclusion of 'experience' is indeed necessary.
[Section 81]

children.text: ekasyeti sāgarasya / itarasya ceti uttārārthasya / tadrūpatāvagater ity ubhayatra vācyam / madirādraveti / atra samābhātīty ekaṃ padaṃ gaṇitam upasargāṇāṃ dyotyapāratantryeṇa pṛthakpadārhatvābhāvāt / ekādiprayoge satīti ekasya prayogābhyupagame 'nyeṣām eva tattvam / tatrāpy ekatvam aniyatam / evaṃ dvayos trayāṇām ityādiyojanā kāryā, tatrāpy aniyatatvena prakārabahutvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Of the one' — of the ocean. 'And of the other' — of the one who wishes to cross. 'From the cognition of its nature' — should be stated in both cases. '<s>Madirādrava</s>' (the flowing of wine) — here, '<s>samābhāti</s>' (shines alike) is counted as a single word, because the prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>), being dependent on what they indicate, do not deserve separate word-status. 'When there is the usage of one etc.' — when the usage of one [word] is conceded, the truth [applies] only to the others. And even there, the oneness is not fixed. Similarly, the construal 'of two, of three' etc. should be made, since there too, because of the unfixed nature, the varieties are many.
[Section 82]

children.text: avivekaprayuktam iti / yady apy avimṛśyakāritvasyaivāpatkaraṇatvaṃ, tathāpy avivekasyāvimṛśyakāritvaprayojakatvāt tasya kāraṇatve 'py avimṛśyakāritvam eva kāraṇam uktaṃ bhavati / na hīti yasmin sati "vahnau dhūma" ityādike pratibandhakā(la?)bhāviny anvaye sati viśeṣaṇasya yasya "asati vahnau na dhūma" ityādivyatirekasya gatiḥ pratītiḥ, tasyānvayasya sa eva vyatireko hetur yuktaḥ vayavasthitasya hetuhetumadbhāvasya vaiparītyaprasaṅgāt / anvayapratītihetuko hi vyatirekapratītyupakramo na tu viparyayaḥ / viśeṣaṇāc ceti guṇalubdhā iti sādhāraṇatvād ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Caused by indiscrimination' (<s>avivekaprayukta</s>) — although it is acting-without-reflection (<s>avimṛśyakāritva</s>) itself that is the cause of [poetic] disaster, nevertheless, because indiscrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) is the cause of acting-without-reflection, even though indiscrimination is the [ultimate] cause, it is acting-without-reflection that is stated as the [proximate] cause. 'For not' — in the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the type 'where there is fire, there is smoke,' when there is no obstructing [factor], [there is] the cognition of the qualifier; and [in] the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) 'where there is no fire, there is no smoke' — the positive concomitance itself is the proper cause of the negative concomitance, because the determined cause-effect relationship would be reversed [otherwise]. For the positive concomitance is the basis for the beginning of the negative concomitance's cognition, not the reverse. 'And from the qualifier' — '<s>guṇalubdhā</s>' (attracted by qualities) — the meaning is: because of [its] commonality.
[Section 83]

children.text: sāmarthyeti / dvividhaṃ paunaruktyam arthagataṃ śabdagataṃ ceti / tatrārthasya sāmarthyasiddhatve 'rthagataṃ gauṇam āmukhe paunaruktyānavabhāsāt / śabdagatam āsukhāvabhāsamānatvād mukhyam / prakṛtipratyayārthasyeti prakṛtyarthaḥ pratyayārthaḥ prakṛtipratyayasamudāyārtha iti vyastasamastatvena yojyam / evaṃ prakṛteḥ pratyayasya cety atrāpi vācyam / anyathā prāṅnirdiṣṭasya pañcavidhasya paunaruktyasyāsaṅgrahaḥ syāt / vihitasyeti / vastuvṛttyā sthitasya bahuvrīher yā karmadhārayaśaṅkā tayā matvarthīyādiḥ śabdaḥ kṛto bisakisalayacchedapātheyavanta ityādau / tasya sphuṭaṃ paunaruktyaṃ vṛttidvayasya gauravāt / yasminn iti "jāmbavapallavā(dau?)nī"tyādau yasmin pallavaśabda ity arthaḥ / (arthaḥ) (yatra + tyalakṣaṇo?) yattaddhitotpattiḥ yasmād aṇpratyayākhyāt taddhitād utpattiḥ pratītiviṣayatvāpattir yasyārthasya / tadantas taddhitapratyayānto jāmbavaśabdādiḥ / tenaiva pallavaśabdena na samasanīyaḥ, jambūpallavānīti samāsena gatatvāt taddhitavaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt / viśeṣaṇavaśād iti / pinākapāṇyādiviśeṣaṇamāhātmyāt / viśiṣṭam utkarṣāpakarṣavantaṃ saṃjñinaṃ harādikaṃ yatrecchet na tatra paunaruktyam / anyathā tu paunaruktyam / yathā "pāyāt sa śītakiraṇā
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>sāmarthya</s>' (semantic capacity): Repetition is twofold — meaning-based and word-based. There, when the meaning is established through [its own] capacity, the meaning-based [repetition] is secondary, since repetition is not apparent at the outset. Word-based [repetition] is primary, since it is immediately apparent. 'Of the meaning of the stem and suffix' should be construed in both individual and collective senses — the stem-meaning, the suffix-meaning, and the combined meaning of stem and suffix. Likewise, 'of the stem and of the suffix' should also be said. Otherwise there would be no inclusion of the previously stated fivefold repetition. 'Of what has been prescribed' — when for a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound established by the nature of things, there is a suspicion of its being a <s>karmadhāraya</s>, and thereby a <s>matvarthīya</s> suffix and the like is added, as in '<s>bisakisalayacchedapātheyavantaḥ</s>' (having the provisions of cutting lotus-stalks) and the like — its repetition is manifest, due to the awkwardness of the double formation. 'In which' — in '<s>jāmbavapallavā</s>' and the like, the word '<s>pallava</s>' — this is the meaning. Where the <s>taddhita</s> suffix arises from [a base], the <s>aṇ</s>-suffix, from which the meaning is perceived — the [word] ending in that <s>taddhita</s> suffix, such as '<s>jāmbava</s>' (relating to the <s>jambū</s> tree), should not be compounded with that very word '<s>pallava</s>' (shoot), since it is already contained in the compound '<s>jambūpallavāni</s>' (shoots of the <s>jambū</s> tree), and there would be the problem of rendering the <s>taddhita</s> meaningless. 'Due to the qualifier' — due to the greatness of qualifiers such as '<s>pinākapāṇi</s>' (trident-handed). Where one wishes a named entity such as <s>Hara</s> qualified with excellence or inferiority, there is no repetition. Otherwise there is repetition. As in '<s>pāyāt sa śītakiraṇā</s>—'

children.text: [Page 49]
children.translated_text: [Page 49]

children.text: bharaṇo bhavo va(ḥ)" ityādau / sakṛd eveti sāmyābhidhāyī ivaśabdādiḥ / "niryāya vidye"tyādau / yadvad iti dṛṣṭāntamukhena "janair ajātaskhalanair" ityādi saṅgṛhītam / arthasyeti "rāhustrīratanayor" ityādau / yadvaśād iti "tajjigīrṣur ive"tyādau / athavā yatra kārakaviśeṣavaśāt kriyāyāḥ pratītiḥ kriyāviśeṣavaśād vā kārakasya, tatra kriyākārakayoḥ prayogo na kārya ity ayam arthaḥ / yathā "mā bhavantam" ityādau / yo yaddharmeti "aparadiggaṇike"tyādau yo diglakṣaṇo 'rtho yaddharmasya gaṇikādharmasya niṣkāsanāder upacāreṇopalakṣitaḥ / tathā "ambunidher mamanthe" ityādau yasya kāmukasya saṃbandhaṃ yad hṛdayādi te(tya?)nānvito 'mbudhilakṣaṇo yaś cārthaḥ, tasya tadrūpaṇā(d?) gaṇikākāmukarūpaṇā(t na?) śābdī / neṣyate / ārthī punar iṣyata eva / prayuktāntargatair eveti "madirādrave"tyādau / kartari iti pradhānabhūte rājādau kartari / tatkriyāyāṃ ca khaḍgena cchadakriyāyāṃ rūḍhāyāṃ sādhakatamasya khaḍgasya yāni bahūni tadapekṣayāṅgāni dhārāvinipātādīni teṣāṃ vāg vacanaṃ neṣyate yathā "karakalite"tyādau / etad uktaṃ bhavati / rājādau karttari cchedādikriyāyāṃ yat sādhakatamaṃ khaḍgādyaṅgaṃ tasyāpy aṅgānāṃ dhārāvinipātādīnāṃ vacanaṃ neṣyate tenaivāṅgena pradhānabhūtenāvāntarāṅgānām apy ākṣepād /
children.translated_text: '<s>bharaṇo bhavo vaḥ</s>' (may he be your sustenance and existence) and the like. 'Only once' — the word <s>iva</s> (like) and the like which express similarity. In '<s>niryāya vidye</s>—' and the like. '<s>Yadvat</s>' (just as) — by way of illustration, '<s>janair ajātaskhalanaiḥ</s>' (by persons who have never stumbled) and the like are included. 'Of the meaning' — in '<s>Rāhu-strīratanayoḥ</s>' and the like. 'By whose force' — in '<s>tajjigīrṣur iva</s>—' and the like. Or alternatively, where through a particular <s>kāraka</s> (case-relation) the action is perceived, or through a particular action the <s>kāraka</s> [is perceived], there the use of both action and <s>kāraka</s> should not be made — this is the meaning. As in '<s>mā bhavantam</s>' and the like. 'Which [entity] has which property' — in '<s>aparadiggaṇike</s>' and the like, the entity characterized as a direction, indicated metaphorically by the property of the courtesan, namely expulsion and the like. Likewise in '<s>ambunidher mamanthe</s>' (he churned the ocean) and the like — the entity characterized as an ocean, connected with the heart and the like which are the relationships of the lover — its representation and the representation of the courtesan-lover [do not constitute] verbal [repetition]. This is not accepted [as verbal repetition]. But meaning-based [repetition] is indeed accepted. 'By those already contained in the usage' — in '<s>madirādrave</s>—' and the like. 'In the agent' — when the agent is the principal entity such as a king. And regarding his action, when the cutting action with a sword has become conventionally established, the many subordinate elements related to it — the fall of the edge and the like — their verbal expression is not desirable, as in '<s>karakalite</s>' and the like. What is said is this: when the agent is a king and the like, and the principal subsidiary instrument is a sword and the like for the action of cutting — the expression of its further subordinate parts, such as the fall of the edge, is not desirable, since even those subsidiary parts are implied by that very principal subsidiary.

children.text: doṣadvayaṃ "prayukte"ti "karttari" iti ca pratipāditam / te iti samāsāḥ / vṛttāv iti / samāse vākye vā asādhāraṇaṃ yatra viśeṣaṇaṃ tatra viśeṣyaṃ na vācyaṃ yathā "duḥkhānubhave"tyādau / yo yadātmeti bāṣpāder jalādirūpatvāvyabhicārāt prayojanābhāve jalādipadaprayogā na kārya ity arthaḥ / yathā "nayane bāṣpavāriṇe"tyādau / yo yasyeti yo niṣyandanādiḥ yasya candrakāntāder dharmiṇo 'vyabhicārī dharmaḥ tayoḥ samāso na praśasyate, yathā "dviṣadvadhūlocane"tyādau / anyathā iti / sādharmyārtha ity arthaḥ / kriyeti kriyāyāḥ śokādilakṣaṇāyāḥ pratītiḥ karaṇapratītiṃ na vyabhicarati karaṇam eva yataḥ kriyā / tadapratītau karaṇāpratītau saiva śokādilakṣaṇā kriyā na niścitā syād ekatvāt / tyāgakriyety atraitad eva kriyāśabdapravṛttinimittam / tat tasmāt / (ta?)(ya)dvaśāt śokādiśabdaprayogavaśād yasya karaṇasya vyaktiḥ prakāśas taduktau śākādiśabdaprayoge tat karaṇādi(vat?) padaṃ na prayuñjītety arthaḥ, yathā "śokakriyākaraṇasye"tyādau / prayukte ceti prakṛtyādipaunaruktyānāṃ caturṇām upasaṃhāraḥ / anyonyeti vākyapaunaruktyasaṃgrahaḥ / ubhayor uktir ekasya ubhayamadhyāt kasya cit / paunaruktyaṃ nātikrāmati / yathā "sahasā vidadhīte"tyādau //
children.translated_text: The twofold fault has been established in [the verses beginning with] '<s>prayukte</s>' and '<s>kartari</s>.' 'Those' means compounds. 'In composition' — in either a compound or a sentence, where the qualifier is unique, there the qualified should not be stated, as in '<s>duḥkhānubhave</s>' and the like. 'Which is of what nature' — since tears (<s>bāṣpa</s>) and the like invariably have the form of water and the like, in the absence of a purpose, words like '<s>jala</s>' (water) should not be used — this is the meaning. As in '<s>nayane bāṣpavāriṇe</s>' (eyes filled with tearful water) and the like. 'Which of which' — that which is an invariable property of a substance-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) such as moonstone — such as exuding [moisture] — the compound of the two is not commendable, as in '<s>dviṣadvadhūlocane</s>' and the like. 'Otherwise' means for the purpose of showing similarity. 'Action' — the perception of an action characterized by grief and the like does not deviate from the perception of the instrument, since the instrument is the very source of the action. When that [instrument] is not perceived, that very action characterized by grief and the like would not be established, due to their unity. 'The action of renunciation' — here, this very thing is the ground for the use of the word 'action.' 'Therefore' — from that. Due to the use of words like '<s>śoka</s>' (grief) and the like, the manifestation of the instrument [being already implied], when expressing it, one should not use words for the instrument and the like, as in '<s>śokakriyākaraṇasya</s>' and the like. 'And when used' — this is the conclusion of the four [types] of stem-etc. repetition. 'Mutual' — this includes sentence-level repetition. The statement of both, or of one from among both — [this degree of] repetition does not exceed [the bounds of the fault]. As in '<s>sahasā vidadhīte</s>' and the like.

body.text: evaṃ paunaruktyaṃ saprapañcaṃ vicārya vācyāvacanaṃ prapañcayitum āha - vācyasyāvacanaṃ yatheti / asamāsena nirdeśo vakṣyamāṇam etatsamānanyāyam avācyasya vacanam api kaṭākṣayitum / idamā parāmarśa iti abādhitapratyakṣanimittatvād bhrāntinivṛtteḥ pratyakṣasya ca viṣayamukhena parāmarśārhatvāt / tasya yat svaśabdena vacanam iti pūrvaṃ saty eva sarvanāmni punaḥ svaśabdena pratipādanaṃ -
body.translated_text: Having thus examined repetition in detail, in order to elaborate on non-expression of the expressible (<s>vācyāvacana</s>), he says '<s>vācyasyāvacanaṃ yathā</s>' (the non-expression of the expressible, as follows). The specification without a compound is also meant to glance at the expression of the inexpressible (<s>avācyasya vacana</s>), which will follow and has the same rationale. 'The reference by this' — since the cause [of the reference], namely direct perception, is unobstructed, error is removed; and since direct perception is worthy of pronominal reference through its object. 'The expression of it by its own word' — that is, even when a pronoun is available, the designation again by its own word —

children.text: "sarvanāmaparāmarśayogyasyārthasya yat punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The re-designation by the word's own [form] of a meaning

children.text: svaśabdenābhidhānaṃ sā śabdasya punaruktatā" //
children.translated_text: that is worthy of pronominal reference — that is verbal repetition."

body.text: iti punaruktam uktam / idānīṃ tu sarvanāmasthanīyatvena svaśabdena vacanaṃ vācyāvacanam ucyate /

children.text: dharmidharmeti dharmī haralakṣaṇo 'rthaḥ / dharmaḥ kapālasaṃbandhena garhitatvam / ubhayaṃ dharmidharmātma
children.translated_text: 'Substance-possessor and property' — the substance-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) is the meaning characterized by <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). The property (<s>dharma</s>) is the reproachability [arising] from [his] association with a skull. Both [together form] a substance-property [unity].

children.text: [Page 50]
children.translated_text: [Page 50]

children.text: kam / viśeṣapratipattaya iti garhitatvam atra viśeṣaḥ / tasyeti garhitatvasya / evaṃ tasya vivakṣitety atra jñeyam / vivakṣito 'rthaḥ śocyatālakṣaṇaḥ / ārtha iti viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa bhāvāt / vāmalocanātvam iti / na cātra vāmalocaneti viśeṣyapadam / yato ('pi?) yattacchabdadvayotthāpitavākyārthadvayasāmarthyān nāyikālakṣaṇasya viśeṣyasya pratītiḥ / viśeṣaṇam evātra vāmalocanāpadam / tṛtīya iti ubhayavṛttitvākhyaḥ / na cāsāv iti āvṛttiḥ / na caiṣām iti tenaiva tatparyāyeṇa sarvanāmnā cety eṣāṃ prakārāṇām / alpadoṣatvād iti / tasyeti vyavahitasaṃbandhāt kiṃ cid utkṛṣṭatvam / tasya samāgamaprārthanayeti vācyam / arthabhedād iti / ayam arthaḥ ekasyāsakṛdvṛttā (sarvā?) vāvṛttiḥ, yathā daridrāṇāṃ bhojane kāṃsyapātryāḥ / tad uktam - "āvṛttir asakṛdvṛttiḥ" iti / na cārthabhede śabdasyaikatvaṃ nyāyyam arthabhedasya pradhānabhūtasya guṇabhūtaṃ śabdaṃ prati bhedaka(tvam?) (tvāt) / tasmād atra dvayoḥ śabdayor vastuvṛttena yat sādṛśyaṃ yaś ca sādṛśyahetukaḥ pratipattṛṛṇām ekatābhramaḥ, tannibandhano 'yaṃ mukhya evāvṛttivyavahāra iti / ataś ceti / yata āvṛttir na yujyate, tata ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the apprehension of the particular' — here the reproachability is the particular. 'Of that' means of the reproachability. Thus it should be understood also in 'of that which is intended.' The intended meaning is characterized by pitiableness. 'Meaning-based' — because it arises through the qualifier. '<s>Vāmalocanā</s>-hood' (beautiful-eyed-ness) — here '<s>vāmalocanā</s>' is not the word for the qualified. Since the perception of the qualified, namely the heroine, arises from the capacity of the two sentence-meanings raised by the pair of <s>yat</s>- and <s>tat</s>-pronouns. The word '<s>vāmalocanā</s>' here is the qualifier alone. 'The third' is named after [its] being common to both [types]. 'Nor is that' means repetition. 'Nor of these' — [namely] of these types, [expressed] by that very [word], by its synonym, or by a pronoun. 'Because of being a minor fault' — 'of that' means somewhat elevated [in severity] due to mediated connection. 'For his meeting-request' should be supplied. 'Due to the difference of meaning' — the meaning is: the recurrence (<s>āvṛtti</s>) of one [word] used repeatedly — like a bronze bowl at a meal for the poor — is total repetition. As stated: '<s>āvṛtti</s> is repeated occurrence.' But it is not proper for a word to be identical when the meaning differs, since the difference of meaning, being principal, is the differentiator for the word, which is subordinate. Therefore the similarity between the two words in actuality, and the mistaken impression of identity in the perceivers caused by that similarity — based on that, this is properly called repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>). 'And therefore' — since repetition is not appropriate — that is the meaning.

children.text: dharmidharmobhayātmakam iti / ubhayamaye vastuni prati(padya?)ta
children.translated_text: 'Consisting of substance-possessor, property, or both' — when a thing consisting of both is apprehended —

children.text: ⟨pratipatsitaḥ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [variant: '<s>pratipatsitaḥ</s>' (intended to be apprehended) conjectured by the editor]

children.text: ity arthaḥ / yatrānyasyetyādinā / vācyāvacanodāharaṇaprasaṅgena śleṣaṃ guṇadoṣavattayā vitataṃ vicārayati / alakālīti / alakāny evāḷikulam alakasadṛśaṃ cālikulam / chado 'dharaḥ patrāṇi ca / āmodaḥ praharṣaḥ saurabhaṃ ca / karṇikā karṇābharaṇaṃ bījakośaś ca / na śleṣasyeti / nanu śleṣaprastāve kaḥ prasaṅgo 'bjasyopamānacarcāyām / naitat / alaṅkārāntaraviviktaviṣayābhāvena sarvālaṅkārāpavādatvāc śleṣasyopamāpratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣa evātra nyāyyo nopamety abhiprāyaḥ / ata eva śleṣe tu tasya vācyatayety uktam / (nibandha iti) nibadhnantīti nirdiṣṭaḥ / tatsāmyaṃ rajjvādisāmyam / na śleṣasyeti upamāśleṣasyety arthaḥ / tena rajjvādipratipādakaṃ guṇā iveti (na) vācyam / nanu viśeṣaṇasāmyanibandhanā samāsoktir na ca nibadhnantīti viśeṣaṇam ity āha na hi viśeṣaṇasāmyam eveti / etac cāsmābhir harṣacaritavārtike nirṇītam iti tata evāvadhāryam / pṛthak tam upādāyeti tacchabdena śaśī parāmṛṣṭaḥ / sa hy ārtha eveti upamānopameyabhāvaḥ / śleṣaviṣaye iti / atra tisraḥ kakṣyāḥ / rājaśabdasyobhayārthatvāc śleṣaḥ / tadanāśrayaṇenendunā rūpaṇaṃ tatpṛṣṭhe cendur ivety upamā / nanu rājendur ity atra tūpamārūpakayor ekaparigrahe sādhakabādhakābhāvāt saṅkaro nyāyyaḥ, na niyamena rūpakam / tat katham uktaṃ "rūpakam āsūtritam" iti / ucyate / prakramyamāṇopamābhiprāyāt paunaruktyabhayena rūpakam āśritam / upamāyā abhāve tu saṅkara evātra yuktaḥ / yad vopamāpekṣayā rūpakasyātra samāse sphuṭatvena pratīte rūpakaṃ saṃśritam / anenaiva hy abhiprāyeṇa vakṣyati "rūpakasya viṣaye upamāyā yathe"ti / tābhyāṃ spardhitum iti / (rūpakaṃ?) śleṣarūpakābhyām / tayor yathāpūrvam iti / upamāpekṣayā rūpakasya rūpakāpekṣayā śleṣasyety arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: — this is the meaning. By "where of another" etc. — incidentally to the examples of expressibility and non-expressibility (<s>vācyāvacana</s>), he examines <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) extensively as possessing both merit and fault. Regarding <s>alakālī</s> — the curls themselves are a swarm of bees (<s>aḷikula</s>), and also a swarm of bees resembling curls. <s>Chada</s> means the lower lip and also leaves. <s>Āmoda</s> means delight and also fragrance. <s>Karṇikā</s> means an ear-ornament and also a seed-pod. "Not of <s>śleṣa</s>" — now, in a discussion of <s>śleṣa</s>, what occasion is there for discussing the lotus as a standard of comparison? Not so. The intent is: since <s>śleṣa</s>, lacking a domain separate from other figures, is the exception to all figures, the cause for the arising of the simile's counterpart is the <s>śleṣa</s> itself — it is <s>śleṣa</s> that is proper here, not simile. For this very reason it was said: "But in <s>śleṣa</s>, its expressibility." "Binding" (<s>nibandha</s>) — those that bind (<s>nibadhnanti</s>) is [the derivation] stated. "That similarity" means similarity to a rope etc. "Not of <s>śleṣa</s>" means: not of the <s>upamā</s>-<s>śleṣa</s> (simile-paronomasia) — this is the meaning. Therefore one should not say that "like qualities" (<s>guṇā iva</s>) conveys rope-like attributes. Now, <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) is based on the similarity of qualifiers — but "those that bind" is not a qualifier — [to this] he says: "For it is not the case that only qualifier-similarity [is the basis]." And this has been decided by us in the commentary on the <s>Harṣacarita</s>, so it should be ascertained from there. "Separately, having taken that up" — by the <s>tat</s>-pronoun, the moon is referred to. "For that is indeed semantic" — that is, the relation of standard and object of comparison. "In the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>" — here there are three layers: since the word <s>rāja</s> (king/moon) has both meanings, there is <s>śleṣa</s>; without relying on that, the metaphorical identification with the moon constitutes <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor); and on top of that, "like the moon" constitutes simile. Now, in <s>rājenduḥ</s> (king-moon), since in the single acceptance of simile and metaphor there is no basis for deciding one over the other, a conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>) would be appropriate — not necessarily metaphor alone. Then how was it said "metaphor is strung together"? The answer is: because of the intent of the simile being introduced [already], metaphor was adopted out of fear of redundancy. But in the absence of simile, conflation alone would be proper here. Or alternatively, because metaphor is clearly perceived here in the compound more prominently than simile, metaphor was adopted. It is with this very intent that he will say: "In the domain of metaphor, as simile" etc. "To compete with those two" — with <s>śleṣa</s> and metaphor. "Of those two, in order" — means: metaphor in relation to simile, and <s>śleṣa</s> in relation to metaphor — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Thus repetition was stated [before]. Now, however, the expression by its own word in the capacity of [standing for] a pronoun is called non-expression of the expressible (<s>vācyāvacana</s>).

children.text: [Page 51]
children.translated_text: [Page 51]

children.text: nanv evaṃ satīti / asya doṣasyātiprasaṅgaṃ brūte / tāpa ātapo 'pi / phalaṃ śālyādikam api / sumanasaḥ puṣpāṇy api / khalatā durjanatvaṃ, dhānyādikṣodanasthānaṃ ca / asatī dūṣaṇīyā aśobhanā ca / yadalaṅkāreti / khalatām ityādāv upamotthāpite śleṣe nopamā śleṣaṃ bādhate / tasya viviktaviṣaytvābhāvāt / śleṣas tu tām bādhate iti yuktam / asya nyāyasyālaṅkārāntare 'pi bhāvād vyāptigarbham uktaṃ yad alaṅkāreti / nibandhanāntarābhāve iti / sati samāsoktyādinibandhane pūrvavat śleṣottāpitopamā na kartavyā syāt / na cātrānirākṛtetyādiviśeṣaṇasāmyāt samāsoktir iti vācyam / viśeṣaṇānāṃ niyatopamānagāmitvāpratīteḥ / (atra?) viṣayatāśaṅkaiveti upamāviṣayatvasaṃbhāvanety arthaḥ / kva cit tu tada[tadv]iṣayateti pāṭhaḥ / tatra śleṣaviṣayatvam upamāviṣayatvaṃ ca yugapan na śaṅkanīyaṃ tayor utsargāpavā(de?)(dabhāve) na vyavasthiter ity arthaḥ / uktadoṣadvayeti / uktaṃ yac śleṣaviṣaye doṣadvayaṃ - yatra samāsoktiviṣaye śleṣaḥ kṛtaḥ śleṣaviṣaye copameti, tasyātra saṃbandhābhāvād ity arthaḥ / yadalaṅkāreti / śleṣopamādīnām alaṅkārāṇām abhivyaktyarthaṃ ye śabdā abjam ivetyādayaḥ tebhyo 'laṅkārebhya itaraḥ samāsoktiśleṣādiḥ tair eva śabdaiḥ alpatarair abjam ivetyādirahitair yadi vyajyeta tadāsau samāsoktiśleṣādir laghutvād grāhyo, nāparaḥ śleṣopamādir ity arthaḥ / nanu śobhātiśayahetutvam alaṅkārāntarāṇāṃ lakṣaṇam / tad viśeṣyate / tat katham idam uktam ity āha - na hy astīti / śobhātiśayajanane nije vyāpāre nāsty alaṅkārāṇāṃ viśeṣaḥ / tataś caiko gṛhyate 'paras tyajyata iti na yuktam / gurulaghutvam āśritya punar yujyata etan nānyatheti tātparyam / vācyātiśayāpekṣayā caitad uktam pratīyamānatvāpekṣayā tu samanantaraṃ viśeṣo vakṣyate / kiṃ cetyādinā kāvyakriyāyāṃ saundaryaniṣpatteḥ prayojakatvam alaṅkāraniṣpatteś ca (anuniṣpāditaṃ yathā vaktā vedanācāmayoḥ?) ity āha / samāsoktiśleṣabhaṅgibhyām eveti / samāsoktyā tu "(ala)kālī"tyādau / śleṣeṇa "bhairavācārya" ityādau / nopameyeti / alakālītyādāv upamā śleṣopamā / bhairavācārya ityādau upamaivopamā / "atra samāsoktiśleṣabhaṅgibhyām eva" ity etadgranthānusāreṇa "rūpakasya viṣaye upamāyā yathe"tyādigranthaḥ prakṣipta iva lakṣyate / rūpakasyehānupasaṃhārād, "uktadoṣadvayayogānupapatteḥ"
children.translated_text: "But if this is so" — he states the over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>) of this fault. <s>Tāpa</s> also means heat of the sun. <s>Phala</s> also means grain such as rice. <s>Sumanasaḥ</s> also means flowers. <s>Khalatā</s> means wickedness and also the place of threshing grain etc. <s>Asatī</s> means a reprehensible woman and also an unattractive one. "Which figure" (<s>yad alaṅkāra</s>) — when in <s>khalatām</s> etc. a simile is elicited within the <s>śleṣa</s>, the simile does not override the <s>śleṣa</s>, because [<s>śleṣa</s>] does not lack its own separate domain. But <s>śleṣa</s> overrides that [simile] — this is proper. Since this principle applies in other figures as well, the statement is framed in terms of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>): "which figure." "In the absence of another basis" — when there is a basis such as <s>samāsokti</s> etc., a simile elicited by <s>śleṣa</s> should not be produced, as before. Nor should one say that here there is <s>samāsokti</s> due to the similarity of the qualifier "those that do not ward off" (<s>anirākṛta</s>) etc. Because there is no perception that qualifiers necessarily pertain to the standard of comparison. "The apprehension of [its being the] domain" (<s>viṣayatāśaṅkā</s>) means: the suspicion that it is the domain of simile — this is the meaning. In some [manuscripts] the reading is <s>tadviṣayatā</s>. There, one should not simultaneously suspect it to be the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> and the domain of simile, because of those two having the relation of general rule and exception (<s>utsargāpavāda</s>), there is no co-existence — this is the meaning. "The pair of faults stated" — the stated pair of faults regarding the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> — where <s>śleṣa</s> is produced in the domain of <s>samāsokti</s>, and where simile is produced in the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> — because here there is no connection of that [pair] — this is the meaning. "Which figure" — those words such as <s>abjam iva</s> (like a lotus) etc. that serve the manifestation of figures like <s>śleṣa</s>, simile etc. — if by those very words, but fewer ones, without <s>abjam iva</s> etc., another figure such as <s>samāsokti</s>-<s>śleṣa</s> etc. were manifested, then that <s>samāsokti</s>-<s>śleṣa</s> etc. should be accepted because of its lightness, not the other <s>śleṣa</s>-simile etc. — this is the meaning. Now, the defining characteristic of other figures is being the cause of an excess of beauty. That is specified. How then can this be stated? — he says: "For there is not" etc. In their own function of producing an excess of beauty, there is no distinction among the figures. Hence to accept one and reject another is not proper. But relying on heaviness and lightness, this is appropriate and not otherwise — this is the purport. And this has been said with reference to the expressible (<s>vācya</s>); with reference to the suggestible (<s>pratīyamāna</s>), a distinction will be stated immediately after. By "moreover" etc., he states that in poetic creation, the production of beauty is the motivating cause, and the production of figures is [merely consequent] — "by the devices of <s>samāsokti</s> and <s>śleṣa</s> alone." By <s>samāsokti</s>, in <s>alakālī</s> etc. By <s>śleṣa</s>, in <s>bhairavācārya</s> etc. "Not the object of comparison" (<s>nopameya</s>) — in <s>alakālī</s> etc., the simile is a <s>śleṣa</s>-simile. In <s>bhairavācārya</s> etc., the simile is simply a simile. Following the text "here, by the devices of <s>samāsokti</s> and <s>śleṣa</s> alone," the text "in the domain of metaphor, as simile" etc. appears to be interpolated — because metaphor is not concluded here, and because of the text "due to the non-establishment of the pair of stated faults,"

children.text: ⟨°yogāsiddheḥ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>°yogāsiddheḥ</s> (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: ity asya ca pūrvoktagranthasyātra pakṣe (ānatvāt?)
children.translated_text: and because of the earlier text being [insufficient] in this alternative,

children.text: ⟨nyūnatvāt conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>nyūnatvāt</s>, i.e., due to insufficiency (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: ataś caivāyaṃ kva cid ādarśe na paṭhyate / aprakṣepe tu (trirūpaka?)grahaṇam iha kartvyaṃ syāt / tasmāt sa vā grantho nivārya iha vā rūpakagrahaṇaṃ prakṣepyam / "uktadoṣadvaye"ti ca prakṛtaucityena vyākhyātam / te hi tatsiddhīti / rasabandhasiddhāv alaṅkārā avaśyaṃ sidhyantīty arthaḥ / niṣpādakatvam ihānmāpakatvam / ata eva bharate "rasaniṣpattir" ity atra rasānumitir iti vyākhyeyam / tadvaicitryaṃ (vibhāvādivaicitryam /) tadāśrayāḥ paraṃparayā rasāśrayā rasajñaptihetava ity arthaḥ / tenaiṣām iti / kaver arthagataṃ cārutvaṃ tātparyeṇa saṃpādyaṃ, nālaṅkāropanibandhaḥ alaṅkārāṇāṃ tannāntarīyakatvenāprādhā
children.translated_text: for this very reason, in some manuscripts this is not read. But if it is not an interpolation, then the inclusion of the three [types of] metaphor should be made here. Therefore either that text should be removed, or the mention of metaphor should be interpolated here. And "the pair of stated faults" has been explained in accordance with the present context. "For those accomplish that" — when the success of <s>rasabandha</s> (aesthetic composition) is achieved, the figures necessarily succeed — this is the meaning. "Being productive" (<s>niṣpādakatva</s>) here means being indicative (<s>anmāpakatva</s>). For this very reason, in <s>Bharata</s>'s [statement] "the production of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment)," it should be explained as the inference of <s>rasa</s>. "The variety of that" means the variety of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. "Based on that" means: indirectly based on <s>rasa</s>, being the causes of the cognition of <s>rasa</s> — this is the meaning. "Therefore of these" — the poet's beauty pertaining to meaning should be accomplished with that as the ultimate aim, not as a by-product of the figures; because figures, being merely entailed by that [beauty], lack predominance.

children.text: [Page 52]
children.translated_text: [Page 52]

children.text: nyāt / ataś cārutvaṃ yathā niṣpadyate tathā teṣām upanibandhaḥ kāryaḥ / tatprayojanāc cādhānoddharaṇādaya ity arthaḥ / nānvahādhānoddharaṇādaya ity uktyā alaṅkārāṇāṃ parasparaṃ cārutvaniṣpādane viśeṣaḥ pratipāditaḥ / pūrvaṃ ca "na hy asti nije" ityādinā viśeṣābhāva uktaḥ / tat kathaṃ na virodhaḥ / naitat / pūrvam avavadhānena cārutvaniṣpādanaṃ manasikṛtya viśeṣābhāvaḥ pratipāditaḥ / iha tu vibhāvādyupakaraṇatvena gurulaghutvādinā viśeṣa ukta ity apekṣābhedā[n na] virodhaḥ kaś cit /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the production of those [figures] should be arranged in such a way that beauty is produced. And from that purpose, introduction, removal, and the like [follow] — this is the meaning. Furthermore, by the statement "introduction, removal, and the like," a distinction in the mutual production of beauty among the figures has been demonstrated. And previously, by "For there is not, in [their] own [function]" etc., the absence of distinction was stated. How is there no contradiction? Not so. Previously, the absence of distinction was demonstrated with the production of beauty through direct apprehension in mind. But here, a distinction is stated through being instrumental to <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. and through heaviness and lightness — hence, because of the difference of the relevant consideration, there is no contradiction whatsoever.

children.text: kaiś cid iti vāmanaprabhṛtibhiḥ / adhunā yat pratijñāmātreṇa pratipāditaṃ yathā "śabdasya śaktyantarābhāvād vyañjakatvaṃ na saṃbhavati" iti tadvācyāvacanodāharaṇatvopayogi śleṣaprasaṅgenopapādayitum āsūtrayati - sa cāyam iti / yas samāsoktiviṣaye kṛto yasya ca viṣaye upamā kṛtā sa ity arthaḥ / dvividha iti vakṣyamāṇasyobhayaśleṣyaivātrāntarbhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: "By some" — by <s>Vāmana</s> and others. Now, what has been established merely by assertion, namely: "Due to the absence of another power of the word, suggestiveness (<s>vyañjakatva</s>) is not possible" — in order to substantiate that through the pretext of <s>śleṣa</s>, useful for illustrations of expressibility and non-expressibility, he introduces the thread: "And this." "This" — that [<s>śleṣa</s>] which was produced in the domain of <s>samāsokti</s>, and in whose domain simile was produced — "that" is the meaning. "Twofold" — the inclusion of both-paronomasia (<s>ubhayaśleṣa</s>) is herein only.

children.text: ⟨ubhayaśleṣasyātraivāntarbhāvaḥ conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: <s>ubhayaśleṣasyātraivāntarbhāvaḥ</s> (editorial conjecture)]

children.text: / ābhyām eva samuccitābhyāṃ tasyotthāpanāt / yatrānyūneti yatra viśeṣyasya viśeṣaṇaṃ na nyūnībhavati nāpy atiricyate, tatra śleṣaḥ / mātragrahaṇaṃ liṅgavacanānāṃ bhedād ubhayasaṃbandhasahiṣṇuśabdatāparigrahārtham / kartṛkarmeti / kartṛkarmarūpaḥ ādigrahaṇāt kriyārūpo yatra pradhānabhūto 'rthaḥ śleṣeṇa svarūpahāniṃ nīyate, na tatra śleṣo niravadya ity arthaḥ / tasya ca dharmapratipādakaśabdaviṣayatvena dharmipratipādakaśabdaviṣayatvena ca dvaividhyam / ubhayapratipādakaśabdaviṣayatvaṃ tu dūṣayiṣyate / aparas tv iti / arthaśleṣaḥ / ubhayatrāpi śabdaśleṣe 'rthaśleṣe ca / yāvad ivādi nibandhanaṃ nāśritaṃ tāvad arthāntaram apramāṇakam eveti śleṣābhivyaktyarthaṃ nibandhanam āśrayaṇīyam / atrāntare iti phullamallikābhir dhavalā ye 'ṭṭās tripuracatuṣpuramahāprakārā āpaṇā vā tair vikāso hāso yasya tadvac ca dhavalāṭṭahāso yasya / kusumasamayayugaṃ māsadvayaṃ ramyatvena tatsadṛśa ca yugaṃ kṛtādim upasaṃharan ajṛmbhata vikasitavān vyaktānanaś cābhūd mahākālo dīrghasamayaḥ saṃhartṛdevatāviśeṣaś ca / samāsoktīti / mahākāla ity atra mahāsamaya ity aśliṣṭe viśeṣyapade prayukte viśeṣaṇasāmyād eva devatāviśeṣapratīteḥ samāsoktir bhavantī mahākālaśabdasyāvṛttau pramāṇam / na cātra mahākālaśabde prayukte prayāsaḥ kaś cit / yena "alakālikule"tivat samāsoktyā śleṣasya vaiyarthyaṃ śaṅkyeta / ācchāditeti / parvatapakṣe ācchāditaṃ vaipulyād diśaś cāmbaram ākāśaṃ ca yena, uccakair ucyatāṃ gāṃ bhūmiṃ cākramya vartamānaṃ, mahārohapariṇāhāni śṛṅgāṇi śikharāṇi yasya, tadaucityāc ca śirasi sphurac candralekham, evaṃvidhaṃ nageśaṃ parvatarājaṃ dṛṣṭvā ko na vismito bhavatīty arthaḥ / harapakṣe tu ācchāditaṃ paridhānīkṛta diśa eva (asya nava?) vastraṃ yena, tathā u[k]taṃ sthūlaviṣāṇa ca vṛṣabham adhiruhya sthitaṃ, mastake candrakalānvitaṃ ca nageśa kailāsādhipatiṃ sākṣātkṛtya anugṛhītammanyatvena ko na vismayata ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: —by these two when combined, [the meaning] is brought forth. '<s>Yatrānyūna</s>': where the qualifier of the qualified is neither deficient nor excessive—there is <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). The word '<s>mātra</s>' is employed for the purpose of including words that can sustain both connections despite differences in gender and number. '<s>Kartṛkarma</s>': where the principal meaning in the form of agent, object, and—by the word '<s>ādi</s>'—action, is led to the loss of its own nature through <s>śleṣa</s>, there the <s>śleṣa</s> is not faultless—that is the meaning. And this has two varieties: one pertaining to the word that denotes the property (<s>dharma</s>), and another pertaining to the word that denotes the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). [<s>Śleṣa</s>] pertaining to the word that denotes both will be criticized. '<s>Aparas tu</s>': [refers to] <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (semantic pun). 'In both cases'—in both <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal pun) and <s>arthaśleṣa</s>: as long as a basis such as '<s>iva</s>' etc. has not been adopted, the alternative meaning remains without authority; therefore a basis must be adopted for the manifestation of the <s>śleṣa</s>. '<s>Atrāntare</s>': [the verse describes a city] whose laughter (<s>aṭṭahāsa</s>) is the unfolding of buildings white with full-blown jasmine—the towers, ramparts of the fourfold city, or marketplaces white [with jasmine]; and whose laughter too is the great white pealing—[in the other sense] whose great laughter is one who has white-towered laughter. The pair of flower-months, being lovely, and likewise the pair [of months] resembling them—[<s>Mahākāla</s>] bringing [them] from beginning to end, blossomed forth, became manifest-faced, [denoting both] a great duration of time and a particular destructive deity. '<s>Samāsokti</s>': when the word '<s>Mahākāla</s>' is used, and the unambiguous qualified word '<s>mahāsamaya</s>' ('great time') is employed, since the cognition of the particular deity arises merely from the similarity of qualifiers—<s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) occurs and is the authority for the use of the word '<s>Mahākāla</s>.' And here no effort is required in using the word '<s>Mahākāla</s>,' lest one suspect, as in '<s>Alakālikule</s>,' that the <s>śleṣa</s> is rendered pointless by <s>samāsokti</s>. '<s>Ācchādita</s>': in the mountain-sense: one by whom the directions and the sky are covered by its vastness, standing having occupied the earth from a great height, having peaks of massive height and girth, and with a crescent moon gleaming on its summit befittingly—seeing such a lord of mountains, who is not amazed? In the <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)-sense: one who has made the directions themselves his garment, who stands mounted upon a stout-horned bull, who has a crescent moon on his forehead—seeing the lord of [Mount] [<s>Kailāsa</s>] in person, who does not feel wonder at being graced?

children.text: śveto dhāvatītivad iti śabdatantram / pradīpavad iti punar arthatantram / yathāyogam iti tulyapradhānatvena sādhāraṇyaṃ tantram / atulyapradhānatvena tu prasaṅgaḥ / tayoḥ pratipattir iti / kiṃ cit khalu vastuśaktyaiva kāryakāri yathā dīpādi / kiṃ cit tu parāmarśāpekṣaṃ yathā dhūmādi liṅgam / yatra yasmin viṣaye parāmarśanairapekṣyeṇa vastuśaktyaivobhayakāritvaṃ tatra tantrādi nānyatra / śabdaḥ parāmarśāpekṣo 'rthapratītikārī / parāmarśo na nirnibandhana iti nātra tantrādipravṛttiḥ / ahāryaḥ parvataḥ / sahakāritā saha karaṇaśīlatva sahakārasaṃbandhaś ca / anavamā utkṛṣṭāḥ / navaḥ pratyagraḥ / mādhavo vasantaḥ / ramyatātireketi sahakārasaṃbandharūpa ity arthaḥ / tasya vācyasyeti / tacchabdena nibandhanaṃ parāmṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: 'Like <s>śveto dhāvati</s> (a white [horse] runs)': this is <s>śabdatantra</s> (word-based technique). 'Like a lamp': this is <s>arthatantra</s> (meaning-based technique). '<s>Yathāyogam</s>': when [both are] equally principal, the common [usage] is the technique. When unequally principal, it is incidental. 'The apprehension of those two': some things indeed produce their effect solely by the power of the object itself, like a lamp and the like. Other things, however, require deliberate reflection, like the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of smoke and the like. Where, in whatever domain, both effects are produced by the power of the object alone without requiring reflection—there <s>tantra</s> etc. [apply], not elsewhere. The word requires reflection to produce cognition of meaning. Since reflection is not without a basis, <s>tantra</s> etc. do not apply here. '<s>Ahārya</s>' means 'a mountain.' '<s>Sahakāritā</s>': the nature of being a cooperating factor, and the connection with a cooperating cause. '<s>Anavamāḥ</s>': excellent, unsurpassed. '<s>Navaḥ</s>': fresh. '<s>Mādhavaḥ</s>': spring. '<s>Ramyatātirekā</s>': means having the form of a connection with a cooperating cause. '<s>Tasya vācyasya</s>': the basis is referred to by the <s>tat</s>-word.

children.text: samayasmṛtiḥ saṅketasmaraṇam / asiddham ekatvam iti / tataś ca nāyaṃ tantrāder viṣayaḥ / tattvam ekatvam / avyayānavyayātmakam iti / avyayam ivādi / anavyayaṃ sadṛśādi / dharmārthasyeti / śleṣād abhinnatvam iti yojyam / prakaṭeti / kulayaś caṭakāḥ tad uktam - "kuliḥ kuliṅgaś caṭakaḥ" iti / te ca te śakuntāḥ śakunayaḥ teṣāṃ cakreṇa samūhena bhāsvatīnāṃ valabhīnāṃ hitāḥ anurūpā mattavāraṇāḥ aṅkaḥ cihnaṃ yasyāḥ / niśānto 'ntaḥpuram / viḍambayantī uapahasantī / samarabhūpakṣe kuliśaṃ vajraṃ / kuntāḥ prāsāḥ / cakrāṇi arīṇi / tair bhāsvadbhiḥ / vyatireko viḍambayantīti prakāśitaḥ / prakaṭetyādau ca viśeṣaṇabhāge 'tra śleṣaḥ / uṣasīti / andhakāra eva malinatvāt paṅkaḥ / tasya vigalitasya (plavam avasthānaṃ?)
children.translated_text: '<s>Samayasmṛtiḥ</s>': the recollection of a convention. '<s>Asiddham ekatvam</s>': and therefore this is not the domain of <s>tantra</s> etc. '<s>Tattvam</s>' means oneness. '<s>Avyayānavyayātmakam</s>': <s>avyaya</s> means '<s>iva</s>' and the like; <s>anavyaya</s> means '<s>sadṛśa</s>' ('similar') and the like. '<s>Dharmārthasya</s>': one should connect [this] with 'non-difference due to <s>śleṣa</s>.' '<s>Prakaṭa</s>': <s>kulayāḥ</s> means sparrows, as stated: '<s>kuliḥ kuliṅgaś caṭakaḥ</s>' ('the sparrow is [called] <s>kuli</s>, <s>kuliṅga</s>, <s>caṭaka</s>'). And those are the birds (<s>śakuntāḥ</s> = <s>śakunayaḥ</s>); by their flock (<s>cakreṇa</s> = <s>samūhena</s>), [the city has] brilliant, befitting balconies (<s>valabhī</s>) and intoxicated elephants as its mark. '<s>Niśāntaḥ</s>' means the women's quarters. '<s>Viḍambayantī</s>': mocking. In the battle-king sense: <s>kuliśa</s> = thunderbolt; <s>kuntāḥ</s> = lances; <s>cakrāṇi</s> = discuses (weapons). By those, brilliant [warriors]. The <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is expressed by '<s>viḍambayantī</s>' (mocking). In '<s>prakaṭa</s>' etc., the <s>śleṣa</s> is in the qualifier portion. '<s>Uṣasī</s>': darkness itself, being dirty, is the mud (<s>paṅka</s>). Its dissolution [is] a floating/unstable state

children.text: ⟨plavo 'navasthānam conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: ⟨'<s>plavaḥ anavasthānam</s>' (floating = instability): conj. (Ed.)⟩

children.text: tena śabalaṃ vicitram / ghanavartma viyat / dūram atyartham / madhuraḥ sukumāro yas taraṇitāpo raviprabhā tadyogena tāraṃ hṛdyam / madhupāyino bhramarās teṣāṃ paṅktiḥ / andhakārapaṅkaplava eva vigalanena nissāratvāc chavaḥ tasya laṅghanena vartmasu (pakṣeṣu)
children.translated_text: —by that, variegated (<s>śabala</s>). '<s>Ghanavartma</s>': the sky. '<s>Dūram</s>': exceedingly. '<s>Madhuraḥ</s>': delicate; that which is the sunshine (<s>taraṇitāpa</s> = <s>raviprabhā</s>)—by its contact, [the dawn is] hṛdya (charming), like a star. '<s>Madhupāyinaḥ</s>': bees; their row. The darkness-mud-floating, by its dissolution being insubstantial, is like a corpse; by stepping over it, on the paths (eyelashes)

children.text: dūramā aramaṇīyaśrīḥ / madhuratā makarandāsaktā tathā raṇitā saśabdā, yad vā madhuratena makarandāsaṅgena raṇitaṃ guñjitaṃ yasyāḥ / payogatā jalagatā / aram atyartham / atra ghanavartmaśabdasyopameyavācinaḥ śleṣe 'ntarbhāvāt dharmidharmobhayārthasyodāharaṇatve nyāyye dharmārthasyodāharaṇatvaṃ cintyam /
children.translated_text: —the beauty is exceedingly far [i.e., abundant]. '<s>Madhuratā</s>': attached to nectar, and also resonant/humming; or alternatively: by the sweet attachment to nectar, there is humming. '<s>Payogatā</s>': being in the water. '<s>Aram</s>': exceedingly. Here, since the word '<s>ghanavartma</s>' (cloud-path), which denotes the object of comparison, is absorbed into the <s>śleṣa</s>—while it would be proper for it to serve as an example of both property-bearer and property meanings—its serving as an example of property-meaning alone is to be considered.

children.text: anavarateti / anavarataṃ nayanasalilena sicyamāno vṛddhiṃ nīyamānaḥ / tathā anavarataṃ nayanaṃ prāpaṇaṃ yasya tena salilena sicyamāna ārdratvaṃ prāpyamāṇaḥ / vipado lavaḥ sūkṣmabhāgo vipallavo vigatakisalayaś ca / prarohati vistīrṇībhavati aṅkurāṃś ca muñcati (dharmāṃś ca muñcati?) dharmārthatvam iti / (kila?) atra sthitam api dharmārthatvaṃ nopamānaviśeṣaṇatvāyālaṃ viśeṣaṇatvasya kakṣyāntarabhāvitvāt / na cāvṛttim antareṇa kakṣyāntaraparigraho nyāyyaḥ / na cātrāvṛttiḥ kāryā / pramāṇābhāvāt / anāvṛttau tu tasyām eva kakṣyāyāṃ viśeṣaṇatve upameyasvarūpāpahāraprasaṅga iti padārthaḥ / tasyopameyeti tacchabdena vipallavaśabdaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ / yaḥ punar iti śleṣaprayojakaḥ śabdaḥ / apradhānaṃ viśeṣaṇabhūtam / pradhānasya hi pūrvoktanyāyenāvṛttir nyāyyā / nibandhanam ivādi / sānuparvatasya mā(la)bhūbhāgaḥ / aṅkollākhyās taravaḥ teṣāṃ pallavā bhāsvanto yatra / aṅkollaśabdaḥ prākṛtabhāṣāpadam api kavibhir atiprasiddhyā śleṣādiṣu prayujyate / tathā ca "sakuśāṅkollapallavā / maithilīva śriyaṃ dhatte" iti parimalena prayutam / saṃskṛte punar aṅkoṭhaśabdaḥ sthitaḥ / tathā bhāsvān aṅke ullapan mukharaḥ lavākhyaḥ putro yatreti sāmānyenānyapadārtho gṛhyate / iheti vipallavaśabde / ivādyavyayam iti / tarur iveti prayuktasyevaśabdasyānyathā vyavasthāpayiṣyamāṇatvāt / alaṅkārāntaraṃ samāsoktyādi / pradhānārthasaṃsparśamātrād iti / yataḥ tena padena saṃbhavadapradhānārthenāpi pradhānabhūto 'rthaḥ saṃspṛṣṭaḥ, tato 'ntarasaṃbandhāsahiṣṇutvāt dvirupādānārhatvam / yatra ca pradhānāpradhānobhayārthasya dvirupādānam avaśyaṃ kāryam, tatra daṇḍāpūpikayā tadekārthasya pradhānamātrārthasya śabdasya dvirupādānaṃ nyāyasiddham eva / rucir dīptiḥ abhilāṣaś ca ruciḥ / atra dvau ruciśabdau viśeṣyavācitvāt pradhānārthau / nanūpamānasya yadi viśeṣyatvaṃ nopameyaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ tat katham upameyasaṃbandhiny upamānasya vibhaktiḥ yathā "vāgarthāv iva saṃpṛktau" iti / naiṣa doṣaḥ / viśeṣaṇatvam avacchedakatvaṃ tac copamānasyopameyaṃ praty upamitikriyāyāṃ vidyata eva / anyathā tayoḥ saṃbandhābhāvād ananvyapra
children.translated_text: '<s>Anavarata</s>': being watered continuously by tears of the eyes and brought to growth. Or: having continuous reaching/attaining (<s>nayana</s> = <s>prāpaṇa</s>), and being watered by that moisture—acquiring tenderness. '<s>Vipadaḥ lavaḥ</s>': a tiny portion of misfortune, and one whose sprouts have departed (<s>vigatakisalaya</s>). '<s>Prarohati</s>': expands, and also sends forth shoots (and also gives up [certain] properties?). '<s>Dharmārthatvam</s>': (indeed?) even though the property-meaning status is established here, it does not suffice to make it a qualifier of the standard of comparison, since qualifier-status belongs to a different level. And without repetition, the inclusion of a different level is not appropriate. And repetition should not be made here, for lack of authority. Without repetition, at that same level, if [the word] has qualifier-status, there would be the fault of annihilating the identity of the object of comparison—that is the word-meaning. '<s>Tasyopameya</s>': by the <s>tat</s>-word, the word '<s>vipallava</s>' is referred to. '<s>Yaḥ punar</s>': this is the word that motivates the <s>śleṣa</s>. '<s>Apradhānam</s>': being in the role of qualifier. For of the principal [element], repetition is appropriate by the previously stated rule. '<s>Nibandhanam</s>': '<s>iva</s>' and the like. '<s>Sānuparvata</s>': a foothill region. '<s>Aṅkolla</s>'-named trees, whose shoots are brilliant. The word '<s>aṅkolla</s>' is a <s>Prākṛta</s> term, yet it is used by poets in <s>śleṣa</s> and the like due to its great familiarity. And thus '<s>sakuśāṅkollapallavā / Maithilīva śriyaṃ dhatte</s>' was used by [the author of] the <s>Parimala</s>. In Sanskrit, however, the established form is '<s>aṅkoṭha</s>.' Or: '<s>bhāsvān</s>' (brilliant), '<s>aṅke ullapan</s>' (chattering in the lap), '<s>mukharaḥ</s>' (noisy)—a son named '<s>lava</s>'—where [all this obtains]: thus an alternative word-meaning is grasped in a general way. '<s>Iha</s>': in the word '<s>vipallava</s>.' '<s>Ivādyavyayam</s>': since the '<s>iva</s>'-word employed in '<s>tarur iva</s>' ('like a tree') will be otherwise accounted for. '<s>Alaṅkārāntaram</s>': <s>samāsokti</s> and the like. '<s>Pradhānārthasaṃsparśamātrāt</s>': since by that word, even with its possible non-principal meaning, the principal meaning is touched—therefore, being unable to tolerate another connection, it deserves to be taken up in both ways. And where the taking up of a word in both principal and non-principal meanings must necessarily be done, there by the maxim of '<s>daṇḍāpūpikā</s>' (the stick-and-cake principle), the taking up in both ways of a word that has one [additional] meaning identical with the principal meaning alone is established by reasoning. '<s>Ruciḥ</s>': brightness, and also desire. Here the two [uses of] the word '<s>ruci</s>' are principal meanings since they denote the qualified. Now, if the standard of comparison has the status of qualified and not of qualifier of the object of comparison—then how does the standard of comparison take the case-ending related to the object of comparison, as in '<s>vāgarthāv iva saṃpṛktau</s>' ('united like word and meaning')? This is not a fault. Qualifier-status means being a delimitor, and that is indeed present for the standard of comparison in relation to the object of comparison in the act of comparison. Otherwise, in the absence of their connection, there would be no anvaya-

children.translated_text: [Page 54]

children.text: saṅgaḥ / sthite viśeṣaṇatve tasya na viśeṣyavibhakter hāniḥ kā cit / yat punar ihopamānaśabdasya viśeṣyavācitvam uktaṃ tad dharmitābhiprāyeṇa / dharmī hy upamānam / na ca svatantratvāt viśeṣyārthaḥ / ataś caivāyaṃ "strīva gacchati ṣaṇḍo 'yam" ity upameyaliṅgaṃ na bhajate / dharmavāci tu viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaliṅgam eva / tad uktam - "guṇavacanānām āśrayato liṅgavacanāni bhavanti" iti / tad evam upamānam upameyavibhaktiṃ na (na) bhajate dharmitvaṃ ca na jahātīti / khalatā durjanatvam / khalatā ākāśavallī / atra prayukta iti / tarur ivety atra / vākyabhedaprasaṅgād iti "saṃbhavaty ekavākyatve vākyabhedaś ca neṣyate" iti vākyabhedasya pratipattigauravavattvād dheyatvam / atha samāsoktīti / anavaratajaletyāder viśeṣaṇasya dvyarthatvāt / upamānabhūteti / yatropamānabhūtasya dharmiṇo 'nyasyārthasya gamyamānatvaṃ tatra samāsoktiḥ, na sākṣād upādāna ity arthaḥ / kva cid iti / babhravaḥ kapilāḥ / etad dāvāgni(viśeṣāḥ ++++?)
children.translated_text: [This is] the connection. / When the qualifier status [of the comparison-standard] is established, there is no loss whatsoever of the case-ending of the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>). / Now, what was said here about the comparison-standard word (<s>upamānaśabda</s>) being expressive of the qualified — that is with the intention [that it expresses] the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). / For the comparison-standard is a property-bearer. / And it does not [take] the meaning of the qualified because of its independence. / Hence it is precisely for this reason that in '<s>strīva gacchati ṣaṇḍo 'yam</s>' (This eunuch walks like a woman), [the comparison-standard] does not take the gender of the comparandum (<s>upameya</s>). / But a qualifier that expresses a property (<s>dharma</s>) does take the gender of the qualified. As it is said: 'The gender and number of quality-denoting words follow their substrate.' / Thus, the comparison-standard does not take the case-ending of the comparandum, nor does it abandon its property-bearer status. / '<s>Khalatā</s>' — villainy, or baldness. '<s>Khalatā</s>' — also 'sky-creeper' (a kind of parasitic plant). / 'Here it is used' — in '<s>tarur iva</s>' (like a tree). / 'Because of the implication of sentence-splitting' — since 'when unity of sentence is possible, sentence-splitting is not desired,' sentence-splitting is to be avoided because it involves heaviness of cognition. / 'Now, <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression)' — because the qualifier '<s>anavaratajala</s>' etc. has double meaning. / 'Being the comparison-standard' — Where the meaning of something other [than what is directly stated] is understood as belonging to the property-bearer that is the comparison-standard, there is <s>samāsokti</s> — not direct mention: this is the meaning. / 'In some [cases]' — '<s>babhravaḥ</s>' means tawny, and '<s>kapilāḥ</s>' means brown. These are (particular types of forest fire?)

children.text: ⟨viśeṣaṇaṃ san nakula° conj (Ed)⟩
children.translated_text: [conjectured reading: 'being a qualifier, <s>san nakula</s>-' (Ed.)]

children.text: lakṣaṇam arthaṃ pratipādayatīti dharmidharmobhayātmatvam / evaṃ hariṇā haritā mṛgāś ca / jaṭā mūlāni keśasaṃniveśāś ca / valkalaṃ vṛkṣatvak tatkṛtaṃ ca vāsaḥ / kapilāḥ piṅgalā muniviśeṣā(ś ca) / āropaviṣayabahutvād āropyamānānām api bahutvam /
children.translated_text: [The word] conveys the meaning characterized as [being both] property-bearer and property (<s>dharmin</s> and <s>dharma</s>) — hence its nature as both. / Similarly, '<s>hariṇa</s>' — green, and also deer. / '<s>Jaṭā</s>' — roots, and also matted hair arrangements. / '<s>Valkala</s>' — tree bark, and also a garment made from it. / '<s>Kapilāḥ</s>' — tawny, and also particular sages. / Because of the multiplicity of objects of superimposition (<s>āropa</s>), the things superimposed are also multiple.

children.text: kesariṇaṃ bakulapuṣpavantaṃ siṃhaṃ ca / vasantaṃ mādhavaṃ nivasantaṃ ca / abhimāno dhārādhirūḍho māno mahāpramāṇaś ca / durvāraṇo 'śakyavāraṇo duṣṭaś ca karī / matto matsakāśāt samadaś ca / abhimāna iti na tathā hṛdayaṅgamaḥ pāṭhaḥ / anyonyam iti vasantam ity asya kesariṇam iti viśeṣaṇaṃ, siṃhapakṣe ca kesariṇam ity asya vasantam iti / rūpyeti yaḥ kesarī pratītaḥ sa vasantasya rūpakatvena na tāṭasthyena / evaṃ vasantam ity asya nivasanārthayoge 'pi vasantārthaḥ kesariṇo rūpakatvena yojanīyaḥ / ittham eva durvāraṇābhimānayor vācyam / viśeṣyatvena rūpyatvena ca svatantratvaṃ, tadviparyayeṇa paratantratvam / viśeṣyādyātmaketi / ādigrahaṇena rūpyarūpakabhāvo gṛhyate / tilakas taruviśeṣas tilakaś ca viśeṣakaḥ / tadabhivyaktir ubhayārthābhivyaktiḥ / tayor ubhayor arthayoḥ / guṇavanto rajjuyuktā api ghaṭakāḥ saṅghaṭayitāro hrasvāś ca ghaṭāḥ / pārthivā rājānaḥ, na tu vakṣyamāṇayuktyā pṛthivīvikārā vyākhyeyāḥ guṇavattvaghaṭakatvayor iti / yady apy atra samīhitasiddhau hetutvena vyavasthitasya ghaṭa(kā) ity asya pārthivā iti prati viśeṣaṇatvaṃ, tathāpi kūpa ivety upamāsāmarthyād viśeṣyatvam api ghaṭate //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kesariṇam</s>' — one possessing the <s>bakula</s> flower [= having a mane], and also a lion. / '<s>Vasantam</s>' — the Spring (<s>Mādhava</s>), and also 'dwelling' (<s>nivasantam</s>). / '<s>Abhimāna</s>' — pride established in a stream (<s>dhārā</s>), great in measure, and also self-regard. / '<s>Durvāraṇa</s>' — impossible to ward off, wicked, and also [having] a bad elephant. / '<s>Matta</s>' — from me (<s>matsakāśāt</s>), and also intoxicated. / The reading '<s>abhimāna</s>' is not as convincing [as alternatives]. / 'Mutually' — '<s>vasantam</s>' has '<s>kesariṇam</s>' as its qualifier; and in the lion-interpretation, '<s>kesariṇam</s>' has '<s>vasantam</s>' [as qualifier]. / 'Is represented' (<s>rūpyate</s>) — The <s>kesarī</s> (lion) that is cognized is [taken] as a metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) of the Spring (<s>vasanta</s>), not merely as an onlooker. / Similarly, even when '<s>vasantam</s>' is construed with the meaning of 'dwelling,' the Spring-meaning should be construed as a metaphor of the lion. / In the same way, [this] should be stated for '<s>durvāraṇa</s>' and '<s>abhimāna</s>.' / Independence [arises] from being the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>) and the thing represented (<s>rūpya</s>); dependence from the opposite of that. / 'Consisting of the qualified etc.' — By the word 'etc.,' the relationship of the thing-represented and the metaphor is included. / '<s>Tilaka</s>' — a particular tree, and also an ornamental mark. / The manifestation of that is the manifestation of both meanings. / Of those two meanings: / '<s>Guṇavantaḥ</s>' — [men] endowed with merits, and also those having ropes; '<s>ghaṭakāḥ</s>' — [those who] join together, short, and also pots. / '<s>Pārthivāḥ</s>' — kings; but they should not be explained, by the reasoning to be stated, as 'products of earth' — [the relevant point is] the qualities of being endowed with merits and being joiners. / Although here '<s>ghaṭakāḥ</s>' has the status of a qualifier with respect to '<s>pārthivāḥ</s>,' being established as the cause for accomplishing the desired end, nevertheless, by the force of the simile '<s>kūpa iva</s>' (like a well), the status of being the qualified also applies.
